modules.name: std/aead
modules.surface:
module std/aead

# The AES block cipher, FIPS 197: a 16, 24 or 32-byte key (10, 12 or 14
# rounds), one 16-byte block at a time, either way. On its own it is a
# building block; a message wants a mode, `AesGcm`.
pub class AES
  # FIPS 197's InvCipher: the block `encrypt_block` answered, back.
  def decrypt_block(block : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  # FIPS 197's Cipher: 16 bytes in, 16 out.
  def encrypt_block(block : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  def initialize(key : String | Array(UInt8))
end

# What `open` answers for sealed bytes it will not open: shorter than a
# tag, or whose tag does not match.
pub struct AeadError
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

# AES in Galois/Counter Mode, NIST SP 800-38D: CTR encryption from the
# counter after the nonce's own, and a 128-bit tag that is GHASH over the
# additional data and the ciphertext, each padded to a block, and their
# lengths in bits, XORed with the key stream of the nonce's counter
# block. The nonce is 12 bytes, and the counter block is it and a 32-bit
# counter that starts at 1 (§7.1).
pub class AesGcm
  def initialize(key : String | Array(UInt8))
  # The plaintext *sealed* came from, when its tag is the one this key,
  # *nonce* and *aad* give; else an `AeadError`, and nothing decrypted.
  def open(nonce : String | Array(UInt8), sealed : String | Array(UInt8), aad : String | Array(UInt8) = "") : String | AeadError
  # The ciphertext of *plaintext*, as long as it, and the 16-byte tag.
  def seal(nonce : String | Array(UInt8), plaintext : String | Array(UInt8), aad : String | Array(UInt8) = "") : String
end

# The ChaCha20 stream cipher, RFC 8439 §2.4: a 32-byte key, a 12-byte
# nonce and a 32-bit block counter, which starts at *counter*. `xor`
# answers its data XORed with the key stream and carries on from where
# it stopped, so a message XORed in pieces is the message XORed whole;
# the same call decrypts. The counter is the RFC's 32 bits, 256 GiB of
# key stream; a stream run past block 2^32 - 1 is refused rather than
# wrapped onto key stream already used.
pub class ChaCha20
  def initialize(key : String | Array(UInt8), nonce : String | Array(UInt8), counter : UInt32 = 0_u32)
  # *count* bytes from *src* to *dst*, which may be the same bytes.
  def xor(src : Pointer(UInt8), dst : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Nil
  def xor(data : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
end

# ChaCha20 and Poly1305 as an AEAD, RFC 8439 §2.8: the Poly1305 key is
# the first 32 bytes of block 0's key stream, the plaintext is encrypted
# from block 1, and the tag covers the additional data and the
# ciphertext, each padded with zeros to 16 bytes, then their lengths as
# 64-bit little-endian numbers.
pub class ChaCha20Poly1305
  def initialize(key : String | Array(UInt8))
  # The plaintext *sealed* came from, when its tag is the one this key,
  # *nonce* and *aad* give; else an `AeadError`, and nothing decrypted.
  def open(nonce : String | Array(UInt8), sealed : String | Array(UInt8), aad : String | Array(UInt8) = "") : String | AeadError
  # The ciphertext of *plaintext*, as long as it, and the 16-byte tag.
  def seal(nonce : String | Array(UInt8), plaintext : String | Array(UInt8), aad : String | Array(UInt8) = "") : String
end

# Poly1305, RFC 8439 §2.5: a 16-byte MAC under a 32-byte one-time key, r
# (clamped) and s. One key authenticates one message: a second message
# under it lets whoever sees both tags forge a third, which is why the
# AEAD derives a fresh key from each nonce, and why there is no `reset`.
# `Poly1305.mac(key, data)` is one piece; `new`, `update` as the message
# arrives, `final` once is the same in pieces. A tag someone sent is
# compared with std/crypto's `Subtle.constant_time_compare`, not `==`.
pub class Poly1305
  # The 16-byte tag. A last block shorter than 16 bytes carries its own
  # 1 bit after its bytes (§2.5.1), rather than the 2^128 of a whole one.
  def final : String
  def initialize(key : String | Array(UInt8))
  def self.mac(key : String | Array(UInt8), data : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  def update(data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : self
  def update(data : String | Array(UInt8)) : self
end

impl Error for AeadError
  def message : String
end

modules.name: std/asn1
modules.surface:
module std/asn1

# What `Der.parse`, `children` and the typed readers answer for bytes that
# are not the DER they were asked for: a sentence, and the offset in the
# bytes `Der.parse` was given where the trouble is.
pub struct Asn1Error
  def initialize(message : String, offset : Int32)
  def offset : Int32
  def to_s : String
end

pub struct Der
  def initialize
  # The one value *bytes* hold, and nothing after it.
  def self.parse(bytes : Array(UInt8)) : DerValue | Asn1Error
  # Every value under *value*, *value* first, in the order they are
  # written, each with its depth below it: the whole tree read and every
  # length and tag checked. Primitive contents are not decoded; that is
  # the typed readers' job, asked of the values a schema names.
  def self.walk(value : DerValue, & : (DerValue, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil | Asn1Error
end

# The two bits at the top of an identifier byte.
pub enum DerClass : Int32
  Universal = 0
  Application = 1
  ContextSpecific = 2
  Private = 3
end

# The universal tag numbers this module reads (X.680 section 8.6).
pub struct DerTag
  def initialize
end

# One value: its identifier, and where its header and content are in the
# bytes it was read from.
pub struct DerValue
  # A BIT STRING whose bits fill whole bytes: a key, a signature.
  def bit_string : Array(UInt8) | Asn1Error
  # A BIT STRING's bytes and how many bits at the end of the last are not
  # part of it, which DER sets to zero: a flags field such as keyUsage.
  def bit_string_bits : ::Tuple(Array(UInt8), Int32) | Asn1Error
  def boolean : Bool | Asn1Error
  # The values a constructed value holds, read one level down.
  def children : Array(DerValue) | Asn1Error
  def constructed? : Bool
  # The content bytes, copied.
  def content : Array(UInt8)
  # The offset of the first content byte, and of the byte after the value.
  def content_offset : Int32
  def content_size : Int32
  def context?(tag : Int32) : Bool
  # The identifier, said the way an error names it: `INTEGER`,
  # `[0] constructed`, `APPLICATION 3`.
  def describe : String
  def end_offset : Int32
  # An ENUMERATED that fits an Int64: a CRL entry's reason code, an
  # OCSP response's status.
  def enumerated : Int64 | Asn1Error
  # An ENUMERATED's two's-complement bytes, held to INTEGER's rules.
  def enumerated_bytes : Array(UInt8) | Asn1Error
  # The one value inside an explicit context tag `[n]`, as X.509 writes a
  # certificate's version and extensions.
  def explicit(tag : Int32) : DerValue | Asn1Error
  def header_size : Int32
  def initialize(data : Array(UInt8), tag_class : DerClass, constructed : Bool, tag : Int32, offset : Int32, header_size : Int32, content_size : Int32)
  # An INTEGER that fits an Int64.
  def integer : Int64 | Asn1Error
  # An INTEGER's two's-complement bytes, as written: checked to be the
  # fewest that hold it. Only an INTEGER: an ENUMERATED is written the same
  # way under another tag, and reading one here took an Ecdsa-Sig-Value
  # whose r or s was tagged ENUMERATED - a signature no DER reader accepts.
  def integer_bytes : Array(UInt8) | Asn1Error
  def null : Nil | Asn1Error
  def octet_string : Array(UInt8) | Asn1Error
  def offset : Int32
  # An OBJECT IDENTIFIER in dotted form, `"2.5.4.3"`. A subidentifier past
  # an Int64 is refused: no algorithm or attribute is one.
  def oid : String | Asn1Error
  # The whole value as it was written, header included: what a signature
  # over a certificate's `tbsCertificate` is computed on.
  def raw : Array(UInt8)
  # One value's header at *at*, its content within *stop*.
  def self.read(data : Array(UInt8), at : Int32, stop : Int32) : DerValue | Asn1Error
  # A SEQUENCE's elements: `children`, after checking it is one.
  def sequence : Array(DerValue) | Asn1Error
  # A SET's elements.
  def set : Array(DerValue) | Asn1Error
  # Any of the string types X.509 names are written in, as UTF-8.
  def string : String | Asn1Error
  def tag : Int32
  def tag_class : DerClass
  # A UTCTime or a GeneralizedTime, in the one form DER writes each.
  def time : Time | Asn1Error
  def universal?(tag : Int32) : Bool
  def self.universal_name(tag : Int32) : String
  # A non-negative INTEGER's magnitude, big-endian, without the 0x00 a
  # high bit makes DER write: an RSA modulus, a serial number. A negative
  # one is refused.
  def unsigned_integer : Array(UInt8) | Asn1Error
end

impl Error for Asn1Error
  def message : String
end

module std/atomic

struct ::Atomic(T)
  def add_acq_rel(value : T) : T
  def add_acquire(value : T) : T
  def add_relaxed(value : T) : T
  def add_release(value : T) : T
  # `word &= value`; answers what the word held before.
  def and(value : T) : T
  # `word |= value`; answers what the word held before.
  def bitwise_or(value : T) : T
  def compare_and_set_acq_rel(expected : T, desired : T) : Tuple(T, Bool)
  def compare_and_set_acquire(expected : T, desired : T) : Tuple(T, Bool)
  # `compare_and_set` at each weaker ordering: if the word holds
  # `expected` it now holds `desired`; answers what the word held and
  # whether the exchange happened.
  def compare_and_set_relaxed(expected : T, desired : T) : Tuple(T, Bool)
  def compare_and_set_release(expected : T, desired : T) : Tuple(T, Bool)
  # A full fence: nothing crosses it in either direction.
  def self.fence : Nil
  # Both halves, without the total order of `fence`.
  def self.fence_acq_rel : Nil
  # Nothing after this fence moves before it.
  def self.fence_acquire : Nil
  # Nothing before this fence moves after it.
  def self.fence_release : Nil
  # The word, read once; nothing after the read moves before it.
  def get_acquire : T
  # The word, read once, atomic and nothing more.
  def get_relaxed : T
  # `word = max(word, value)`, signed or unsigned as `T` is; answers what
  # the word held before.
  def max(value : T) : T
  # `word = min(word, value)`, signed or unsigned as `T` is; answers what
  # the word held before.
  def min(value : T) : T
  # `word = ~(word & value)`; answers what the word held before.
  def nand(value : T) : T
  # The word, written once, atomic and nothing more.
  def set_relaxed(value : T) : Nil
  # The word, written once; nothing before the write moves after it.
  def set_release(value : T) : Nil
  def sub_acq_rel(value : T) : T
  def sub_acquire(value : T) : T
  def sub_relaxed(value : T) : T
  def sub_release(value : T) : T
  def swap_acq_rel(value : T) : T
  def swap_acquire(value : T) : T
  def swap_relaxed(value : T) : T
  def swap_release(value : T) : T
  # `word ^= value`; answers what the word held before.
  def xor(value : T) : T
end

struct ::IyiAtomic
  def self.fence(ordering : Symbol, singlethread : Bool) : Nil
end

module std/benchmark

pub class Benchmark
  module BM
    class Job
      def execute : Nil
      def initialize
      def report(label : String = " ", &block : (->)) : Nil
    end
    class Tms
      def initialize(real : Float64, label : String = "")
      def label : String
      def real : Float64
      def to_s(io) : Nil
      def to_s : String
    end
  end
  module IPS
    class Entry
      def action : (->)
      def action=(value : (->)) : (->)
      def calculate_stats(samples : Array(Float64)) : Nil
      def call : Nil
      def call_for_100ms : Nil
      def cycles : Int32
      def cycles=(value : Int32) : Int32
      def human_compare : String
      def human_iteration_time : String
      def human_mean : String
      def initialize(label : String, action : (->))
      def label : String
      def label=(value : String) : String
      def mean : Float64
      def mean=(value : Float64) : Float64
      def ran? : Bool
      def relative_stddev : Float64
      def relative_stddev=(value : Float64) : Float64
      def set_cycles(duration : Std::Time::Span, iterations : UInt64) : Nil
      def size : Int32
      def size=(value : Int32) : Int32
      def slower : Float64
      def slower=(value : Float64) : Float64
      def stddev : Float64
      def stddev=(value : Float64) : Float64
      def variance : Float64
      def variance=(value : Float64) : Float64
    end
    class Job
      def execute : Nil
      def initialize(calculation : Std::Time::Span = Std::Time::Span.seconds(5), warmup : Std::Time::Span = Std::Time::Span.seconds(2), interactive : Bool = false)
      def items : Array(Entry)
      # Seconds as numbers, as the other library takes them. It asked
      # `Time.seconds`, which `Time` (an instant) does not have, so
      # `Job.new(1, 1)` did not compile; a length of time is a `Span`. The
      # answer is named: a program built from this module's artifact read
      # a method with none as one that answers nil.
      def self.new(calculation = 5, warmup = 2, interactive = false) : Job
      def report(label : String = "", &action : (->)) : Entry
      def report : Nil
    end
  end
  def self.bm(& : (BM::Job -> Nil)) : BM::Job
  def self.ips(calculation : Std::Time::Span = Std::Time::Span.seconds(5), warmup : Std::Time::Span = Std::Time::Span.seconds(2), interactive : Bool = false, & : (IPS::Job -> Nil)) : IPS::Job
  def self.ips(calculation : Int32 = 5, warmup : Int32 = 2, interactive : Bool = false, & : (IPS::Job -> Nil)) : IPS::Job
  def self.measure(label : String = "", & : (-> Nil)) : BM::Tms
  def self.realtime(& : (-> Nil)) : Std::Time::Span
end

pub alias Span = Std::Time::Span

pub alias Time = Std::Time::Time

modules.name: std/big
modules.surface:
module std/big

pub struct BigDecimal
  def !=(other : BigDecimal) : Bool
  def %(other : BigDecimal) : BigDecimal
  def *(other : BigDecimal) : BigDecimal
  def *(other : Int32 | Int64) : BigDecimal
  def +(other : BigDecimal) : BigDecimal
  def +(other : Int32 | Int64) : BigDecimal
  def + : BigDecimal
  def -(other : BigDecimal) : BigDecimal
  def -(other : Int32 | Int64) : BigDecimal
  def - : BigDecimal
  def /(other : BigDecimal) : BigDecimal
  def /(other : Int32 | Int64) : BigDecimal
  def //(other : BigDecimal) : BigDecimal
  def abs : BigDecimal
  protected def self.align(a : BigDecimal, b : BigDecimal) : Tuple(BigInt, BigInt, Int32)
  # `self / other` rounded to `precision` fractional digits, half away from
  # zero. A quotient that is exact within `precision` digits is answered with
  # the fewest digits that write it: `1/4` is `0.25`, `6/3` is `2`. One that
  # is not keeps all `precision` digits, so the reader sees where it was cut.
  def div(other : BigDecimal, precision : Int32) : BigDecimal
  # The same value at another scale is the same key: `1.10`, `1.1` and
  # `11e-1` hash alike because `==` says they are equal. The digits without
  # their trailing zeros and the exponent that goes with them name the value;
  # multiplying a negative scale out made `1e1000000.hash` take 2.6 s.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(value : BigInt, scale : Int32 = 0)
  def initialize(num : Int32 = 0, scale : Int32 = 0)
  def initialize(num : Int64, scale : Int32 = 0)
  # Parses `[+-]digits[.digits][e[+-]digits]`; anything else is refused.
  def initialize(str : String)
  def inspect : String
  # Bounds on the place of the leading digit, from the limb count alone:
  # 10^(lo - 1) <= |self| < 10^hi. 30102 and 30103 in 100,000 bracket
  # log10(2) for each 32-bit limb.
  protected def magnitude_bounds : Tuple(Int64, Int64)
  def negate : BigDecimal
  def negative? : Bool
  # The same value with the smallest non-negative scale: trailing zeros of
  # the fraction are dropped and a negative scale is multiplied out.
  def normalized : BigDecimal
  def positive? : Bool
  def scale : Int32
  # The value without its trailing zeros, at most `limit` of them, and how
  # many went. Counted once in the digits and divided out once: one divmod
  # by ten per zero was quadratic, and the hash of `1.` and 40,000 zeros, or
  # `3.div(3, 40000)`, took 725 ms. A value that does not end in zero is
  # answered by one division by ten, without printing it.
  protected def strip_zeros(limit : Int32) : Tuple(BigInt, Int32)
  def to_big_d : BigDecimal
  def to_big_i : BigInt
  def to_f : Float64
  def to_f64 : Float64
  def to_i32 : Int32
  def to_i64 : Int64
  # Zero is `0` whatever its scale; every other value prints every digit of
  # its scale, so `1.10` stays `1.10`.
  def to_s : String
  def value : BigInt
  def zero? : Bool
end

# A binary floating-point number of any precision: `±mantissa · 2^exponent`,
# the mantissa exactly *precision* bits long (128 unless asked), every
# result rounded once, to the nearest value of that many bits, ties to even
# - the rounding IEEE 754 gives a double, at any width. The other library's
# BigFloat is GMP's `mpf`, which truncates and keeps more bits than it was
# asked for; this one answers what MPFR does.
#
#     a = BigFloat.new(2, 256)
#     a.sqrt.to_s
#     # => "1.4142135623730950488016887242096980785696718753769480731766797379907324784621"
#     BigFloat.new("0.1", 24).to_f64   # => 0.10000000149011612
#
# An operation between two answers at the larger precision; with an
# integer, at the BigFloat's. `to_s` writes the fewest decimal digits that
# read back to the same value at its precision, positional from 1e-4 to
# below 1e15 and with an exponent outside, as `Float64#to_s` writes. There
# is no NaN or infinity: dividing by zero, the square root of a negative
# number, a NaN or an infinite double, a precision under 1 and a string
# that is no number are refused.
pub struct BigFloat
  def *(other : BigFloat) : BigFloat
  def *(other : Int32 | Int64 | BigInt) : BigFloat
  # The power, its exact value rounded once; a negative exponent is the
  # reciprocal of the power, rounded once.
  def **(exponent : Int32) : BigFloat
  def +(other : BigFloat) : BigFloat
  def +(other : Int32 | Int64 | BigInt) : BigFloat
  def + : BigFloat
  def -(other : BigFloat) : BigFloat
  def -(other : Int32 | Int64 | BigInt) : BigFloat
  def - : BigFloat
  def /(other : BigFloat) : BigFloat
  def /(other : Int32 | Int64 | BigInt) : BigFloat
  def ==(other : BigFloat) : Bool
  def abs : BigFloat
  def ceil : BigFloat
  protected def self.check(precision : Int32) : Nil
  # An integer at exactly the bits it has.
  protected def self.exactly(value : Int32 | Int64 | BigInt) : BigFloat
  protected def exponent : Int64
  def floor : BigFloat
  # Equal values hash alike whatever their precision: the mantissa without
  # its trailing zero bits.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(negative : Bool, mantissa : BigInt, exponent : Int64, precision : Int32)
  def inspect : String
  # The largest integer whose square is at most *value*, by Newton's
  # method from above.
  protected def self.isqrt(value : BigInt) : BigInt
  protected def mantissa : BigInt
  def negative? : Bool
  def self.new(value : Int32, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  def self.new(value : Int64, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  def self.new(value : BigInt, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  # The double's exact value, rounded to *precision* bits.
  def self.new(value : Float64, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  def self.new(value : BigRational, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  def self.new(value : BigDecimal, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  # A decimal - `-12.5`, `1e-30`, `6.02214076E23` - rounded to *precision*
  # bits; anything else is refused.
  def self.new(text : String, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat
  # As `new`, nil for a string that is no number.
  def self.parse?(text : String, precision : Int32 = DEFAULT_PRECISION) : BigFloat | ::Nil
  # *digits* with its first digit at 10^*point*, as `Float64#to_s` puts
  # a point: positional from 10^-4 to 10^14, an exponent outside.
  protected def self.place(digits : String, point : Int64) : String
  def positive? : Bool
  def precision : Int32
  # Under one half is zero; from there the fraction is at most
  # *precision* bits, compared with one half exactly.
  def round : BigFloat
  # *num*/*den* · 2^*shift* (both non-negative, *den* not zero), rounded to
  # *precision* bits, ties to even: every value here is made by this, from
  # an exact one.
  protected def self.rounded(negative : Bool, num : BigInt, den : BigInt, shift : Int64, precision : Int32) : BigFloat
  # The square root, rounded once. The mantissa is widened to at least
  # 2·precision + 4 bits over an even power of two, so the integer root
  # has two bits past the ones kept, and a root that is not exact carries a
  # half below its last bit into the rounding, which no tie can be.
  def sqrt : BigFloat
  # The exact sum, rounded once. An addend more than *precision* + 2 bits
  # below the other cannot move it - it is under a quarter of the larger's
  # last place, even where that place halves below a power of two - and
  # is not shifted out to a size it would only be rounded away from.
  protected def sum(other : BigFloat, precision : Int32) : BigFloat
  # Toward zero, floor, ceiling, and to the nearest integer, ties to even.
  def to_big_i : BigInt
  # The exact value as a fraction.
  def to_big_r : BigRational
  # The double nearest, ties to even; past the largest double, infinite,
  # and below the smallest, zero.
  def to_f64 : Float64
  # The fewest decimal digits that read back as this value at its
  # precision, the nearest such when there are two; written as
  # `Float64#to_s` writes a double.
  def to_s : String
  # The place above the leading bit: 2^(top - 1) <= |self| < 2^top.
  protected def top : Int64
  def trunc : BigFloat
  protected def trunc_whole : BigInt
  # This value at another precision, rounded if it is fewer bits.
  def with_precision(bits : Int32) : BigFloat
  def zero? : Bool
end

pub struct BigInt
  # Three-way comparison is `<=>`, from `impl Comparable` below.
  def !=(other : BigInt) : Bool
  def !=(other : Int64) : Bool
  def !=(other : Int32) : Bool
  def %(other : BigInt) : BigInt
  def %(other : Int64) : BigInt
  def %(other : Int32) : BigInt
  # Bitwise AND (&) with two's complement semantics
  def &(other : BigInt) : BigInt
  # Multiplication
  def *(other : BigInt) : BigInt
  def *(other : Int64) : BigInt
  def *(other : Int32) : BigInt
  # Exponentiation by squaring: a ** exp
  def **(exp : Int32) : BigInt
  def **(exp : Int64) : BigInt
  def **(exp : BigInt) : BigInt
  # Addition
  def +(other : BigInt) : BigInt
  def +(other : Int64) : BigInt

pub struct Bzip2
  # *data* as one bzip2 stream with blocks of *level* * 100,000 bytes,
  # 1 to 9 (bzip2's -1 to -9); any other level is a panic.
  def self.compress(data : String, level : Int32 = 9) : String
  # Every byte *data*'s streams hold, or the error the first wrong thing in
  # them is. Bytes after the last stream that do not start another are
  # ignored, as bzip2(1) ignores them.
  def self.decompress(data : String) : String | Bzip2Error
  def initialize
end

# What `Bzip2Reader#read` and `Bzip2.decompress` answer for a stream they
# cannot read: one that is corrupt, whose CRC does not match, or that ends
# early.
pub struct Bzip2Error
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

# A bzip2 stream read a piece at a time: the compressed bytes come from
# the block, the decompressed ones go out through `read`, and memory
# stays at one block's links and a 64 KiB buffer.
#
# ```
# body = Bzip2Reader.new { file.read_bytes(65536) }
# while (piece = body.read(65536)!) != ""
#   ...
# end
# ```
pub class Bzip2Reader
  # Whether every stream has ended, its CRCs checked, and every byte been
  # read: the next `read` answers "".
  def finished? : Bool
  # *source* answers the next bytes of the compressed stream, nil (or "")
  # when there are no more. It is called only when the decoder has no
  # bytes in hand for what it must read next, so it is never asked for
  # anything past a stream's end - except that the input ends only where
  # no stream follows, which takes a look at the next four bytes.
  def initialize(&source : (-> String | ::Nil))
  # Bytes the source gave beyond the last stream, for a caller that frames
  # other data after it; "" before the input has ended.
  def leftover : String
  # Up to *max* decompressed bytes, 64 KiB at most; "" once every stream
  # has ended and its CRCs been checked. A read that has bytes when a
  # block ends answers them rather than reading the next block, so it can
  # answer fewer than *max* before the end.
  #
  # A corrupt stream, a CRC that does not match, or input that ends early
  # is a `Bzip2Error`, after which every read answers the same error. A
  # block's bytes are given out before its CRC is known, as the CRC is
  # over them; the read that gives its last byte checks it, and answers
  # the error instead of those bytes. A *max* below 1 is a panic.
  def read(max : Int32 = 65536) : String | Bzip2Error
end

impl Error for Bzip2Error
  def message : String
end

module std/compress

# What `Inflater#read` answers for a stream it cannot read: one that is
# corrupt, whose checksum or length does not match, or that ends early.
# `message` is the sentence the whole-string calls panic with.
pub struct CompressError
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

pub struct Deflate
  # *data* as a DEFLATE stream, at *level*: 1 is fastest, 9 smallest, 6
  # (the default) zlib's own balance, 0 stored blocks only; anything else
  # is a panic. The same level writes what zlib's would size for size,
  # within the margins the exercise records.
  def self.compress(data : String, level : Int32 = 6) : String
  def self.decompress(data : String) : String
  # The bytes, and how many of the stream's bytes they took: an envelope
  # reads its trailer from there.
  #
  # *expected* is how long the caller thinks the result is, so that the
  # result is one allocation rather than a guess grown by doubling; -1,
  # the default, is no idea, and the guess is three times the stream's
  # bytes. Held to what the stream could expand to, so a length that lies
  # is not an allocation it asked for.
  def self.inflate(data : String, start : Int32, expected : Int64 = -1_i64) : ::Tuple(String, Int32)
  def initialize
end

# A compressed stream written a piece at a time. Each `compress` codes its
# piece in blocks as `Deflate.compress` does and ends in zlib's sync
# flush: an empty stored block, so everything written so far ends on a
# byte boundary and decodes without waiting for more. The window is kept
# from piece to piece - the next piece's matches reach back into the last
# 32 KiB of the ones before it, as zlib's do across a sync flush - so a
# stream written in pieces costs little more than the same bytes written
# whole. `finish` writes the final block, empty, and the envelope's
# trailer.
pub class Deflater
  # The compressed bytes for *data*: the envelope's header on first use,
  # then *data* as complete non-final blocks and the sync flush. "" for
  # empty data after the first call. After `finish`, a panic.
  def compress(data : String) : String
  # The final block and the envelope's trailer. Once only: a second call
  # is a panic.
  def finish : String
  # *level* is `Deflate.compress`'s: 0 stores, 1 is fastest, 9 smallest,
  # 6 the default. *window_bits* is the base-2 logarithm of how far back a
  # match may reach, 8 to 15: 15 is DEFLATE's whole 32 KiB, and a smaller
  # one is what a decoder that keeps less can read - RFC 7692's
  # `max_window_bits`. Anything else for either is a panic.
  def initialize(envelope : Envelope, level : Int32 = 6, window_bits : Int32 = 15)
end

# What a DEFLATE stream travels in: nothing (RFC 1951), zlib's two-byte
# header and Adler-32 (RFC 1950), or gzip's header and CRC-32 and length
# (RFC 1952).
pub enum Envelope : Int32
  Raw = 0
  Zlib = 1
  Gzip = 2
end

pub struct Gzip
  # The ten-byte header with nothing optional set, an mtime of zero, the
  # level's XFL and an unknown OS; then the CRC-32 and the length modulo
  # 2^32, little-endian. *level* as `Deflate.compress`.
  def self.compress(data : String, level : Int32 = 6) : String
  # Every member of the file, one after another; bytes after the last
  # that do not start another are left as zlib leaves them.
  #
  # The last member's trailer names its length, which for a file of one
  # member is the length of the answer, so that is the size the output
  # starts at; a file of several grows past it by doubling. Every member
  # had been sized on its own, by the last trailer or by three times the
  # bytes after it, so each allocated what the rest of the file could
  # hold, and a hundred two-byte members ahead of one of 64 MB took 2.5 s
  # to read where Python's gzip took 0.15.
  def self.decompress(data : String) : String
  def initialize
end

# A compressed stream read a piece at a time: the compressed bytes come
# from the block, the decompressed ones go out through `read`, and memory
# stays at the 32 KiB window and what is waiting to be read.
#
# ```
# body = Inflater.new(Envelope::Gzip) { socket_read }
# while (piece = body.read(65536)!) != ""
#   ...
# end
# ```
#
# `Inflater.flushed` is the same decoder for a raw stream that comes as
# pieces each ending between blocks - zlib's sync flush, what each
# `Deflater#compress` ends with - and is decoded a piece at a time, the
# window kept from one to the next: RFC 7692's permessage-deflate, whose
# messages are such pieces with the flush's last four bytes left off.
pub class Inflater
  # Whether the stream has ended, its trailer checked, and every byte been
  # read: the next `read` answers "".
  def finished? : Bool
  # A raw stream decoded by `inflate`, a piece at a time.
  def self.flushed : Inflater
  # The next piece of a `flushed` stream, decoded whole: the blocks it
  # holds, which may refer back to the 32 KiB before it, and may be final
  # (RFC 7692 §7.2.1 lets a final block be followed by more). A piece
  # that does not end between blocks, or is not DEFLATE, is a
  # `CompressError`, and so is every piece after it. More than *limit*
  # bytes out is nil, found as they come - a piece that would decode to
  # gigabytes stops 64 KiB past *limit* - and fails the stream the same
  # way. On another `Inflater`, a panic.
  def inflate(piece : String, limit : Int32 = 2147483647) : String | CompressError | Nil
  # *source* answers the next bytes of the compressed stream, nil (or "")
  # when there are no more. It is called only when the decoder has no
  # bytes in hand for what it must read next, so it is never asked for
  # anything past the end of the stream - except that a gzip stream ends
  # only where no member follows, which takes a look at the next two
  # bytes.
  def initialize(envelope : Envelope, &source : (-> String | ::Nil))
  def initialize(core : Inflate)
  # Bytes the source gave beyond the end of the stream (gzip: after the
  # last member), for a caller that frames other data after it; "" before
  # the stream has ended.
  def leftover : String
  # Up to *max* decompressed bytes; "" once the stream and its trailer
  # (CRC-32 and length, or Adler-32) have ended and been checked. A read
  # answers as soon as it has bytes and going on would call the source,
  # so it can answer fewer than *max* before the end; and never more than
  # 64 KiB less a match at once, the room ahead of the window.
  #
  # A corrupt stream, a bad checksum, or input that ends early is a
  # `CompressError`, after which every read answers the same error. What
  # the same read decoded before the error is not handed out. A *max*
  # below 1 is a panic.
  def read(max : Int32 = 65536) : String | CompressError
end

pub struct Zlib
  # CMF 0x78 (deflate, a 32 KiB window), FLG with the level's band and the
  # check bits that make the pair a multiple of 31 (no dictionary), then
  # the Adler-32 of the bytes, big-endian. *level* as `Deflate.compress`.
  def self.compress(data : String, level : Int32 = 6) : String
  def self.decompress(data : String) : String
  def self.hex(w : UInt32) : String
  def initialize
end

impl Error for CompressError
  def message : String
end

# pseudorandom key, `expand` stretches that key into as many bytes as are
# asked for, bound to an `info` that names their use; `derive` is both.

  def self.derive(algorithm : H.class, ikm : String | Array(UInt8), salt : String | Array(UInt8), info : String | Array(UInt8), length : Int32) : Array(UInt8) forall H

module std/curve25519

# What is wrong with a peer's key: `message` is the sentence.
pub struct CurveError
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

# Ed25519, RFC 8032 §5.1: the seed is the 32-byte private key; SHA-512 of
# it gives the secret scalar (its first half, clamped) and the prefix the
# per-message nonce is hashed from (its second half). Signing is
# deterministic: one seed and one message give one signature.
pub struct Ed25519
  def initialize
  # The 32-byte public key of *seed*, RFC 8032 §5.1.5.
  def self.public_key(seed : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  # The 64-byte signature of *message* under *seed*, RFC 8032 §5.1.6:
  # R = [r]B for r = SHA-512(prefix || M) mod L, then
  # S = (r + SHA-512(R || A || M) * s) mod L. The public key A is worked
  # out again from the seed, which costs a second multiplication of the
  # base point; the two are each a fixed-window constant-time one.
  def self.sign(seed : String | Array(UInt8), message : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  # Whether *signature* is *public_key*'s signature of *message*, RFC 8032
  # §5.1.7 with the cofactorless equation (the header says why). False,
  # not a panic, for a key or signature of the wrong size, a key that is
  # not a canonical encoding of a point on the curve, and an S of L or
  # more.
  def self.verify(public_key : String | Array(UInt8), message : String | Array(UInt8), signature : String | Array(UInt8)) : Bool
end

# An Ed25519 public key held as a value, as a certificate carries one (RFC
# 8410): the 32 bytes, checked once to be the canonical encoding of a point
# on the curve, so a key read from outside that is not one is refused where
# it is read rather than failing every signature later.
pub struct Ed25519PublicKey
  def bytes : Array(UInt8)
  # The key *bytes* encode, or a `CurveError`: not 32 bytes, or not a
  # canonical encoding of a point on the curve (RFC 8032 §5.1.3).
  def self.from_bytes(bytes : String | Array(UInt8)) : Ed25519PublicKey | CurveError
  def initialize(bytes : Array(UInt8))
  # Whether *signature* is this key's signature of *message*, as
  # `Ed25519.verify` answers it.
  def verify(message : String | Array(UInt8), signature : String | Array(UInt8)) : Bool
end

# X25519, RFC 7748 §5: the u-coordinate of a clamped scalar times a point
# on Curve25519. The private key is any 32 bytes; it is clamped here
# (bits 0 to 2 and 255 cleared, bit 254 set), so the caller need not.
pub struct X25519
  def initialize
  # The public key of *private_key*: its multiple of the base point, u = 9.
  def self.public_key(private_key : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  # The secret *private_key* shares with the owner of *peer_public*. A
  # peer key that is not 32 bytes, and a secret of all zeros (a peer key of
  # small order, RFC 7748 §6.1), are a `CurveError`. Whether the secret was
  # zero is the one thing that leaves the ladder by a branch, and it says
  # nothing of the private key: which keys give zero depends on the peer's.
  def self.shared(private_key : String | Array(UInt8), peer_public : String | Array(UInt8)) : String | CurveError
end

impl Error for CurveError
  def message : String
end

pub class Deque(T)

  def +(other : Deque(T)) : Deque(T)

  # The same elements in the same order, where one element type holds the
  # other, as tuples compare (src/iyi/object.iyi). Restricted to
  # `Deque(T)`, a `Deque(Int32)` was taken for a `Deque(Int32?)` and not
  # back: the one equality answered true one way and false the other.
  def ==(other : Deque(U)) : Bool forall U
  def []=(index : Int32, value : T) : T
  # Slots allocated, live or not.
  def capacity : Int32
  # Forgets every element; the capacity stays.
  def clear : Deque(T)
  # Appends every element of other; answers the deque. The count is read
  # once: walking `other.size` while pushing grew it along with this deque
  # when the two were one, so `d.concat(d)` never ended.
  def concat(other : Deque(T)) : Deque(T)
  def concat(items : Array(T)) : Deque(T)
  # Removes and answers the element at index; the shorter side closes
  # the gap.
  def delete_at(index : Int32) : T
  # A copy with the same elements, contiguous from slot 0.
  def dup : Deque(T)
  # size copies of value.
  def initialize(size : Int32, value : T)
  # An empty deque with room for initial_capacity elements before it grows.
  def initialize(initial_capacity : Int32)
  # An empty deque; the first push allocates.
  def initialize
  # Inserts value before index; `size` appends, `-1` appends too (the
  # position after the last). The shorter side moves.
  def insert(index : Int32, value : T) : Deque(T)
  def inspect : String
  # The array's elements, in its order.
  def self.new(items : Array(T)) : Deque(T)
  # size elements, each what the block answers for its index.
  def self.new(size : Int32, & : (Int32 -> T)) : Deque(T)
  # Removes the last n elements, or all of them when there are fewer.
  def pop(n : Int32) : Nil
  # Removes and answers the last element.
  def pop : T
  def pop? : T | ::Nil
  # Appends value; answers the deque.
  def push(value : T) : Deque(T)
  # Rotates in place so that the element at position n comes first; a
  # negative n rotates the other way. A full buffer only moves `@start`;
  # otherwise the shorter end is walked around.
  def rotate_in_place(n : Int32 = 1) : Deque(T)
  # A copy rotated by n, this deque untouched.
  def rotated(n : Int32 = 1) : Deque(T)

  # `Deque{1, 2, 3}`, elements inspected.

  # the checking.
  def unsafe_fetch(index : Int32) : T
  # Prepends value; answers the deque.
  def unshift(value : T) : Deque(T)
end

# The same convention as `CRC32`: `update(sum, data, count)` goes on from a
# finished Adler-32, and 1 is the start (the Adler-32 of nothing), as in
# zlib's `adler32(adler, buf, len)`.
pub struct Adler32
  def self.checksum(data : String) : UInt32
  def self.hexdigest(data : String) : String
  def initialize
  def self.update(sum : UInt32, data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : UInt32
end

# `checksum(data)` is the CRC-32 of *data*. `update(crc, data, count)` goes
# on from a CRC-32 already taken, zlib's `crc32(crc, buf, len)` convention:
# what goes in and what comes out are finished checksums, the inversion
# before and after done inside, so 0 is the start (the CRC-32 of nothing)
# and `update(update(0, a), b)` is the CRC-32 of *a* then *b*, the same
# number `checksum` answers for the two joined.
pub struct CRC32
  def self.checksum(data : String) : UInt32
  def self.hexdigest(data : String) : String
  def initialize
  # Eight bytes a step through eight tables (slicing-by-8), where it had
  # been one bit a step: twenty megabytes took 105 ms, which was most of
  # what `Gzip.decompress` spent, the inflating itself taking 30.
  def self.update(crc : UInt32, data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : UInt32
end

# CRC-64 with ECMA-182's polynomial, reflected (0xc96c5795d7870f42), and
# inverted before and after: the CRC-64 the .xz format checks a block
# with (xz file format 1.0.4 §3.4, check ID 0x04), which reveng's
# catalogue names CRC-64/XZ. The same convention as `CRC32`: `update(crc,
# data, count)` goes on from a finished checksum, 0 is the start (the
# CRC-64 of nothing), and `hexdigest` writes the number most significant
# digit first, as `xz --robot --list` does; the stream stores it
# little-endian.
pub struct CRC64
  def self.checksum(data : String) : UInt64
  def self.hexdigest(data : String) : String
  def initialize
  # Eight bytes a step through eight tables, as `CRC32` goes: the bytes
  # loaded as one little-endian word, xored into the checksum, and each
  # of the eight looked up in the table for how many bytes of zeros
  # follow it in the step.
  def self.update(crc : UInt64, data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : UInt64
end

# What every block hash shares: the message is cut into blocks, the last
# one padded with a one bit, zeros and the message's length in bits, and
# each block is compressed into the state. A subclass is the state and
# its compression; this is the cutting and the padding.
pub abstract class Digest
  # Bytes compressed at a time: 64, or 128 for SHA-384 and SHA-512. HMAC
  # pads its key to this.
  def block_size : Int32
  # Becomes *other*: the same bytes taken, the same state, the same
  # `final` given or not. Nothing is allocated. *other* must be the same
  # algorithm, and a different one is refused by name.
  def copy_from(other : Digest) : Nil
  # Bytes in a digest: 16 for MD5, 20 for SHA-1, 28, 32, 48 and 64 for
  # the SHA-2s.
  abstract def digest_size : Int32
  def dup : self
  # The digest, into the first `digest_size` bytes of *dst*: no array is
  # made, which is what a loop that hashes a hash wants.
  def final(dst : Array(UInt8)) : Nil
  def final : Array(UInt8)
  def self.hash_bytes(data : String | Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  def self.hexdigest(data : String | Array(UInt8)) : String
  def hexfinal : String
  def initialize(block_size : Int32)
  # The digest of no bytes yet, ready again after a `final`.
  def reset : Nil
  def update(data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : self
  def update(data : String) : self
  def update(data : Array(UInt8)) : self
end

  def digest_size : Int32
  def initialize
  # The type's own name, which is what a value that has said nothing about
  # itself can honestly print. A type that wants better defines its own.
  def to_s : String
end

# starting state, its digest the first 28 bytes.

# digest, so a rate (the `block_size`) of 200 bytes less two digests.

# SHA-512, FIPS 180-4 §6.4: 64-bit words, 128-byte blocks, 80 rounds.
# SHA-384 is the same compression from another starting state, its digest
# the first 48 bytes.

  def digest_size : Int32
  def initialize
  # The type's own name, which is what a value that has said nothing about
  # itself can honestly print. A type that wants better defines its own.

  def initialize
  # The type's own name, which is what a value that has said nothing about
  # itself can honestly print. A type that wants better defines its own.

  def initialize
  # The type's own name, which is what a value that has said nothing about
  # itself can honestly print. A type that wants better defines its own.
  def to_s : String
end

# SHAKE128 and SHAKE256, FIPS 202 section 6.2: the sponge at a capacity of
# 256 and 512 bits, as much output as is asked for. `update` absorbs;
# the first `read` pads and every `read` squeezes on from where the last
# stopped, so reads of 3 and 5 bytes are the first 8 bytes of one read.
# Absorbing after squeezing would be a different function, not more
# input, and is refused until `reset`.
pub abstract class Shake
  # Bytes absorbed at a time: 168 for SHAKE128, 136 for SHAKE256.
  def block_size : Int32
  # *count* bytes of the output for *data*.
  def self.hash_bytes(data : String | Array(UInt8), count : Int32) : Array(UInt8)
  def self.hexdigest(data : String | Array(UInt8), count : Int32) : String
  def initialize(rate : Int32)
  # The next `dst.size` bytes of output into *dst*, with no array made.
  # While squeezing, `@fill` counts the bytes of the state given out.
  def read(dst : Array(UInt8)) : Nil
  def read(count : Int32) : Array(UInt8)
  def reset : Nil
  def update(data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : self
  def update(data : String) : self
  def update(data : Array(UInt8)) : self
end

# XXH64, the 64-bit xxHash (Yann Collet; the algorithm as xxhash's
# `doc/xxhash_spec.md` gives it): the hash whose low 32 bits are a
# Zstandard frame's content checksum (RFC 8878 §3.1.1), which is what
# std/zstd takes it for. Not a cryptographic hash - a fast check that
# bytes arrived as they left, with nothing to keep anyone from making two
# messages that collide.
#
# `checksum(data, seed)` hashes one piece. `new(seed)`, then `update` as
# the data arrives, then `digest`, hashes it in pieces; `digest` leaves
# the state as it was, as xxhash's `XXH64_digest` does, so it can be
# asked midway and the hash go on. `hexdigest` is xxhash's canonical form,
# most significant byte first. A word of the message is loaded as one
# little-endian load, which is what every target iyi builds for is.
pub class XXH64
  def self.checksum(data : String, seed : UInt64 = 0_u64) : UInt64
  # The hash of everything given since the start or `reset`; the state is
  # left as it was.
  def digest : UInt64
  def self.hexdigest(data : String, seed : UInt64 = 0_u64) : String
  def initialize(seed : UInt64 = 0_u64)
  def self.merge(acc : UInt64, v : UInt64) : UInt64
  # Back to the hash of nothing, under the same seed.
  def reset : Nil
  def self.rotl(x : UInt64, n : Int32) : UInt64
  def self.round(acc : UInt64, input : UInt64) : UInt64
  def update(data : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Nil
  def update(data : String) : Nil
end

modules.surface:
module std/dns

# Why a name was not resolved. One type with a question per answer, as
# `SocketError` has, so a caller tells a name that does not exist
# (`not_found?`, NXDOMAIN - authoritative, not worth asking again) from a
# server that failed (`server_failure?`, SERVFAIL - maybe worth asking
# again later) without reading a sentence.
pub struct DnsError
  # The same failure, said about *name*: a failure found while reading
  # bytes knows no name, and the resolver that asked does.
  def about(name : String, server : String) : DnsError
  def detail : String
  def initialize(kind : Int32, name : String, server : String = "", detail : String = "")
  # Not a host name at all, so nothing was asked.
  def invalid_name? : ::Bool
  def kind : Int32
  # An answer that carried the query's ID and question and could not be
  # read: a compression loop, a pointer past the end, a record running off
  # the message, an alias chain that does not end.
  def malformed? : ::Bool
  # The name as the caller wrote it.
  def name : String
  # The name exists and has no address of the kind asked for (NOERROR
  # with no records, "NODATA").
  def no_address? : ::Bool
  # NXDOMAIN: the name does not exist.
  def not_found? : ::Bool
  def reason : String
  # REFUSED, FORMERR or NOTIMP: the server would not answer this query.
  def refused? : ::Bool
  # The server whose answer this is, `address:port`; empty when no server
  # was asked.
  def server : String
  # SERVFAIL from every server asked.
  def server_failure? : ::Bool
  # No server answered within the timeout, on any attempt.
  def timed_out? : ::Bool
  # The server could not be reached: nothing listens on its port (an ICMP
  # refusal), no route to it, or the TCP connection the truncated answer
  # needed failed.
  def unreachable? : ::Bool
end

# A query, and the reading of an answer to one.
pub struct DnsMessage
  # The addresses of *type* this answer gives *name*, following CNAMEs:
  # the records for the end of the chain, the name the chain ended at, and
  # how many links it took. No addresses and a different name is a chain
  # that left this answer before it ended, which the resolver asks about
  # next. A chain of more than *budget* links is malformed.
  def addresses(name : String, type : Int32, budget : Int32 = MAX_CNAMES) : Tuple(Array(Bytes), String, Int32) | DnsError
  def answers : Array(DnsRecord)
  # Whether this is the answer to query *id* for *name* and *type*: a
  # response, a standard query's, with the ID, and repeating the question.
  # A refusal of the query (SERVFAIL, REFUSED, FORMERR, NOTIMP) may come
  # without the question, as some servers send it; an answer that says
  # anything about the name - NOERROR or NXDOMAIN - must carry it.
  def answers?(id : UInt16, name : String, type : Int32) : ::Bool
  def flags : Int32
  def id : UInt16
  # The ID in a datagram's first two bytes, or -1 when it is too short to
  # be a message: what the resolver reads before it reads anything else.
  def self.id_of(packet : Bytes) : Int32
  def initialize(id : UInt16, flags : Int32, question_name : String, question_type : Int32, question_class : Int32, answers : Array(DnsRecord))
  def self.malformed(why : String) : DnsError
  def opcode : Int32
  # The message in *packet*: its header, its one question, and - unless it
  # is truncated - its answer section. Anything that does not fit the
  # bytes is `DnsError` with `malformed?`, never a read past them.
  def self.parse(packet : Bytes) : DnsMessage | DnsError
  # The query for *name*'s records of *type*, class IN, with recursion
  # desired: a 12-byte header and one question. *name* is a host name
  # (`DnsName.valid?`); a trailing dot is dropped.
  def self.query(id : UInt16, name : String, type : Int32) : Bytes
  def question_class : Int32
  # The question the answer repeats; empty with `question_type` 0 when it
  # repeats none.
  def question_name : String
  def question_type : Int32
  def rcode : Int32
  # The name at *at* in *packet*, and the offset just past it where it
  # sits; nil when it cannot be read. Labels are 1 to 63 bytes, a label may
  # not hold a `.` (it would read as two), the name is at most 255 bytes on
  # the wire, and each compression pointer must point before the place the
  # name was last read from - RFC 1035 4.1.4's "prior occurrence" - so the
  # positions strictly fall and a loop cannot be written.
  def self.read_name(packet : Bytes, at : Int32) : Tuple(String, Int32) | ::Nil
  def response? : ::Bool
  # TC: the answer did not fit in the datagram and is to be asked again
  # over TCP. Its records are not read: what is there is a fragment.
  def truncated? : ::Bool
end

# What a host name may be, and the names a short one stands for.
pub struct DnsName
  # The fully qualified names a lookup of *name* asks for, in order, as
  # resolv.conf(5) says: a name ending in `.` is only itself; one with at
  # least *ndots* dots is tried as it is first and then under each search
  # domain; one with fewer is tried under each search domain first and as
  # it is last. A candidate longer than a name can be is left out.
  def self.candidates(name : String, search : Array(String), ndots : Int32) : Array(String)
  def initialize
  # *name* without the trailing dot that makes it absolute.
  def self.relative(name : String) : String
  # Two names are the same name in any case (RFC 4343), with or without
  # the trailing dot.
  def self.same?(a : String, b : String) : ::Bool
  # A host name as RFC 1123 and glibc's `res_hnok` read one: labels of 1 to
  # 63 letters, digits, `-` and `_`, no label starting with `-`, at most
  # 253 characters, one trailing dot allowed. The last label must not be
  # all digits (RFC 3696 2: no top-level domain is), so `999.1.1.1` and
  # `1.2.3` stay what the numeric parser refuses rather than becoming
  # questions to a name server.
  def self.valid?(name : String) : ::Bool
  # Why *name* is not a host name, or nil when it is.
  def self.why(name : String) : String | ::Nil
end

# One resource record from an answer section.
pub struct DnsRecord
  # The record's data as it came: four bytes for an A record, sixteen for
  # an AAAA, the encoded name for a CNAME.
  def data : Bytes
  def initialize(name : String, type : Int32, record_class : Int32, ttl : UInt32, data : Bytes, target : String)
  def name : String
  def record_class : Int32
  # A CNAME's target, read with compression; empty for any other type.
  def target : String
  def ttl : UInt32
  def type : Int32
end

# The hosts file: an address, then the names it answers for.
pub struct HostsFile
  def initialize
  # The addresses *text* gives *name*, as written and in the file's order:
  # every line whose names include it, in any case and with or without a
  # trailing dot. A line with an address and no name says nothing.
  def self.lookup(text : String, name : String) : Array(String)
end

# `/etc/resolv.conf`, as resolv.conf(5) describes it and glibc reads it.
pub struct ResolvConf
  def attempts : Int32
  def initialize(nameservers : Array(String) = [] of String, search : Array(String) = [] of String, ndots : Int32 = 1, timeout_ms : Int32 = 5000, attempts : Int32 = 2)
  # Each an address as written - IPv4, or IPv6 without a zone - optionally
  # with a port (`192.0.2.1:5353`, `[2001:db8::1]:5353`), which
  # resolv.conf itself never has and a resolver built in a program may.
  def nameservers : Array(String)
  def ndots : Int32
  # The keywords glibc reads: `nameserver`, `domain`, `search` (the later
  # of `domain` and `search` wins, as there) and `options` with `ndots:`,
  # `timeout:` (seconds) and `attempts:`, each held to glibc's bounds - 15,
  # 30 and 5. A `#` or `;` starts a comment. Anything else is ignored, as
  # glibc ignores it: a file other programs read too is not this module's
  # to refuse.
  def self.parse(text : String) : ResolvConf
  def search : Array(String)
  def timeout_ms : Int32
end

impl Error for DnsError
  def message : String
end

module std/enumerable

pub trait Enumerable
  type Elem
  def accumulate(initial : U, & : (U, Elem -> U)) : Array(U) forall U
  def all?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  def any?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  # The same flag as `each_cons_pair`: with the nil test, a nil element
  # read as "no previous element", so the block was never asked about the
  # element after it and `[nil, nil, 1]` came back as one chunk.
  def chunk_while(& : (Elem, Elem -> Bool)) : Array(Array(Elem))
  def compact_map(& : (Elem -> U | ::Nil)) : Array(U) forall U
  def count(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Int32
  def cycle(n : Int32, & : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  abstract def each(& : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Yields each overlapping window of *n* elements; nothing when the source
  # is shorter than one window.
  def each_cons(n : Int32, & : (Array(Elem) -> Nil)) : Nil
  def each_cons(n : Int32) : Array(Array(Elem))
  # Whether there is a previous element is a flag, not a nil: an element
  # that is itself nil is still an element, and `[nil, 2]` has the pair
  # `{nil, 2}`. The nil test skipped every pair whose first half was nil.
  def each_cons_pair(& : (Elem, Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Yields each window of *n* elements, the last one short if the source
  # does not divide. The block form is the one `each_` promises everywhere
  # else in this trait — `each`, `each_with_index`, `each_with_object`,
  # `each_cons_pair`, `each_step` all take one — and these two were the
  # exception: they materialised `Array(Array(Elem))` and refused a block,
  # which allocates every window up front, the cost a block exists to
  # avoid. `Indexable` has had both shapes all along.
  def each_slice(n : Int32, & : (Array(Elem) -> Nil)) : Nil
  # And the same windows as an array, for a caller that wants them all.
  def each_slice(n : Int32) : Array(Array(Elem))
  def each_step(n : Int32, & : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  def each_with_index(& : (Elem, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The element first and the memo second, as the other library yields them.
  # It was the reverse, so `[[1], [2]].each_with_object([] of Int32) { |x,
  # acc| acc.concat(x) }` compiled under both and answered `[]` here: the
  # element was the one mutated (SPEC.md III.1.7a's worst shape).
  def each_with_object(obj : U, & : (Elem, U -> Nil)) : U forall U
  def empty? : Bool
  def find(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Elem | ::Nil
  # The first truthy answer, as the other library's: this took the first
  # non-nil one, `false` included, so `[1, 2, 3, 4].find_value { |i| i > 2 }`
  # answered false where the other library documents true for that very
  # call, and `{ |i| i > 8 }` answered false where it answers nil.
  def find_value(& : (Elem -> U | ::Nil)) : U | ::Nil forall U
  def first(n : Int32) : Array(Elem)
  def first : Elem
  def first? : Elem | ::Nil
  def flat_map(& : (Elem -> Array(U))) : Array(U) forall U
  def group_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : Hash(U, Array(Elem)) forall U : Hashable
  # Refused under its own name, as `minmax` below is: delegated, a size of
  # zero was refused with `each_slice`'s sentence, "slice size must be
  # positive", from a call the reader never wrote.
  def in_groups_of(n : Int32, filler : Elem) : Array(Array(Elem))
  def in_slices_of(n : Int32) : Array(Array(Elem))
  # Equality, as `Array#includes?` asks it: `<=>` answering 0 is ordering,
  # and for a float it said a NaN was present in a list of NaNs, which no
  # `==` says and `[nan].includes?(nan)` does not. And so no bound: every
  # type has `==`, and the `Comparable` one left from the `<=>` days
  # refused a list of arrays, of nilable numbers or of any class.
  def includes?(value : Elem) : Bool
  def index(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def index_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : Hash(U, Elem) forall U : Hashable
  # The separator defaults to nothing, the way `Array#join` (src/iyi/array.iyi)
  # and `Indexable#join` already default it: one name means one thing
  # (SPEC.md III.1.7a), and `slice.join` has to compile
  # where `array.join` does. A mandatory separator made the arity of one name
  # depend on which tower the receiver came from.
  #
  # Into one builder: adding each element to the text so far copied that
  # text once per element, and a `List` of 100,000 took nine seconds.
  def join(separator : String = "") : String
  def map(& : (Elem -> U)) : Array(U) forall U
  def map_with_index(& : (Elem, Int32 -> U)) : Array(U) forall U
  def max : Elem where Elem : Comparable
  def max? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable
  # Whether there was an element is the key's to say, not the element's: a
  # nil element can be the largest, and `found.nil?` refused
  # `List.new([nil, 1]).max_by { |x| x ? x : 5 }` as empty where
  # `Array#max_by` and the other library answer nil. `min_by` and
  # `minmax_by` read the key the same way.
  def max_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : Elem forall U : Comparable
  def max_by?(& : (Elem -> U)) : Elem | ::Nil forall U : Comparable
  def max_of(& : (Elem -> U)) : U forall U : Comparable
  def max_of?(& : (Elem -> U)) : U | ::Nil forall U : Comparable
  def min : Elem where Elem : Comparable
  def min? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable
  def min_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : Elem forall U : Comparable
  def min_by?(& : (Elem -> U)) : Elem | ::Nil forall U : Comparable
  def min_of(& : (Elem -> U)) : U forall U : Comparable
  def min_of?(& : (Elem -> U)) : U | ::Nil forall U : Comparable
  # Refuses under its own name rather than letting `min`'s refusal surface
  # from a call the reader never wrote: `minmax` of an empty collection is
  # `minmax`'s mistake, not `min`'s.
  def minmax : Tuple(Elem, Elem) where Elem : Comparable
  # One walk, as `minmax_of?` below takes: `min?` and then `max?` walked the
  # collection twice, so a source that can be read once (a pipe, a
  # generator) answered {1, nil} for [3, 1, 4, 1, 5] and `minmax` refused
  # it as empty.
  def minmax? : Tuple(Elem | ::Nil, Elem | ::Nil) where Elem : Comparable
  def minmax_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : Tuple(Elem, Elem) forall U : Comparable
  def minmax_by?(& : (Elem -> U)) : Tuple(Elem | ::Nil, Elem | ::Nil) forall U : Comparable
  def minmax_of(& : (Elem -> U)) : Tuple(U, U) forall U : Comparable
  def minmax_of?(& : (Elem -> U)) : Tuple(U | ::Nil, U | ::Nil) forall U : Comparable
  def none?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  def one?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  def partition(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Array(Array(Elem))
  def present? : Bool
  def product : Elem where Elem : Num
  def reduce(initial : U, & : (U, Elem -> U)) : U forall U
  # A flag for "an element was seen", not a nil accumulator: a nil element
  # reset the fold, so `[nil, 2]` answered 2 without calling the block.
  def reduce?(& : (Elem, Elem -> Elem)) : Elem | ::Nil
  def reject(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Array(Elem)
  def select(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Array(Elem)
  def size : Int32
  def skip(n : Int32) : Array(Elem)
  def skip_while(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Array(Elem)
  def sorted : Array(Elem) where Elem : Comparable
  def sum : Elem where Elem : Num
  def sum_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : U forall U : Num
  def take(n : Int32) : Array(Elem)
  def take_while(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Array(Elem)
  def tally : Hash(Elem, Int32) where Elem : Hashable
  def tally_by(& : (Elem -> U)) : Hash(U, Int32) forall U : Hashable
  def to_a : Array(Elem)
  def to_h(& : (Elem -> Tuple(K, V))) : Hash(K, V) forall K : Hashable, V
  def zip(other : O) : Array(Tuple(Elem, O::Elem)) forall O : Enumerable
end

end

class ::IyiIO
  # Advisory locks on the whole file, the other library's `flock_*`: a
  # shared one many holders may have at once, an exclusive one a single
  # holder. The holder is this open file - another `File.open` of the same
  # path, in this process or another, is another holder - until
  # `flock_unlock`, or until the file is closed.
  #
  #     File.open("app.lock", "w") do |f|
  #       f.flock_exclusive { run_alone }.or_panic
  #     end

  # A lock another holder has is waited for a task at a time: tried again
  # after 1, 2, 4 ... 64 ms, the thread's other tasks running meanwhile,
  # and cancellable. `try_flock_*` answers at once whether it took it.
  #
  # Linux and darwin lock with `flock(2)`, which only other locks heed, and
  # turn a shared lock this file holds into an exclusive one in place.
  # Windows locks every byte with `LockFileEx`, which is mandatory - while
  # one handle holds it exclusively, another handle's reads and writes of
  # the file fail - and counts each lock a handle takes: unlock a shared
  # lock before taking the exclusive one.

  # when the block panics.

  # Gives the lock back; one this file does not hold is no error.

  # no descriptor - a `Memory` - is -1, which Windows' `to_u64` of it
  # panicked "arithmetic overflow" on; it is EBADF everywhere, as Linux's
  # kernel answers it.

module std/format

# The argument list as one array or tuple, as `sprintf` takes it.
pub def printf(format_string : String, args : Array) : Nil

pub def printf(format_string : String, args : Tuple) : Nil

pub def printf(format_string : String, *args : *T) : Nil forall T

# The argument list may be one array or tuple, as the other library takes
# it: `"%s, %s, %s, D" % ['A', 'B', 'C']`, its own example, panicked "too
# few arguments for format string" here, and `"[%s]" % ["A"]` printed
# `[["A"]]` where it prints `[A]`. Two overloads rather than one taking
# `Array | Tuple`: a union with Array in it cannot be written into an
# artifact ("can't use Array(T) in unions yet").
pub def sprintf(format_string : String, args : Array) : String

pub def sprintf(format_string : String, args : Tuple) : String

pub def sprintf(format_string : String, *args : *T) : String forall T

class ::IyiBig
  # self / small for a `small` under 2^32, self reduced to the quotient,
  # the remainder answered. A limb is 32 bits in a 64-bit word, so the
  # running remainder shifted up by a limb still fits the word.
  def div_small(small : UInt64) : UInt64
  # Base ten, most significant digit first, nine digits per division.
  def to_decimal : String
end

module ::IyiFloatText
  # Extracts Dragon4 digits for a non-zero, finite double.
  # Returns {digits_pointer, count, k} where value = 0.d1 d2 ... dn * 10^k.
  def self.dragon4(value : Float64) : ::Tuple(Pointer(UInt8), Int32, Int32)
  # Scientific notation with exact places, half to even.
  def self.format_exp(value : Float64, uppercase : Bool, precision : Int32, hash_flag : Bool) : String
  # Fixed-point decimal format with exact places, half to even.
  def self.format_fixed(value : Float64, precision : Int32) : String
  # a * b as its high and low words, from 32-bit halves.
  def self.mul_wide(a : UInt64, b : UInt64) : ::Tuple(UInt64, UInt64)
  # Every digit the double has, not the shortest ones padded with zeros:
  # `round(f * 2^e * 10^places)`, half to even, as decimal digits. This is
  # what a fixed or scientific format prints, and what it did not print:
  # `%.0f` of 1e23 answered 100000000000000000000000 where the double is
  # 99999999999999991611392, `%.20f` of 0.1 answered twenty zeros where
  # the value's digits are 0.10000000000000000555, and `%e` of the
  # smallest denormal answered 5.000000e-324 for 4.940656e-324 - the
  # shortest digits, which round-trip, are not the value, and past them
  # there was nothing but zeros. `places` may be negative, a scale down.
  def self.scaled_digits(f : UInt64, e : Int32, places : Int32) : String
  # `scaled_digits` in two words, when they hold it: f * 10^places is
  # under 2^117 for the places a word of ten's powers reaches, and the
  # quotient by 2^-e and its half-to-even rounding are shifts and one
  # comparison of the remainder with the half. The same integer the
  # bignum's division gives - it is the same arithmetic, exact - where
  # that division made `%.2f` three times what Go's takes. nil when the
  # value, the places or the answer do not fit.
  def self.scaled_quick(f : UInt64, e : Int32, places : Int32) : UInt64 | ::Nil
end

module ::IyiFormat
  # Any integer: an `Int64` or a `UInt64`, whose top half `to_i64` refuses.
  def self.code_point(code) : Char
  # A width or a precision, which an `Int32` holds: read into one, the
  # digits of `%99999999999d` panicked "arithmetic overflow".
  def self.field_number(format_string : String, start : Int32, stop : Int32, what : String) : Int32
  def self.format_arg(val, verb : Char, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String

  # `é`, where it panicked "233 is out of char range" (`chr` is ASCII).
  # Anything else is its first character, not its first byte, which cut
  # `é` in half.
  def self.format_char_arg(val, minus : Bool, width : Int32) : String
  # Digits as `to_s(base)` writes them, a `-` first when negative, given
  # the verb's sign, prefix, precision and width.
  def self.format_digits(text : String, verb : Char, base : Int32, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String
  def self.format_float64(val : Float64, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String
  def self.format_float_exp(val : Float64, uppercase : Bool, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String
  # `%g`: the shorter of the two notations, C's rule. With P the precision
  # (6 when none is given, 1 when it is 0) and X the exponent `%e` would
  # write at P - 1 places, it is `%e` at P - 1 places when X < -4 or X >= P
  # and `%f` at P - 1 - X places otherwise; either way the trailing zeros
  # of the fraction go, and its point with them, unless `#` keeps them.
  # NaN and the infinities are written as `%e` writes them.
  def self.format_float_general(val : Float64, uppercase : Bool, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String
  def self.format_int64(val : Int64, base : Int32, uppercase : Bool, signed : Bool, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String

  # short by one space per extra byte, and a precision cut a character in
  # half. The prelude's `ljust`/`rjust` decided the same thing.

  # The characters a precision keeps are written into one buffer, as
  # `each_char` decodes them and `size` counts them: added one at a time
  # onto a string of their own, the text was copied once per character,
  # and `%.800000s` of a megabyte took 12.8 s, four times as long for
  # every doubling.
  def self.format_string_arg(str : String, minus : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String

  # and the other language answer to it. Past an `Int64` the truncation is
  # the double's own integer, f * 2^e, written whole as Python writes it:
  # `%d` of 1e30 is 1000000000000000019884624838656, where `to_i64`
  # panicked "arithmetic overflow". NaN and the infinities have no
  # integer, and the refusal says that rather than "arithmetic overflow".
  def self.format_truncated(val : Float64, verb : Char, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String
  def self.format_uint64(val : UInt64, base : Int32, uppercase : Bool, signed : Bool, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String

  # `Int64` is.
  def self.format_wide(val, verb : Char, minus : Bool, plus : Bool, space : Bool, zero : Bool, hash : Bool, width : Int32, precision : Int32) : String

module std/gc

pub struct GC
  # What the collector can answer, read at one instant.
  struct Stats
    # Bytes the last sweep handed back, and bytes it found still live.
    def bytes_freed_by_last_sweep : UInt64
    def bytes_kept_by_last_sweep : UInt64
    # Bytes allocated since the last collection: the word the allocation
    # trigger reads, folded in per cache slice and reset by every
    # collection.
    def bytes_since_collection : UInt64
    # How many collections have run.
    def collections : UInt64
    def initialize(mapped_bytes : UInt64, bytes_since_collection : UInt64, bytes_freed_by_last_sweep : UInt64, bytes_kept_by_last_sweep : UInt64, collections : UInt64)
    # Bytes the arenas and large mappings hold from the machine. A
    # reservation, counted in whole mappings; not bytes in use.
    def mapped_bytes : UInt64
    def to_s : String
  end
  # Runs one collection now.
  def self.collect : Nil
  # The allocation trigger stops running collections until `enable`.
  def self.disable : Nil
  # The allocation trigger runs collections again. `collect` still works
  # while disabled.
  def self.enable : Nil
  # Hands a chunk back before the sweep would. A null pointer is nothing
  # to free.
  def self.free(pointer : ::Pointer(Void)) : Nil
  def initialize
  # Whether `pointer` points into a live chunk on the collector's heap:
  # its start or any byte inside it. Null, a stack address and a freed
  # chunk answer false.
  #
  # Under the runtime lock, as `stats` is: a word in no arena walks the
  # large-mapping list, and another thread's `free` or sweep unlinks and
  # unmaps those nodes under that lock. Walked without it, beside three
  # threads whose large chunks come and go, two seconds of `is_heap_ptr`
  # died of a memory fault in 10 runs of 10 (`bench/std_gc_exercise.iyi`).
  def self.is_heap_ptr(pointer : ::Pointer(Void)) : Bool
  # `size` zeroed bytes the collector scans for pointers. A negative size
  # is refused by name.
  def self.malloc(size : Int) : ::Pointer(Void)
  # `size` bytes the collector does not scan: for bytes that hold no
  # pointers, so the marker skips them. They are not cleared - a chunk the
  # sweep handed back comes out with its last owner's bytes, as Boehm's
  # `GC_malloc_atomic` hands them out - so the caller writes every byte
  # it reads. This said "zeroed" while 2000 chunks taken after a
  # collection freed 2000 filled ones came back dirty, every one.
  def self.malloc_atomic(size : Int) : ::Pointer(Void)
  # The chunk at `pointer`, resized to `size` bytes; the answer may be a
  # new address, with the old bytes copied.
  def self.realloc(pointer : ::Pointer(Void), size : Int) : ::Pointer(Void)
  # The numbers the collector keeps, read now.
  #
  # The walk holds the runtime lock, which a collection takes before it
  # stops anything and holds while the scavenge unlinks an arena or a
  # large mapping. Walked without it, a collection another thread's
  # allocation started could stop this walk on a mapping, unlink and unmap
  # it, and the walk's next read was of memory gone: beside three threads
  # allocating, two seconds of `stats` died of a memory fault in 10 runs
  # of 10 (`bench/std_gc_exercise.iyi`).
  def self.stats : Stats
end

module std/http

# A body as it arrives: from a connection, framed by its length, by chunks
# or by the connection's close, or from a string already in hand. `read`
# answers the next piece, "" once the body is done; what the other end
# does wrong is an `HTTPError`, and a connection that fails or is
# cancelled answers that. The first failure is kept: every read after it
# answers the same. A body coded `gzip`, `deflate` or `zstd` is decoded
# as it is read when the client asked for that.
#
# A body has a limit: past it a read answers an `HTTPError` with status
# 413. The server's is `Server::MAX_BODY`; a client's is none.
pub class BodyReader
  # The body's coding undone from here on: `Envelope::Gzip` for gzip,
  # `Envelope::Zlib` for HTTP's deflate - which some servers send as the
  # bare stream instead, without zlib's two bytes of header, so the first
  # two bytes are looked at first, and a pair that is not a zlib header
  # (RFC 1950 §2.2: method 8, a multiple of 31) is read as the bare
  # stream. A body that does not decode is an `HTTPError` naming the
  # coding and why.
  def decode(envelope : Envelope) : Nil
  # The body's `zstd` coding (RFC 8878) undone from here on, by std/zstd's
  # `ZstdReader` as the pieces arrive, frames one after another. A frame
  # that asks for a window past *max_window* bytes is refused rather than
  # given the memory (a window outside 1 KiB to 512 MiB is a panic), and a
  # body that does not decode is an `HTTPError` naming the coding and why.
  def decode_zstd(max_window : Int32 = Zstd::WINDOW_LIMIT) : Nil
  # Reads past the rest of the body, *limit* bytes at most: whether it
  # ended within them. A server reads past what a block left unread, so
  # the next request on the connection starts where it should.
  def drain(limit : Int64) : Bool
  # Whether every byte of the body has been read, the framing's end too.
  def finished? : Bool
  # A body that arrives as an HTTP/2 stream's DATA: refused past *limit*.
  protected def self.frames(h2 : H2Connection, id : Int32, limit : Int64) : BodyReader
  def initialize(conn : Conn | ::Nil, kind : Int32, length : Int64, limit : Int64, text : String = "", hello : Proc(Bool) | ::Nil = nil)
  protected def on_frames(h2 : H2Connection, id : Int32) : Nil
  # The body's bytes as the framing delivers them, before any decoding.
  protected def raw(max : Int32) : String | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # The next piece of the body, at most *max* bytes; "" when it is done.
  def read(max : Int32 = 65536) : String | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # The rest of the body as one string, refused past *limit* bytes (413).
  # The pieces are kept as they arrive and joined once: a builder of the
  # length a head declared was made before any of it had come, and a head
  # that declared 64 MB and sent two bytes cost the server 64 MB.
  def read_all(limit : Int64 = 2147483647_i64) : String | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  protected def remember(fault : HTTPError | Cancelled | SocketError) : HTTPError | Cancelled | SocketError
  # A body that is a string already in hand.
  def self.text(text : String) : BodyReader
  # Whether the body ends where the connection does: nothing can follow
  # it on the connection.
  def to_close? : Bool
end

# What a streamed body is written to: an answer's `Response.stream`
# block's, and a client's upload from an `IyiIO`. Each `write` goes out as
# one chunk (RFC 9112 §7.1), or as it is where the connection's close ends
# the body, so a block that writes a line a second is read a line a
# second. Under a server's `compress`, each write is a gzip piece flushed
# whole (std/compress's `Deflater`), which decodes as it arrives too. The
# first failure is kept, and every write after it answers it; `finish`,
# which the server calls when the block returns, writes the end.
pub class BodyWriter
  # The end of the body: the gzip trailer, and the last chunk with the
  # blank line after it. Once; the server's call after a block that
  # finished its own body writes nothing.
  def finish : Nil | Cancelled | SocketError
  def initialize(socket : IyiSocket | TlsStream | H2Out, chunked : Bool, deflater : Deflater | ::Nil = nil)
  def write(text : String) : Nil | Cancelled | SocketError
  # Bytes of the body written so far, before any framing or coding.
  def written : Int64
end

# What `HTTP.request`'s `jar:` keeps cookies in: the `Cookie` header a
# request to a URL carries, and an answer's `Set-Cookie` lines taken in.
# std/cookie's `CookieJar` is one; std/http itself reads no clock, so the
# expiry of a cookie is the store's to keep.
pub trait CookieStore
  abstract def header_for(url : String) : String | ::Nil
  abstract def update(url : String, response : Response) : Nil
end

pub struct HTTP
  # For a request target in absolute form (RFC 9112 §3.2.2), where its
  # authority starts: after `http://` or `https://`, in any case.
  def self.absolute_form(target : String) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Whether a list of codings a client accepts (`Accept-Encoding`, RFC
  # 9110 §12.5.3) takes *coding*: named, or `*`, with a `q` above 0.
  def self.accepts?(list : String, coding : String) : Bool
  # A 1xx, 204 or 304: an answer with no content (RFC 9110 §15).
  def self.bodiless?(status : Int32) : Bool
  # Where a chunked body that starts at *from* ends in `text` — the byte
  # after the last chunk's terminating CRLF (trailers included) — nil when
  # it has not all arrived, or why it is not a chunked body. What
  # `decode_chunked` will then read whole.
  def self.chunked_end(text : String, from : Int32 = 0) : Int32 | String | Nil
  # How much a list of codings a client accepts wants *coding*, as its
  # `q` in thousandths: the weight it is named with, else `*`'s, else 0 -
  # and 0 refuses it.
  def self.coding_weight(list : String, coding : String) : Int32
  # A `Content-Length` as a number, or nil when it is not one. Repeated
  # lines arrive joined, and are one length only when every one says the
  # same (RFC 9112 §6.3). A length past 2147483647 is still a length, too
  # large for either side, and is read as one past it: `to_i?` answered
  # nil for it, and 3000000000 was refused as "not a number".
  def self.content_length(value : String) : Int64 | ::Nil
  # A control character other than a tab, or DEL: what a field value may
  # not hold (RFC 9110 §5.5), nor a request target or a reason phrase.
  def self.control?(text : String) : Bool
  # The pairs of a request's `Cookie` header, `a=1; b=2` (RFC 6265 §4.2),
  # a value's quotes taken off; the first of a name is kept, as a server
  # reads the most specific cookie first.
  def self.cookie_pairs(value : String) : Hash(String, String)
  # A chunked body (RFC 9112 §7.1) as one string: each chunk's size line
  # is hexadecimal, extensions after `;` are ignored, and a zero-length

  # here reads.
  def self.decode_chunked(text : String) : String
  def self.delete(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  def self.find_headers_end(text : String, from : Int32 = 0) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # The request as it goes on the wire, whole. `Host`, `Connection` and
