  # always written for the methods a body belongs to, so `POST` with
  # nothing to say still says `Content-Length: 0`. A byte of the path past
  # 127 goes as `%` and two hex digits: a request target is ASCII (RFC
  # 9112 §3.2, RFC 3986 §2.1), and `/ü` went out as its UTF-8 bytes, raw.
  def self.format_request(method : String, path : String, host : String, body : String = "", headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : String
  def self.get(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # *text* in gzip, whole: an answer's body under a server's `compress`.
  def self.gzip(text : String) : String
  # A writer whose body goes out in gzip as it is written.
  def self.gzip_writer(socket : IyiSocket | TlsStream | H2Out, chunked : Bool) : BodyWriter
  def self.has_break?(text : String) : Bool
  # Whether a list of tokens (RFC 9110 §5.6.1), its repeated lines joined
  # with ", ", holds *token*, in any case.
  def self.has_token?(list : String, token : String) : Bool
  def self.head(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # The value of a chunk size's hex digits, nil for anything else or for
  # one past what an Int32 holds.
  def self.hex(text : String) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # *n* in lowercase hexadecimal: a chunk's size line.
  def self.hex_text(n : Int64) : String
  # A Host value - the `a` of `Host: a` - or an absolute-form target's
  # authority, made of what a host and its port are spelled with (RFC 3986
  # §3.2.2, §3.2.3): a name, an IPv4 address or an IPv6 one in brackets,
  # and digits after a colon. Empty is one too, for a target with no
  # authority (RFC 9112 §3.2). A blank, a `/`, an `@` - the bytes another
  # host or a path begins with - are not.
  def self.host?(text : String) : Bool
  def initialize
  # One request, and the block's answer to the response, its body still
  # arriving: `response.body_io.read` takes it a piece at a time, and
  # `response.body` all of it. The connection closes when the block
  # returns. A body of *body* is a string, sent with its length, or an
  # `IyiIO`, sent chunked as it is read - which a redirect that keeps the
  # method (307, 308) cannot send again, so that answer is handed to the
  # block as it is.
  #
  # The redirects followed are RFC 9110 §15.4's: 301 and 302 make a POST a
  # GET, 303 makes anything but a HEAD a GET, and 307 and 308 keep the
  # method and the body. `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization` and
  # `Cookie` written by the caller are not sent to another host. One more
  # than *redirects* is an `HTTPError`; with 0 the first answer is the
  # block's.
  #
  # *timeout_ms* bounds the connect, and each read and write after it -
  # a pause, not the whole exchange, as Python's `timeout` is: a body that
  # keeps arriving is read for as long as it takes. One that runs out is a
  # `SocketError` whose `timed_out?` is true. 0, the default, waits as
  # long as the server does, as Go's and Python's clients do; a client
  # that talks to servers it does not control should give one.
  #
  # *proxy* is a proxy's URL - `http://user:password@host:port`, or
  # `host:port` alone - and every request goes through it, every redirect
  # too: `http://` as an absolute-form request to the proxy (RFC 9112
  # §3.2.2), which carries `Proxy-Authorization: Basic` when the URL has
  # a user; `https://` through a tunnel the proxy opens with `CONNECT
  # host:port` (RFC 9110 §9.3.6), the credential on the CONNECT alone and
  # TLS to the server inside it, its certificate checked as without a
  # proxy. A caller's own `Proxy-Authorization` is the proxy's too: sent
  # on the CONNECT when the URL has no user, and never inside the tunnel.
  # A CONNECT answered with anything but a 2xx - 407 when the proxy wants
  # credentials, 403, 502 - is an `HTTPError` naming the proxy and its
  # answer. `http://` through a proxy is HTTP/1.1 whatever
  # *prior_knowledge* says. Which proxy, if any, a URL's environment
  # names is `proxy_for`'s, and std/http_proxy's `HTTPProxy.from_env`.

  # The field lines after the first, or why they are not fields. A name
  # repeated, in any case, is one field, its values joined in order with
  # ", " (RFC 9110 §5.3): into a Hash by name, a second line spelled the
  # same replaced the first and one spelled otherwise was an entry
  # `header` never reached, so two different `Content-Length`s were read
  # as whichever came first or last. A value with a control character in
  # it - a CR or LF that ends no line, a NUL - is refused (§5.5) rather than
  # handed to whoever reads it or echoes it into a header.

  # *unfold*, for an answer: a line that begins with a blank continues the
  # field above it (obs-fold, RFC 9112 §5.2), and a user agent joins it on

  # "header without a colon: \" b\"". A server may refuse one, and this
  # one does.

  # name in the answer, a line each, before they are joined.
  def self.parse_fields(lines : Array(String), unfold : Bool = false, apart : Hash(String, Array(String)) | ::Nil = nil) : Hash(String, String) | String

  # send. An interim answer - `100 Continue`, `103 Early Hints` - is read
  # past to the final one after it (RFC 9110 §15.2). A `101` switches
  # protocols, and HTTP ends with it. What is not a response panics with
  # why: this is the text a program has in hand; the client answers the
  # same sentences as `HTTPError`s.
  def self.parse_response(text : String, head : Bool = false) : Response
  # A response's head - the text before its blank line - read: status,
  # reason, the fields, and the lines of those on more than one. A line
  # that begins with a blank continues the field above it (obs-fold, RFC
  # 9112 §5.2), which a user agent joins on with one space.
  def self.parse_response_head(text : String) : ::Tuple(Int32, String, Hash(String, String), Hash(String, Array(String)) | ::Nil) | HTTPError
  # Where *text* goes on at *from* past the empty lines there: what a
  # server skips before a request line (RFC 9112 §2.2).
  def self.past_empty_lines(text : String, from : Int32) : Int32
  def self.post(url : String, body : String | IyiIO = "", headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError

  # line, as its documentation and tests state it:
  #

  #   scheme none. A proxy written without a scheme is `http://`'s, and is
  #   answered with it, ready for `open`'s *proxy*.

  #   An entry that is none of these (`:80`) is passed over.

  # std/http_proxy reads them from it.

  # server writes; a status this table does not know gets its class's.
  def self.reason_for(status : Int32) : String

  # `close`, or `Upgrade`), the caller's headers, and the body's framing -
  # *length*, chunks, or none.
  def self.request_head(method : String, path : String, host : String, headers : Hash(String, String), length : Int64 | ::Nil, chunked : Bool, connection : String) : String

  # a name may carry.
  def self.same_name?(a : String, b : String) : Bool
  def self.split_crlf(text : String) : Array(String)
  # A status line read: the status and its reason, or why it is not one.
  def self.status_line(line : String) : ::Tuple(Int32, String) | HTTPError

  # system's roots, and ALPN's `http/1.1`, unless a program sets its own -

  def self.tls_config : TlsConfig
  def self.tls_config=(config : TlsConfig) : TlsConfig
  # A token (RFC 9110 §5.6.2): what a method or a field name is made of.
  def self.token?(text : String) : Bool
  # Without the blanks at either end (RFC 9112 §5.1: field values are
  # trimmed of the whitespace around them).
  def self.trim(s : String) : String

  # which is the caller's from then on: std/websocket's handshake. Any
  # other answer is an `HTTPError` naming it.
  #
  # *proxy* is `open`'s, and so is its credential, on the CONNECT alone;
  # but an upgrade goes through a tunnel for `http://` as for `https://`,
  # the handshake inside it in origin form. `Upgrade` belongs to the
  # connection it is sent on (RFC 9110 §7.8), and a proxy forwarding a
  # request removes `Connection` and every field it names (§7.6.1), so a
  # handshake handed to a forward proxy in absolute form reaches the
  # server, at best, as a plain GET: the gate's proxy, which drops
  # `Connection`, leaves std/websocket's server a request it answers 400.
  def self.upgrade(url : String, protocol : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String, timeout_ms : Int32 = 0, proxy : String | ::Nil = nil) : Upgraded | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
end

# Requests that keep their connections: an `HTTPClient` holds the connections
# its answers left open, by host and port, and the next request to that
# server goes over one of them instead of a new one - the TCP handshake,
# and the slow start after it, paid once rather than per request. Its
# methods are `HTTP`'s, redirects, cookies and decoding included:
#
# ```
# client = HTTPClient.new
# client.get("http://127.0.0.1:8080/a")
# client.get("http://127.0.0.1:8080/b") # the same connection
# client.close
# ```
#
# A connection goes back once its answer has been read to the end (inside
# `open`, up to 64 KiB left unread is read past for it) and the answer
# allows it; at most *idle* wait per server, and the rest close. A server
# may close an idle connection whenever it likes (RFC 9112 §9.3.1), so a
# request whose kept connection turns out closed - the write fails, or it
# ends before a byte of an answer - is sent again once on a new one, when
# its method is idempotent (RFC 9110 §9.2.2) and its body a string;
# anything else answers the failure. One task at a time per request: two
# tasks sending at once take two connections, and a client is not for
# sharing across threads.
#
# Over HTTP/2 - `https://` where ALPN chose `h2`, or `http://` with
# *prior_knowledge* (h2c, RFC 9113 §3.3) - a kept connection carries the
# next request on a new stream, until the server says GOAWAY.
pub class HTTPClient
  # Every idle connection closed. The client may be used after; it opens
  # new ones.
  def close : Nil
  # Connections this client has opened, and requests sent over one it
  # kept: what a program reads to see that its connections are kept.
  def connections_made : Int32
  def connections_reused : Int32
  def delete(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  def get(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  protected def give_back(key : String, conn : Conn) : Nil
  def head(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # *timeout_ms* and *proxy* are `HTTP.open`'s, for every request the
  # client sends.
  def initialize(idle : Int32 = 4, timeout_ms : Int32 = 0, prior_knowledge : Bool = false, proxy : String | ::Nil = nil)
  protected def made : Nil
  def open(method : String, url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String, body : String | IyiIO = "", redirects : Int32 = 10, jar : CookieStore | ::Nil = nil, decompress : Bool = true, &block : (Response -> R)) : R | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError forall R
  def post(url : String, body : String | IyiIO = "", headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # `http://` spoken as HTTP/2 from the first byte, without asking: for a
  # server known to take it.
  def prior_knowledge : Bool
  # The proxy every request goes through, `HTTP.open`'s *proxy*; its
  # connections are kept under it.
  def proxy : String | ::Nil
  def put(url : String, body : String | IyiIO = "", headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  def request(method : String, url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String, body : String | IyiIO = "", redirects : Int32 = 10, jar : CookieStore | ::Nil = nil, decompress : Bool = true) : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # A kept connection to *key*, nil when none waits. An HTTP/2 connection
  # that can take no more requests is closed rather than handed out.
  protected def take(key : String) : Conn | ::Nil
end

# What the other end did that HTTP does not allow, as a value: `reason` is
# the sentence, `status` the answer a server gives a request that did it
# (400, or 413 and 431 for the limits). `message` says it is HTTP's.
pub struct HTTPError
  def initialize(reason : String, status : Int32 = 400)
  def reason : String
  def status : Int32
  def to_s : String
end

# A `multipart/form-data` body (RFC 7578) read a part at a time, as it
# arrives: `next_part` answers the next `Part`, nil after the last, and a
# part's `read` answers its bytes up to the boundary, "" at its end. A part
# not read to its end is read past by the next `next_part`. The body of a
# request is `Request#multipart`'s; any `BodyReader` and boundary will do.
# A part's head is refused past 16 KiB, and a body that ends before its
# closing boundary is an `HTTPError`.
pub class Multipart
  # The boundary a `Content-Type` of `multipart/...` names, nil when it
  # names none.
  def self.boundary(content_type : String) : String | ::Nil
  # Where *pattern* is in what is held, -1 when it is not there yet.
  protected def find(pattern : String) : Int32
  def initialize(body : BodyReader, boundary : String)
  # The next part, nil after the last.
  def next_part : Part | Nil | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # Up to *max* bytes of the part being read, "" at its boundary. What is
  # held back is what may yet be the start of the boundary.
  protected def part_read(max : Int32) : String | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # One more piece of the body onto what is held: false at its end.
  protected def pull : Bool | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
end

# A multipart/form-data body to send: fields and files in order. Its
# boundary is chosen when the body is first asked for - `finish`,
# `content_type` or `boundary`, whichever comes first, after which no
# part is added - as `iyi-` and 32 hex digits of the parts' SHA-1, made
# again from itself in the rare case a part holds it: so it is none of
# the parts' bytes by construction rather than by chance, the same
# fields make the same body, and std/http reaches no source of
# randomness for it. A boundary given to `new` is used as it is, and a
# part that holds it is refused.
pub class MultipartBuilder
  def boundary : String
  def content_type : String
  def field(name : String, value : String) : self
  def file(name : String, filename : String, data : String, content_type : String = MIME.from_extension(filename)) : self
  # The body, closing boundary and all.
  def finish : String
  # The boundary ends a part where it follows a CRLF, the part's first
  # bytes included, which follow the head's blank line.
  protected def self.holds?(data : String, mark : String) : Bool
  def initialize(boundary : String | ::Nil = nil)
  # A name inside quotes, as browsers write one: a quote and a line break
  # percent-encoded (the WHATWG form encoding), so no field can end the
  # parameter or the line early.
  protected def self.quoted(text : String) : String
end

# One part of a multipart body: its head's fields, its name and file name
# from `Content-Disposition`, and its bytes, read up to its boundary.
pub class Part
  def content_type : String | ::Nil
  # The file name a browser sent the part under, `filename=`.
  def filename : String | ::Nil
  def finished? : Bool
  def header(name : String) : String | ::Nil
  def headers : Hash(String, String)
  def initialize(owner : Multipart, headers : Hash(String, String))
  # The form field's name, `name=` of `Content-Disposition`.
  def name : String | ::Nil
  # The part's next bytes, at most *max*; "" at its end.
  def read(max : Int32 = 65536) : String | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  # The rest of the part as one string, refused past *limit* bytes.
  def read_all(limit : Int64 = 2147483647_i64) : String | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
end

# What a server's block is handed: one request. Its body is `body`, read
# whole before the block ran, or under `stream_bodies` read by the block
# from `body_io` as it arrives; `body` then reads the rest itself, and a
# body that cannot be read - the client went, or sent one that is not
# HTTP - ends the connection with that sentence rather than be answered as
# if it were whole.
pub class Request
  def body : String
  def body_io : BodyReader
  # The pairs of the request's `Cookie` header, the first of a name kept.
  def cookies : Hash(String, String)
  # The fields of a form: the query's, and an
  # `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body's after them. The body is
  # read for it.
  def form : Params
  def header(name : String) : String | ::Nil
  def headers : Hash(String, String)
  # A request whose body is in hand: what `parse_request` answers.
  def initialize(method : String, path : String, query : String | ::Nil, headers : Hash(String, String), body : String, version : String = "HTTP/1.1", remote_address : String | ::Nil = nil)
  # A request whose body is still on the connection.
  def initialize(method : String, path : String, query : String | ::Nil, headers : Hash(String, String), version : String, reader : BodyReader, remote_address : String | ::Nil = nil)
  def method : String
  # The body as `multipart/form-data` parts, read as they arrive; nil when
  # the `Content-Type` is not multipart or names no boundary.
  def multipart : Multipart | ::Nil
  def path : String
  # The client's certificate chain, leaf first, as std/tls checked it:
  # under `serve(tls:)` with `client_roots` set, the certificate the
  # client presented; empty otherwise.
  def peer_certificates : Array(Certificate)
  # The client's certificate chain, leaf first, as std/tls checked it:
  # under `serve(tls:)` with `client_roots` set, the certificate the
  # client presented; empty otherwise.
  def peer_certificates=(value : Array(Certificate)) : Array(Certificate)
  def query : String | ::Nil
  # The client's address, as the server's socket saw it (no port): nil
  # for a request a program made, or when the client had already gone. A
  # proxy in front is what this names; `X-Forwarded-For` is the proxy's
  # word, and a header any client can write.
  def remote_address : String | ::Nil
  def version : String
end

# A response: what a server's block answers, and what a client is handed.
#
# To write one: `Response.new(200, "hello")`, a status and a string;
# `Response.new(200, io)`, a stream the server copies out and closes, with
# the caller's `Content-Length` when it gives one and chunked otherwise;
# `Response.stream(200) { |w| w.write("...") }`, whose block writes as it
# goes; `Response.upgrade(headers) { |socket, leftover| ... }`, a 101 after
# which the connection is the block's. `add_header` writes a field on a
# line of its own, as each `Set-Cookie` must be.
#
# What a client is handed: the status, reason and headers, and the body -
# `body` whole, or `body_io` as it arrives inside `HTTP.open`'s block.
pub class Response
  # One more line of the field *name*, written on a line of its own: what
  # two `Set-Cookie`s need, since the ", " a field's lines are joined with
  # is part of a cookie's date.
  def add_header(name : String, value : String) : Nil
  # The lines of each field written on more than one, by its name in
  # `headers`; nil when every field is on one line.
  def apart : Hash(String, Array(String)) | ::Nil
  # The body: whole. Inside `HTTP.open`'s block it is read here, the first
  # time it is asked for, and a body that cannot be read panics with why;
  # `body_io` answers that as a value.
  def body : String
  # The body as it arrives. For a response a program made, its string.
  def body_io : BodyReader
  # Whether the client undid the body's `gzip`, `deflate` or `zstd`
  # coding; the `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` that described it
  # are gone from the headers then.
  def decoded? : Bool
  # A header by name, as the server spelled it or otherwise: a field
  # name is case-insensitive (RFC 9110 §5.1), and `content-length` is as
  # common on the wire as `Content-Length`.
  def header(name : String) : String | ::Nil
  # A field's lines apart, in the order they came: `header` joins them
  # with ", ", and `Set-Cookie` is the field that join breaks (RFC 9110
  # §5.3), since a cookie's `Expires` date has a comma in it - two cookies
  # read as "a=1; Expires=Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT, b=2", which no
  # split takes back apart. Empty for a field that is not there.
  def header_values(name : String) : Array(String)
  def headers : Hash(String, String)
  # A response a client read: its body comes from *reader*, and *url* is
  # where it came from.
  def initialize(status : Int32, reason : String, headers : Hash(String, String), apart : Hash(String, Array(String)) | ::Nil, reader : BodyReader, url : String, decoded : Bool)
  def initialize(status : Int32, reason : String, headers : Hash(String, String), body : String, apart : Hash(String, Array(String)) | ::Nil = nil)
  # A response to write: the reason is the status's own, the headers the
  # caller's. `Response.new(200, "hello")` is the common shape.
  def initialize(status : Int32, body : String = "", headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String)
  # A response whose body is *source*, copied out by the server and
  # closed after.
  def initialize(status : Int32, source : IyiIO, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String)
  # The body read whole into the response, which is answered; why not,
  # when it cannot be.
  def load : Response | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  def reason : String
  def source : IyiIO | ::Nil
  def status : Int32
  # A response whose body the block writes as it goes, chunked.
  def self.stream(status : Int32, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String, &writer : (BodyWriter -> Nil)) : Response
  def success? : Bool
  def takeover : Proc(IyiSocket | TlsStream, String, Nil) | ::Nil
  protected def takeover=(takeover : Proc(IyiSocket | TlsStream, String, Nil)) : Proc(IyiSocket | TlsStream, String, Nil)
  # A 101 Switching Protocols with *headers* (`Upgrade` and the
  # protocol's own), after which the connection is the block's: it is
  # handed the connection - the socket, or under `serve(tls:)` the
  # `TlsStream` over it - and the bytes the client sent after its request,
  # and the connection closes when it returns.
  def self.upgrade(headers : Hash(String, String), &takeover : (IyiSocket | TlsStream, String -> Nil)) : Response
  # The URL the answer came from, after any redirects; nil for one a
  # program made.
  def url : String | ::Nil
  def writer : Proc(BodyWriter, Nil) | ::Nil
  protected def writer=(writer : Proc(BodyWriter, Nil)) : Proc(BodyWriter, Nil)
end

pub struct Server
  # The headers a coded body goes with: the coding, and `Vary` so that a
  # cache keeps the answers apart. A `Content-Length` the block gave is
  # the plain body's, and goes.
  protected def self.coded(response : Response, coding : String) : Response
  # The coding *response* goes in to the client of *req*, or nil: one the
  # client takes (RFC 9110 §12.5.3, a `q` of 0 refusing it), for an
  # answer with a body and a type worth compressing, and no coding of its
  # own. A whole body goes `zstd` when the client's `q` for it is at least
  # its `q` for gzip, and `gzip` otherwise. The tie goes to zstd for the
  # server's time: measured on this machine, release builds, on
  # src/std/http.iyi (199,134 bytes) `Gzip.compress` wrote 54,484 bytes in
  # 5 ms and `Zstd.compress` 61,753 in 1 ms, and on CHANGELOG.md (1.5 MB)
  # 552,446 in 58 ms against 589,785 in 13 ms - a quarter of the time, for
  # an eighth more bytes at most. A stream - an `IyiIO` or a
  # `Response.stream` - goes gzip or as it is: std/compress's `Deflater`
  # writes each piece as it comes, where std/zstd's compressor takes its
  # input whole, and a frame a write would code each piece alone.
  def self.coding_for(req : Request, response : Response) : String | ::Nil
  # A string body compressed whole in *coding*, `zstd` or `gzip`, with
  # the headers that say so. `Zstd.compress`'s frame needs a window of
  # 1 MiB at most, inside the 8 MB RFC 9659 §3 holds an encoder to.
  protected def self.compressed(response : Response, coding : String) : Response
  # A response's head. `Content-Length` is *length*'s - the caller's own
  # line is checked against it, and kept only where no body follows it: a
  # HEAD, or a 304 that names the length a 200 would have (RFC 9110 §8.6) -
  # or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` when *chunked*, or neither for a body
  # the connection's close ends. `Connection` says what the connection will
  # do next, except on an *upgrade*, whose own line says it. A 1xx, 204 or
  # 304 has no content (RFC 9110 §15), and writes neither a body nor a
  # length of its own (§8.6): the body was read by the client as the start
  # of the next answer, and `Content-Length: 0` on a 304 told a cache that
  # the resource had become empty. A field added on lines of its own
  # (`add_header`) is written a line each.
  def self.format_head(response : Response, head : Bool, close : Bool, length : Int64 | ::Nil, chunked : Bool, upgrade : Bool = false) : String
  # The response as it goes on the wire, whole: `format_head` for its
  # string body, and the body.
  def self.format_response(response : Response, head : Bool, close : Bool) : String
  # One connection: requests until the client is done. A request that is
  # not HTTP is answered with why and the connection closed, since the
  # bytes after it cannot be trusted to be a request either. Requests that
  # came in one read are read where they lie, one after another. A
  # connection that opens with HTTP/2's preface is served as HTTP/2. Under
  # *tls* the handshake comes first, and the connection ends with
  # close_notify.
  def self.handle(client : IyiSocket, handler : Proc(Request, Response), listener : IyiSocket | ::Nil = nil, idle : Hash(UInt64, IyiSocket) | ::Nil = nil, stream_bodies : Bool = false, compress : Bool = false, timeout_ms : Int32 = 0, tls : TlsServerConfig | ::Nil = nil) : Nil
  def initialize
  # A request's head - the text before its blank line - read and checked,
  # or why it is not one.
  def self.parse_head(text : String) : RequestHead | HTTPError
  # A request at *from* in `text`, if a whole one is there. No request and
  # no error means "not yet". `consumed` counts from the start of `text`.
  def self.parse_request(text : String, from : Int32 = 0) : ParsedRequest
  # Serve `listener` until it is closed. The block runs on the
  # connection's fiber, once per request; what it answers is written back.
  # The close ends a connection waiting on its client too, for its next
  # request or for the rest of one, and one that is answering ends when its
  # answer is written: a keep-alive client that sat idle kept `serve` from
  # returning for as long as it stayed, and so did one that had sent
  # what has arrived of a request so far - one byte of it was enough.
  #
  # *stream_bodies*: the block reads each request's body from `body_io`
  # rather than being handed it whole. *compress*: an answer whose type
  # std/mime calls compressible goes zstd or gzip to a client that
  # accepts one (`coding_for`).
  #
  # *timeout_ms*: a request's head must have arrived within it, counted
  # from when the server starts waiting for one - a kept-alive connection's
  # idle time included - and no read of a body nor write of an answer may
  # wait longer; a connection that does is closed. Without it, a client
  # that sends a byte of its head every few seconds (Slowloris) holds a
  # connection and its fiber for as long as it likes, and so does one that
  # reads none of its answer. A minute by default, nginx's
  # `client_header_timeout`; 0 for none. A connection handed over by
  # `Response.upgrade` waits as its protocol likes.
  #
  # *tls*: each connection is TLS 1.3 (std/tls's `TlsServer`) under this
  # configuration, its handshake held to *timeout_ms* too; one whose
  # handshake fails is closed, the client told why by an alert. Inside
  # it a connection that opens with HTTP/2's preface - as a client whose
  # ALPN chose `h2` does, when `tls.alpn` offers it - is served HTTP/2,
  # and any other HTTP/1.1. A `Response.upgrade` block over TLS is handed
  # the `TlsStream`, so a WebSocket is `wss://`.
  def self.serve(listener : IyiSocket, stream_bodies : Bool = false, compress : Bool = false, timeout_ms : Int32 = 60000, tls : TlsServerConfig | ::Nil = nil, &handler : (Request -> Response)) : Nil
  protected def self.writer_for(socket : IyiSocket | TlsStream, chunked : Bool, gzip : Bool) : BodyWriter
end

# A TLS connection used as a socket is: read into a buffer, written to,
# closed, its timeouts set - by a `Conn`, a `BodyWriter`, and a connection
# handed over by an upgrade (`wss://` at either end). What TLS refuses is a
# `SocketError` carrying TLS's own sentence (`layer_reason`), so answers
# keep the types they have over a plain socket.
pub class TlsStream
  def close : Nil
  def closed? : Bool
  def initialize(tls : TlsConnection, host : String)
  # The peer's certificate chain, leaf first, as the handshake checked it:
  # the server's, at a client; the client's, at a server that asked.
  def peer_certificates : Array(Certificate)
  # Up to *count* bytes into *buffer*: 0 once the peer closed with
  # close_notify.
  def read(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  # Up to *max_bytes* as a string, what is held first: "" once the peer
  # closed with close_notify. `IyiSocket#read`'s form, for a block an
  # upgrade hands either.
  def read(max_bytes : Int32 = 4096) : String | Cancelled | SocketError
  # How long a read or a write of the connection under it may wait.
  def read_timeout_ms=(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def write(text : String) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  def write_timeout_ms=(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
end

# What `HTTP.upgrade` answers: the 101, and the connection, which is the
# caller's now - the socket, and the bytes the server sent after its head.
pub class Upgraded
  def initialize(response : Response, socket : IyiSocket | TlsStream, leftover : String)
  def leftover : String
  def response : Response
  # The connection: the socket, or for `https://` the `TlsStream` over it.
  def socket : IyiSocket | TlsStream
end

impl Error for HTTPError
  def message : String
end

# Host names to and from the ASCII form DNS looks up, IDNA2008's way, label
# by label; the header says what is checked and what is not.
pub struct IDNA
  def initialize
  # RFC 5892's derived property of *char* (section 3), computed in the
  # order the RFC gives: the exceptions (section 2.6), unassigned code
  # points, the LDH characters, the joiners, and then a letter, digit or
  # mark that neither case folding nor NFKC changes, that is not default
  # ignorable, white space or a noncharacter, and not in the ignorable
  # blocks or old Hangul jamo. Everything else is Disallowed.
  def self.property(char : Char) : IdnaProperty
  # The name as DNS looks it up: every U-label as its `xn--` A-label,
  # every ASCII label lower-cased.
  def self.to_ascii(name : String) : String | IdnaError
  # The name as a person reads it: every A-label decoded, every ASCII
  # label lower-cased; checked as `to_ascii` checks it.
  def self.to_unicode(name : String) : String | IdnaError
  # `U+00FC`: four hex digits at least, upper case.
  def self.u_plus(cp : Int64) : String
end

# What `IDNA.to_ascii`, `IDNA.to_unicode` and `URI.ascii_host` answer for a
# name they cannot carry: the sentence names the label and why.
pub struct IdnaError
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

# The derived property of RFC 5892 section 2: whether a code point may
# appear in a U-label (PValid), only in a context (ContextJ, ContextO), not
# at all (Disallowed), or is unassigned in the Unicode `std/unicode` holds.
pub enum IdnaProperty : Int32
  PValid = 0
  ContextJ = 1
  ContextO = 2
  Disallowed = 3
  Unassigned = 4
end

# RFC 3492's bootstring with its Punycode parameters (section 5).
pub struct Punycode
  # The string *text* is the Punycode of (section 6.2), or the reason it
  # is none. Digits are read in either case; basic code points are kept
  # in the case they were written.
  def self.decode(text : String) : String | PunycodeError
  # The Punycode of *text*'s code points (section 6.3). Total: every
  # string has one. Bytes that are not UTF-8 are read as `each_char` reads
  # them, U+FFFD each.
  def self.encode(text : String) : String
  def initialize
end

# What `Punycode.decode` answers for input that is not Punycode.
pub struct PunycodeError
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

impl Error for PunycodeError
  def message : String
end

  def message : String

module std/indexable

pub trait Indexable
  type Elem
  # Returns the element at the given index. Negative indices count from the
  # end, so `a[-1]` returns the last element. Raises when index is out of
  # bounds, naming the index as it was written and the size there was:
  # `index out of range` on its own told a caller with a computed index
  # nothing it did not already know. The wording is `Array`'s
  # (src/iyi/array.iyi), because one mistake gets one sentence.
  def [](index : Int32) : Elem
  # Returns the element at the given index, or nil when index is out of bounds.
  # Negative indices count from the end.
  def []?(index : Int32) : Elem | ::Nil
  # Binary search on a sorted collection. Returns the first element for which
  # the block returns true, or nil if no element matches.
  def bsearch(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Elem | ::Nil
  # Binary search returning the index of the first element for which the block
  # returns true, or nil.
  def bsearch_index(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Single-index navigation.
  def dig(index : Int32) : Elem
  # Single-index nilable navigation.
  def dig?(index : Int32) : Elem | ::Nil
  # Default iteration yielding elements sequentially from 0 up to size - 1.
  # It answers `Enumerable`'s requirement for a type that also says `impl
  # Enumerable`, which is one more line than the ergonomics claim implies
  # (SPEC.md II.6) — the claim that this trait supplied it was false, and
  # `Array` went without `zip`, `take` and the rest until the line existed.
  def each(& : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Yields consecutive overlapping windows of n elements each.
  def each_cons(n : Int32, & : (Array(Elem) -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Returns an Array of consecutive overlapping windows of n elements each.
  def each_cons(n : Int32) : Array(Array(Elem))
  # Yields each valid index from 0 up to size - 1.
  def each_index(& : (Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Yields slices of n elements each to the given block.
  def each_slice(n : Int32, & : (Array(Elem) -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Returns an Array of slices of n elements each.
  def each_slice(n : Int32) : Array(Array(Elem))
  # Returns true when the collection contains no elements.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Structural equality comparing collection size and element values.

# `Indexable` with one more requirement, `unsafe_put`, from which the
# in-place operations follow. In-place variants are spelled `_in_place`;
# the copies (`rotated`, `reversed`) live on the concrete type, since a
# trait cannot build one without knowing how.
pub trait IndexableMutable : ::Std::Indexable::Indexable
  type Elem

  # mistake; a window that runs past the end is refused by naming the
  # index that would have been written.
  def fill(value : Elem, offset : Int32, count : Int32) : self
  # Every element becomes value.
  def fill(value : Elem) : self
  # Every element becomes what the block answers for its index.
  def fill(& : (Int32 -> Elem)) : self
  # Reverses elements in place.
  def reverse_in_place : self

  # first; a negative n rotates the other way. Three reversals, no
  # scratch space.
  def rotate_in_place(n : Int32 = 1) : self

  def swap(index0 : Int32, index1 : Int32) : self
  abstract def unsafe_put(index : Int32, value : Elem) : Elem
  # Replaces the element at index with what the block answers for it,
  # and answers the new value.
  def update(index : Int32, & : (Elem -> Elem)) : Elem
end

  # multiplicative fold, and one name means one thing.

  # Forgets every element.
  def clear : Array(T)
  # Removes the nils in place.
  def compact_in_place : Array(T)
  # Removes and answers the element at index, shifting what follows left.
  def delete_at(index : Int32) : T
  # Removes every element the block answers true for, in place, keeping
  # the order of the rest; one pass, no per-element shifting.
  def delete_if(& : (T -> Bool)) : Array(T)

  # Everything left in `source` (at most `limit` bytes) written to
  # `target`, which is flushed; answers the number of bytes moved.
  def self.copy(source : IyiIO, target : IyiIO, limit : Int32 | ::Nil = nil) : Int64
  def each_line(chomp : Bool = false, &block : (String -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Every remaining line, `chomp` dropping the line ends.
  def lines(chomp : Bool = false) : Array(String)
  # The two ends of a pipe between tasks: what is written to the writer is
  # read from the reader, in order.
  #
  #     reader, writer = IyiIO.pipe
  #     group do |g|
  #       g.spawn { IyiIO.copy(file, writer); writer.close; 0 }
  #       g.spawn { IyiIO.copy(reader, socket.io); 0 }
  #     end
  #
  # Each write is delivered at once, as one piece, and a write waits while
  # *capacity* pieces are unread; a read waits for one. Closing the writer
  # ends the reader after the last piece; closing the reader refuses the
  # next write, as a pipe whose reader is gone does. The pipe is its
  # thread's, for the tasks on the thread that made it.
  def self.pipe(capacity : Int32 = 16) : ::Tuple(Std::Io::PipeReader, Std::Io::PipeWriter)
  # The next byte, or nil at the end.
  def read_byte : UInt8 | ::Nil
  # The next UTF-8 code point, or nil at the end. A lead byte that is not
  # one (a continuation byte, C0/C1, F5 and above), a continuation byte that
  # is not one, or a sequence the stream ends inside is refused. The first
  # continuation byte is held to the range its lead allows (Unicode Table
  # 3-7), so an overlong form, a surrogate and a code point past U+10FFFF
  # are refused at the byte that gives them away, not decoded into a Char
  # outside Unicode.
  def read_char : Char | ::Nil
  def write_byte(byte : UInt8) : Nil
end

module std/iterator

# The sources are classes, as the other library's are: an adaptor keeps
# its source by value, and a struct source was copied into it, so
# `it.first(2).to_a` and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where
# the other library gives [1, 2] and [3, 4]. Shared, the adaptor's pulls
# are the source's. An adaptor that keeps a count, a flag or a buffer is
# the source of whatever is built on it, so it is a class for the same
# reason: as a struct it was copied too, and `t = it.take(3)`,
# `t.first(2).to_a` and then `t.to_a` gave [3, 4, 5] where the other
# library gives [3], `each_cons` handed its first window out again and
# `step` and `with_index` restarted their strides and counts. An adaptor
# that keeps only its sources, a block or a size stays a struct: a copy of
# it pulls from the same place.
#
# Each type defines `next` once and its `impl` names only `Elem`, as
# `NumericStepIterator` (std/steppable) does: every adaptor carried the same
# `next` twice, once on the type and once in the `impl`.
pub class ArrayIterator(T)
  def initialize(array : Array(T))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class ChainIterator(I1, I2, T)
  def initialize(iter1 : I1, iter2 : I2)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct CompactMapIterator(I, T, U)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> U | ::Nil))
  def next : U | Stop
end

pub class ConsIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : Array(T) | Stop
end

pub class CycleIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class CycleNIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

# The source an endless range gets: it counts up by one from the beginning
# with no end, as an endless range does in the other library.
pub class EndlessRangeIterator(B)
  def initialize(current : B)
  def next : B
end

pub class EntryIterator(K, V)
  def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V))
  def next : Tuple(K, V) | Stop
end

pub class FlatMapIterator(I, T, U)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Array(U)))
  def next : U | Stop
end

pub trait Iterator
  type Elem
  def all?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  # Whether an element is truthy, which is what the other library's `any?`
  # answers: this said whether there was an element at all, so
  # `Iterator.of([false, false]).any?` was true. It pulls until it meets a
  # truthy element, and what it pulled is gone: an iterator is a pull, so a
  # predicate over one cannot be free. For a source with no `false` in it
  # that is one element. The block form below reads as much as it has to
  # and no more. Said here because a method spelled like a question that
  # quietly takes elements is the kind of thing a caller finds out from the
  # answer to the *next* question.
  def any? : Bool
  def any?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  def chain(other : O) : ChainIterator(self, O, Elem | O::Elem) forall O : Iterator
  def compact_map(&func : (Elem -> U | ::Nil)) : CompactMapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U
  def count : Int32
  def count(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Int32
  def cycle(n : Int32) : CycleNIterator(self, Elem)
  def cycle : CycleIterator(self, Elem)
  def each(& : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  def each_cons(n : Int32) : ConsIterator(self, Elem)
  def each_slice(n : Int32) : SliceIterator(self, Elem)
  # Nil when nothing matched, which is what `Enumerable#find` and `Array#find`
  # answer: not finding is the ordinary outcome of a search, and a caller who
  # wants the panic writes `|| raise` as the prelude does. `first?`/`first`
  # below keeps its pair — an exhausted iterator has no first element, which
  # is a question with no answer.
  def find(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Elem | ::Nil
  def first(n : Int32) : TakeIterator(self, Elem)
  def first : Elem
  def first? : Elem | ::Nil
  def flat_map(&func : (Elem -> Array(U))) : FlatMapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U
  def map(&func : (Elem -> U)) : MapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U
  def max : Elem where Elem : Comparable
  # The largest, or nil when there is none. `max?`/`max` is a real pair:
  # an empty source has no largest element, so the plain name raising is
  # the common case. This file keeps the same pair for `first?`/`first`,
  # and answers `find` with nil, where not finding is the ordinary outcome.
  def max? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable
  def min : Elem where Elem : Comparable
  # And the same pair at the other end.
  def min? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable
  abstract def next : Elem | Stop
  def none?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  # Convenience constructor for arrays.
  def self.of(array : Array(T)) : ArrayIterator(T) forall T
  # An endless range counts up for as long as it is pulled, as the other
  # library's does: `Iterator.of((1..)).first(3).to_a` was accepted here
  # and then refused from inside `RangeIterator#next`, "expected argument
  # #1 to 'Int32#<' to be ... not Nil", a line of this file. A beginless
  # range has no first element to count from, and is refused at the call.
  def self.of(range : Range(B, Nil)) : EndlessRangeIterator(B) forall B
  def self.of(range : Range(Nil, E)) : Nil forall E
  def self.of(range : Range(B, E)) : RangeIterator(B, E) forall B, E
  def self.of_entries(hash : Hash(K, V)) : EntryIterator(K, V) forall K, V
  def self.of_keys(hash : Hash(K, V)) : KeyIterator(K, V) forall K, V
  def self.of_values(hash : Hash(K, V)) : ValueIterator(K, V) forall K, V
  def product : Elem where Elem : Num
  def reduce(initial : U, & : (U, Elem -> U)) : U forall U
  def reduce?(& : (Elem, Elem -> Elem)) : Elem | ::Nil
  def reject(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : RejectIterator(self, Elem)
  def select(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : SelectIterator(self, Elem)
  def size : Int32
  def skip(n : Int32) : SkipIterator(self, Elem)
  def skip_while(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : SkipWhileIterator(self, Elem)
  def step(n : Int32) : StepIterator(self, Elem)
  def sum : Elem where Elem : Num
  def take(n : Int32) : TakeIterator(self, Elem)
  def take_while(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : TakeWhileIterator(self, Elem)
  def to_a : Array(Elem)
  def with_index(offset : Int32 = 0) : WithIndexIterator(self, Elem)
  def with_index(offset : Int32 = 0, & : (Elem, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Bounded, as `Enumerable#zip` is (SPEC.md II.6 finding 6). Unbounded, a
  # zip with an array was refused from inside this file, "undefined
  # constant O::Elem" at the line below, and a chain with one from
  # `ChainIterator#next`; with `forall O : Iterator` the refusal names the
  # caller's line, the argument's type and `O`. A chain of two element
  # types yields either, as the other library's does: it was a return-type
  # error inside `ChainIterator`.
  def zip(other : O) : ZipIterator(self, Elem, O, O::Elem) forall O : Iterator
end

# The three views of a hash, in insertion order. Each takes its snapshot of
# the hash once, when built — `Hash#keys` and `Hash#values` allocate a fresh
# array per call, so asking per element was a copy of the table per step —
# and then walks that snapshot, so a hash that changes under the iterator
# does not change what it yields.
pub class KeyIterator(K, V)
  def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V))
  def next : K | Stop
end

pub struct MapIterator(I, T, U)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> U))
  def next : U | Stop
end

# Counts up by one from the range's beginning, the way the prelude's
# `Range#each` does, and stops at the end rather than stepping past it:
# on an inclusive range whose end is the type's largest value, the step
# after the last element would overflow.
pub class RangeIterator(B, E)
  def initialize(range : Range(B, E))
  def next : B | Stop
end

pub struct RejectIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct SelectIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class SkipIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class SkipWhileIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct SliceIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : Array(T) | Stop
end

pub class StepIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, by : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct Stop
  def initialize
end

pub class TakeIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class TakeWhileIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class ValueIterator(K, V)
  def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V))
  def next : V | Stop
end

pub class WithIndexIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, offset : Int32)
  def next : Tuple(T, Int32) | Stop
end

pub struct ZipIterator(I1, T1, I2, T2)
  def initialize(iter1 : I1, iter2 : I2)
  # Asks the second source only when the first has an element. Asking both
  # took one from the second each time the first had run out: after
  # `a.zip(b).to_a` with `a` = [1] and `b` = [10, 20, 30], `b.next`
  # answered 30 where the other library and Python's `zip` answer 20.
  def next : Tuple(T1, T2) | Stop
end

impl Iterator for EndlessRangeIterator(B) forall B
end

impl Iterator for ArrayIterator(T) forall T
end

impl Iterator for RangeIterator(B, E) forall B, E
end

impl Iterator for KeyIterator(K, V) forall K, V
end

impl Iterator for ValueIterator(K, V) forall K, V
end

impl Iterator for EntryIterator(K, V) forall K, V
end

impl Iterator for MapIterator(I, T, U) forall I, T, U
end

impl Iterator for SelectIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for RejectIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for TakeIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for TakeWhileIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for SkipIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for SkipWhileIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for ZipIterator(I1, T1, I2, T2) forall I1, T1, I2, T2
end

impl Iterator for ChainIterator(I1, I2, T) forall I1, I2, T
end

impl Iterator for FlatMapIterator(I, T, U) forall I, T, U
end

impl Iterator for SliceIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for ConsIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for WithIndexIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for CycleIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for CycleNIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for StepIterator(I, T) forall I, T
end

impl Iterator for CompactMapIterator(I, T, U) forall I, T, U
end

modules.surface:
module std/json

# `derive serializable`, in a struct or class whose fields are written with
# their types: the type reads and writes itself as a JSON object, a key per
# field, named as the field is.
#
#     pub struct Coord
#       getter x : Float64
#       @[JSON::Field(key: "label")]
#       getter name : String
#       derive serializable
#     end
#
#     Coord.from_json(%({"x": 1.5, "label": "a"})).x   # => 1.5
#     coord.to_json                                    # => {"x":1.5,"label":"a"}
#
# A field's value is read and written as `JSON.read_value` and
# `JSON.write_value` read and write its type: the built-in values, an enum,
# an `Array` or `Hash(String, V)` of them, an `Any`, another serializable
# type. A key the type has no field for is passed over; a field with no
# key keeps its default when it is written with one, as does a field with
# a default whose key holds `null` where its type does not admit nil; a
# field with neither is refused by name unless its type admits `nil`,
# which it then holds. `@[JSON::Field(...)]` renames a field, leaves it
# out either way, leaves a nil one out, or reads and writes it through a
# converter (see `JSON::Field`). It is what the other library's `include
# JSON::Serializable` writes, and the derive runs once, in the type's own
# module (SPEC.md II.4), so a consumer calls the methods without the macro.
#
# Each field's options are read off the type when its methods are compiled,
# in one `begin` so what a field's annotation says is known to every line
# after it; and refused there, with the field named, when they do not make
# sense.
pub macro serializable(declaration)

# One JSON value of any kind, the result of `JSON.parse`. The `as_x` methods
# panic when the value is of another kind; the `as_x?` ones answer `nil`.
pub struct Any
  alias Type = Nil | Bool | Int64 | Float64 | String | Array(Any) | Hash(String, Any)
  # Equal when the values are: an integer equals the float with the same
  # value, arrays element by element, objects key by key in any order.
  def ==(other : Any) : Bool
  def [](index : Int32) : Any
  def [](key : String) : Any
  def []?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def []?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def as_a : Array(Any)
  def as_a? : Array(Any) | ::Nil
  def as_bool : Bool
  def as_bool? : Bool | ::Nil
  # A float, or an integer read as one.
  def as_f : Float64
  def as_f? : Float64 | ::Nil
  def as_h : Hash(String, Any)
  def as_h? : Hash(String, Any) | ::Nil
  def as_i : Int32
  def as_i64 : Int64
  def as_i64? : Int64 | ::Nil
  def as_i? : Int32 | ::Nil
  def as_nil : Nil
  def as_s : String
  def as_s? : String | ::Nil
  def dig(key : String) : Any
  def dig(index : Int32) : Any
  def dig(k : String, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig(idx : Int32, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(k : String, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(idx : Int32, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  protected def float_value? : Float64 | ::Nil
  # Consistent with `==`: a whole float hashes as the integer it equals, an
  # object's hash does not depend on the order its keys were written in.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(raw : Type)
  def inspect : String
  # The kind of value this is, in the word a refusal uses: `null`, `bool`,
  # `integer`, `float`, `string`, `array` or `object`.
  def kind : String
  def self.new(val : Int32) : Any
  def raw : Type
  # How many elements an array or an object holds. A scalar has no size.
  def size : Int32
  def size? : Int32 | ::Nil
  def to_ascii_json : String
  def to_json : String
  def to_pretty_json(indent : String = "  ") : String
  # A string as itself and null as nothing, as `YAML::Any#to_s` and the
  # other library answer them; a number, a boolean or a collection as its
  # JSON text. A string was its JSON text too, so `"hello #{doc["name"]}"`
  # printed `hello "Ada"`, and null printed `null`.
  def to_s : String
end

# Writes a document one value at a time. `indent=` makes it pretty;
# `ascii_only=` escapes every non-ASCII code point.
pub class Builder
  def array(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  def ascii_only : Bool
  def ascii_only=(value : Bool) : Bool
  def bool(val : Bool) : Nil
  # Whether no value has been written yet.
  def empty? : Bool
  def end_array : Nil
  def end_object : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Any) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : String) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Int32) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Int64) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Float64) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Bool) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Nil) : Nil
  # A key; the value that follows it is written by the next call. A key
  # whose text is one this object already holds is refused, naming both:
  # the reader refuses a duplicate key, and the builder wrote one - a key
  # given twice, or two Strings whose bytes are not UTF-8 and are both
  # written as U+FFFD (`{"a\xFF" => 1, "a\xFE" => 2}` was written
  # `{"a\uFFFD":1,"a\uFFFD":2}`, and `JSON.parse` refused it).
  def field(name : String) : Nil
  def field(name : String, & : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  def indent=(spaces : Int32) : Nil
  def indent=(str : String) : Nil
  def initialize
  def max_nesting : Int32
  def max_nesting=(value : Int32) : Int32
  def null : Nil
  def number(val : Int32) : Nil
  def number(val : Int64) : Nil
  def number(val : UInt8) : Nil
  def number(val : UInt64) : Nil
  def number(val : Float64) : Nil
  def object(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  # Text written as it is: the caller's own JSON.
  def raw(str : String) : Nil
  def start_array : Nil
  def start_object : Nil
  def string(val : String) : Nil
  # The document's text. A container still open or no value written at all
  # is not a document, and is refused.
  def to_s : String
end

pub struct JSON
  # How `derive serializable` writes and reads one field, the other
  # library's `JSON::Field`:
  #
  #     @[JSON::Field(key: "userName")]
  #     getter user_name : String
  #
  # * `key:` the object key, where it is not the field's own name;
  # * `ignore: true` neither written nor read, `ignore_serialize: true` not
  #   written, `ignore_deserialize: true` not read - a field that is not
  #   read keeps its default, or is nil, and needs one or the other;
  # * `emit_null: false` a nil field left out of the object. A nil field is
  #   written as `null` otherwise, where the other library leaves it out
  #   unless asked;
  # * `converter:` a type whose `self.to_json(value, json : Builder)` writes
  #   the field and `self.from_json(pull : PullParser)` reads it.
  #
  # An option it does not know, a key that is not a string, and two fields
  # written under one key are refused when the type is compiled.
  annotation Field
  end
  # Text written through a `Builder` the block is handed. `indent` is a
  # count of spaces or the string one level is indented by. A block that
  # writes no value, or leaves a container open, is refused.
  def self.build(indent : String | Int32 | Nil = nil, & : (Builder -> Nil)) : String
  # The document read into `type`: `Nil`, `Bool`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt8`,
  # `UInt64`, `Float64`, `String`, `Any`, a type with `derive serializable`,
  # one of those or `nil`, or an `Array` or `Hash(String, V)` of those. An
  # integer outside the type is refused, as is anything after the root
  # value.
  def self.from_json(str : String, type : T.class) : T forall T
  def initialize
  # The document as an `Any`; panics with the line and column of the first
  # thing it refuses.
  def self.parse(input : String) : Any
  # The document as an `Any`, or `nil` when it is not one.
  def self.parse?(input : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Nil.class) : Nil
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Bool.class) : Bool
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Int32.class) : Int32
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Int64.class) : Int64
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : UInt8.class) : UInt8
  # An integer past Int64 reaches the reader as a float that still carries
  # its digits; those are read here, so the whole UInt64 range comes back.
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : UInt64.class) : UInt64
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Float64.class) : Float64
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : String.class) : String
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Any.class) : Any
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Array(T).class) : Array(T) forall T
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Hash(String, V).class) : Hash(String, V) forall V
  # A type that reads itself: the `initialize(pull)` a `derive
  # serializable` wrote. A type that admits nil reads `null` as the nil and
  # anything else as the other type (`x || raise`, as the derive asks it),
  # the way `write_or_null` writes it. That was `T.new(pull)` too, and
  # `Int32 | Nil` has no such `new`, so `JSON.from_json("5", Int32?)` and
  # `Array(Int32?)` did not build.
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : T.class) : T forall T
  # Any value `write_value` knows: `nil`, a `Bool`, a prelude integer, a
  # `Float64`, a `String`, an `Any`, an `Array` or `Hash` of those, or a type
  # that implements `ToJSON`; each of them or `nil`.
  def self.to_json(obj : T) : String forall T
  def self.write_value(val : Nil, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Bool, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Int32, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Int64, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : UInt8, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : UInt64, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Float64, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : String, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Any, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Array(T), b : Builder) : Nil forall T
  # A String key is written as it is, and two of them are never one text.
  def self.write_value(val : Hash(String, V), b : Builder) : Nil forall V
  # Any other key is written by its `to_s`, `nil` as `"null"`, the word a
  # JSON null is, so two keys can be one text: `{nil => 1, "null" => 2}`
  # was written `{"null":1,"null":2}`, which `JSON.parse` refuses
  # ("duplicate key 'null' at line 1, column 11"). The texts written are
  # kept, and a repeat is refused, naming both keys.
  def self.write_value(val : Hash(K, V), b : Builder) : Nil forall K, V
  # A `ToJSON` value writes itself. An enum member is written as the other
  # library writes one: its name underscored (`Color::DarkRed` is
  # `"dark_red"`), and a `@[Flags]` enum as the array of its members'
  # names; a value no member has is written as its number. Told apart here
  # and not by an overload restricted to `Enum`, which a program built
  # from this module's artifact read as a class and could not pass an enum
  # to.
  def self.write_value(val : T, b : Builder) : Nil forall T
end

# Reads a whole document into an `Any`. Like the lexer it records the first
# failure instead of panicking; `JSON.parse` and `JSON.parse?` decide what to
# do with it.
pub class Parser
  def error : String | ::Nil
  def initialize(input : String)
  def parse : Any
end

# Reads a document one event at a time: `kind` names what the reader is on,
# the `read_x` methods take it and move on. The grammar is checked as it is
# read, so a missing comma or colon is refused where it is, with a panic.
pub class PullParser
  enum Kind : Int32
    Null = 0
    Bool = 1
    Int = 2
    Float = 3
    String = 4
    BeginArray = 5
    EndArray = 6
    BeginObject = 7
    EndObject = 8
    EOF = 9
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `BeginArray`
    def begin_array? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `BeginObject`
    def begin_object? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Bool`
    def bool? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EndArray`
    def end_array? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EndObject`
    def end_object? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EOF`
    def eof? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Float`
    def float? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Int`
    def int? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Null`
    def null? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `String`
    def string? : ::Bool
  end
  def bool_value : Bool
  def column_number : Int32
  def float_value : Float64
  def initialize(input : String)
  def int_value : Int64
  def kind : Kind
  def line_number : Int32
  def max_nesting : Int32
  def max_nesting=(value : Int32) : Int32
  # Reads an object, yields once at the value of `key`, and skips the rest.
  def on_key(key : String, & : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  # The number the reader is on, as it was written.
  def raw_value : String
  # The value the reader is on, as an `Any`.
  def read_any : Any
  def read_array(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  def read_begin_array : Nil
  def read_begin_object : Nil
  def read_bool : Bool
  def read_end_array : Nil
  def read_end_object : Nil
  # A float, or an integer read as one.
  def read_float : Float64
  def read_int : Int64
  def read_next : Kind
  def read_null : Nil
  def read_null? : Bool
  # Yields each key of the object the reader is on, with the reader at its
  # value. A key named twice is refused, as `JSON.parse` refuses it.
  def read_object(& : (String -> Nil)) : Nil
  def read_object_key : String
  # The value the reader is on, written into `json` as it is read. A number
  # is written as its own text, the text it was read from: rebuilt from the
  # Int64 or Float64 it parsed to, `12345678901234567890` came back as
  # `1.2345678901234567e+19` and `1E+2` as `100.0`, and a UInt64 id passed
  # through here did not read back as itself.
  def read_raw(json : Builder) : Nil
  # The value the reader is on, as JSON text.
  def read_raw : String
  def read_string : String
  # Passes over the value the reader is on, whole.
  def skip : Nil
  def string_value : String
end

# A type that can write itself into a `Builder`. `JSON.to_json` accepts any
# value whose type implements it, as a `derive serializable` type does.
pub trait ToJSON
  abstract def to_json(json : Builder) : Nil
end

impl ToJSON for Any
  def to_json(json : Builder) : Nil
end

# Terminates the program with *status*, after writing *message* to
# standard error as a line, as `puts` writes one: a message that already
# ends in a newline gets no second one, as in the other library.

# The ending is `exit`'s, as the other library's `abort` is its `exit`:

# holds is written. This wrote through the runtime's own `__iyi_write` and
# ended with `__iyi_exit`, which skip both: `STDOUT.sync = false`,
# `puts "before"`, `abort "bye"` left standard output empty, a `defer`
# around the call never ran, and a line buffered on standard error before
# the message was lost.

modules.name: std/list
modules.surface:
module std/list

# The store is built at construction and never handed out, so no method of this
# type can be observed to change it. That is what makes the value shareable
# under III.4.4 — every field immutable after construction — and it is why the
# constructor **copies**.
#
# The copy is not defensive habit, it is the missing borrow checker. `List`
# cannot express "I own this array now", so a caller that kept a reference to
# what it passed in could mutate the list from underneath a task holding it.
# Rust says this with ownership and pays nothing; here it costs one copy at the
# boundary, once, and it is the honest price of not having that machinery.
pub struct List(T)
  # Two lists are the same value when they hold the same elements in the same
  # order, which is the whole of what a list is. Until this method, the one
  # answering was `Object#==` (src/iyi/object.iyi:37-39), the constant
  # `false` — not even reflexive, so `list == list` was false too, and every
  # collection that asks said no: `includes?`, `index` and `uniq` all go
  # through `==`, a list could never be found in a `Hash`, and a `case` over
  # a list matched no `when`, because a `when` is `===` and `===` is `==`.
  # That is the failure object.iyi:111-120 wrote up for `Tuple`, reproduced
  # by the one type III.4.7 added for handing a value between tasks — where
  # comparing what two tasks produced is the point.
  #
  # Sizes first, because that is the cheap half of the answer. No shared-store
  # fast path like `Slice#same?`: the constructor copies, so two lists never
  # share a store, and the comparison would pay for every call to fire only
  # when a list is compared with itself.
  #
  # Restricted to `List(T)`, so a list of another element type is unequal by
  # the prelude's default rather than a compile error — the reasoning
  # object.iyi:119-120 gives for restricting `Tuple#==` to its own shape.
  def ==(other : List(T)) : Bool
  # Indexed with `[]`, because every other sequence here is — `Slice`
  # (std/slice.iyi:107), the prelude's `Array` (src/iyi/array.iyi:78) and
  # everything under `Indexable` (std/indexable.iyi:75) — and III.1.7a says a
  # name shared with Crystal means the same thing here. A negative index
  # counts from the end, so `list[-1]` is the last element; that rule was
  # already true through the backing array and unwritten, which is worse than
  # either answer.
  #
  # The out-of-range sentence is raised here rather than left to the store.
  # The array's wording is the right wording — it names the index asked for
  # and how many elements there are, and names no receiver, so there is
  # nothing in it about an array the caller never handed over — but a message
  # this type promises is this file's, not one inherited by accident from a
  # field nobody can see.
  def [](index : Int32) : T
  # The nilable partner, which is the one question `[]` cannot answer: "the
  # element there, or nothing". Without it every caller probing a list past
  # its end rewrites the bounds rule above by hand against `size`, and two
  # copies of a rule is one too many.
  def []?(index : Int32) : T | ::Nil
  protected def adopt(items : Array(T)) : Nil
  # Every operation that would change a sequence returns a new one instead, so
  # by III.1.7's convention they are all participles. The plain verbs — `push`,
  # `sort`, `reverse` — name the mutating form, and this type has none. That the
  # naming rule falls out rather than being applied is the point of having
  # settled it before any library code existed.
  #
  # Each builds its array at the size it ends with, once. `dup` then `<<`
  # copied the list, grew the copy to twice its size and handed it to the
  # constructor, which copied it a third time: an append to a list of n
  # elements wrote 4n words where n + 1 is the whole of the work.
  def appended(item : T) : List(T)
  # `at` is the name this file had before `[]`, and samples/iyi/immutable.iyi
  # is written in it. It stays, spelled out, and delegates — so both names
  # exist but only one bounds rule does.
  def at(index : Int32) : T
  def concatenated(other : List(T)) : List(T)
  def empty? : Bool
  # Hashing follows equality, or the agreement above buys nothing: a `Hash`
  # finds a key by its slot first and compares second, so two equal lists in
  # different slots are still two keys. `Object#hash` answered with the type
  # id — every `List(Int32)` in one slot, "correct and useless" in exactly
  # the way object.iyi:20-23 says of a key type that never said how it
  # hashes.
  #
  # The array's own hash, which is `Indexable#hash`'s mixing (the prelude's
  # `Array#hash`): one function, so a list and the array it was built from
  # land in the same slot.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(items : Array(T))
  # Written down the same way it prints, because a list has no second form:
  # the elements inside it are already inspected. Stated rather than left to
  # `Object#inspect` so it is in this module's exported surface, which is
  # what a list nested in another collection is asked for — `List[List[1]]`
  # rather than a type name — and it is how `Slice` states it too.
  def inspect : String
  # A list over an array nothing else holds: the one `appended` or
  # `concatenated` has just built. The copy above is for a caller's array,
  # which the caller still has; one made here has no other owner.
  protected def self.owning(items : Array(T)) : List(T)
  def size : Int32
  # A list prints its elements, like both of its siblings: `Slice[10, 20, 30]`
  # and the array's `[10, 20, 30]`. Inherited, it printed
  # `Std::List::List(Int32)`, which object.iyi:7-8 calls what "a value that
  # has said nothing about itself can honestly print" — and a sequence has
  # plenty to say, so the default was the type failing to answer.
  #
  # The elements are *inspected* rather than printed, which is `Slice#to_s`'s
  # reasoning (std/slice.iyi:353-364): a list of strings reads back as
  # `List["pear", "fig"]`, telling a reader the elements are strings, where
  # printing them loses that with no way to get it back.
  def to_s : String
end

# And the lazy half, for the same reason `std/slice` has one: a `List` could
# only reach the iterator tower through `to_a`, which copies the sequence
# the type exists to hand around without copying.
#
# A class, as `ArrayIterator` is (std/iterator.iyi): an adaptor keeps its
# source by value, and this struct was copied into it, so
# `it.first(2).to_a` and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where
# an iterator over an array gives [1, 2] and [3, 4].
pub class ListIterator(T)
  def initialize(list : List(T))
  def next : T | Stop
end

impl Std::Enumerable::Enumerable for List(T) forall T
  def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
end

impl Std::Iterator::Iterator for ListIterator(T) forall T
end

modules.surface:
module std/log

# Entries written by a thread of their own, so a call that logs does not
# wait for the write: the entry is formatted where it is logged and
# queued, and a writer thread writes what has queued up since its last
# write, in order, in one write, to *io*'s descriptor.
#
#     AsyncBackend.open do |backend|   # closed, and drained, at the end
#       Log.setup(Severity::Info, backend)
#       ...
#     end
#
# `close` waits for every queued entry to be written and the thread to
# end; an entry written after it is refused. Entries queued when a program
# ends without `close` are lost, which the block form rules out. The
# backend is the thread that made it's, as every object not Share is.
#
# A thread needs the collector and a target with threads: under
# `-Dgc_none` or `-Dgc_boehm`, or on another target, `new` refuses.
pub class AsyncBackend < Backend
  def close : Nil
  def formatter : Formatter
  def formatter=(value : Formatter) : Formatter
  def initialize(io : IO = STDOUT, formatter : Formatter = DefaultFormatter.new)
  # A backend for the block, closed and drained when the block ends.
  def self.open(io : IO = STDOUT, formatter : Formatter = DefaultFormatter.new, &block : (AsyncBackend -> R)) : R forall R
  def write(entry : Entry) : Nil
end

pub abstract class Backend
  abstract def close : Nil
  abstract def write(entry : Entry) : Nil
end

pub class DefaultFormatter < Formatter
  def format(entry : Entry) : String
end

pub struct Entry
  # The task's context, the logger's bound data and the call's own, in
  # that order, a later key's value over an earlier's.
  def data : Hash(String, String)
  def initialize(source : String, severity : Severity, message : String, timestamp : Time = Time.utc, data : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String)
  def message : String
  def severity : Severity
  def source : String
  def timestamp : Time
end

pub abstract class Formatter
  def format(entry : Entry, io : IO) : Nil
  abstract def format(entry : Entry) : String
end

pub class IOBackend < Backend
  def close : Nil
  def formatter : Formatter
  def formatter=(value : Formatter) : Formatter
  def initialize(io : IO, formatter : Formatter = DefaultFormatter.new)
  def io : IO
  def write(entry : Entry) : Nil
end

# The root logger and the calls that go straight to it.
pub class Log
  def self.backend : Backend | ::Nil
  def self.backend=(backend : Backend | ::Nil) : Nil
  # The data this task's open contexts give an entry, the outermost first.
  def self.context : Hash(String, String)
  def self.debug(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.debug(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def self.error(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.error(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def self.fatal(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.fatal(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def self.for(source : String) : Logger
  def self.info(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.info(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def self.level : Severity
  def self.level=(level : Severity) : Nil
  def self.notice(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.notice(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def self.root : Logger
  # Reconfigures the root in place, so loggers obtained earlier follow.
  def self.setup(level : Severity = Severity::Info, backend : Backend = IOBackend.new(STDOUT)) : Logger
  # `setup`, the level read from *variable* - a severity's name, any case
  # - or *default_level* when it is unset or empty. A name that is no
  # severity is refused, the severities named.
  def self.setup_from_env(default_level : Severity = Severity::Info, backend : Backend = IOBackend.new(STDOUT), variable : String = "LOG_LEVEL") : Logger
  def self.trace(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.trace(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def self.warn(msg : String, **data) : Nil
  def self.warn(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  # Runs the block with *data* on every entry logged in this task and in
  # the tasks it starts, over the context already open, and answers the
  # block's answer. The context before it is back when the block ends,
  # panic or not.
  def self.with_context(**data, &block : (-> R)) : R forall R
end

pub class Logger
  # This logger's own backend, or the nearest ancestor's; nil silences.
  def backend : Backend | ::Nil
  def backend=(b : Backend | ::Nil) : Nil
  # A logger for the same source, its level and backend this one's, whose
  # entries all carry *data*: a request's id, a connection's peer.
  def bind(**data) : Logger
  # The data `bind` gave this logger and its parents, the root's first.
  protected def bound_into(found : Hash(String, String)) : Nil
  def debug(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def debug(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def debug? : Bool
  def error(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def error(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def error? : Bool
  def fatal(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def fatal(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def fatal? : Bool
  # The logger for *child_name* under this one, created on first ask;
  # `"a.b"` is the child `b` of the child `a`.
  def for(child_name : String) : Logger
  protected def get_or_create_child(name : String) : Logger
  def info(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def info(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def info? : Bool
  def initialize(source : String, level : Severity | ::Nil = nil, backend : Backend | ::Nil = nil, parent : Logger | ::Nil = nil, bound : Metadata | ::Nil = nil)
  # This logger's own level, or the nearest ancestor's; Info at a root
  # never given one.
  def level : Severity
  # nil hands the decision back to the parent.
  def level=(lvl : Severity | ::Nil) : Nil
  # None is a level and not a severity: an entry logged at None was
  # written by a logger set to None, the one level meant to write nothing.
  def log(severity : Severity, message : String, **data) : Nil
  def log(severity : Severity, **data, &block : (-> String)) : Nil
  def notice(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def notice(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def notice? : Bool
  def own_backend : Backend | ::Nil
  def own_level : Severity | ::Nil
  def source : String
  def trace(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def trace(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def trace? : Bool
  def warn(message : String, **data) : Nil
  def warn(**data, &b : (-> String)) : Nil
  def warn? : Bool
end

pub class MemoryBackend < Backend
  def clear : Nil
  def close : Nil
  def entries : Array(Entry)
  def formatter : Formatter
  def formatter=(value : Formatter) : Formatter
  def initialize(formatter : Formatter = DefaultFormatter.new)
  # The entries as the formatter would have written them.
  def output : Array(String)
  def write(entry : Entry) : Nil
end

# Keys and values, the newest first: immutable, so a task's context can sit
# in the table every thread reads.
pub class Metadata
  def initialize(key : String, value : String, rest : Metadata | ::Nil)
  def key : String
  # Into *into*, the oldest first, so a later key's value replaces an
  # earlier one's.
  def merge_into(into : Hash(String, String)) : Nil
  def rest : Metadata | ::Nil
  def to_h : Hash(String, String)
  def value : String
end

pub enum Severity : Int32
  Trace = 0
  Debug = 1
  Info = 2
  Notice = 3
  Warn = 4
  Error = 5
  Fatal = 6
  None = 7
  def <(other : Severity) : Bool
  def <=(other : Severity) : Bool
  def >(other : Severity) : Bool
  def >=(other : Severity) : Bool
  def label : String
  def self.parse(name : String) : Severity
  # The severity named by *name*, case-insensitively, or nil: what a
  # `LOG_LEVEL` variable holds.
  def self.parse?(name : String) : Severity | ::Nil
  def to_s : String
end
