module std/mail

pub struct Mail
  # A mailbox: an address and the name shown with it.
  class Address
    def ==(other : Address) : Bool
    # The addr-spec: the local part quoted where it is not a dot-atom.
    def address : String
    def domain : String
    # What `parse` makes, already read.
    def initialize(local : String, domain : String, name : String, read : Bool)
    # *address* is an addr-spec: `user@example.com`, or
    # `"john doe"@example.com` with its local part quoted. Anything else
    # is a panic, as is a name with a line break in it.
    def initialize(address : String, name : String = "")
    # The local part, unquoted, and the domain as written.
    def local : String
    # The display name, decoded; "" when there is none.
    def name : String
    # The one mailbox *text* holds.
    def self.parse(text : String) : Address | MailError
    # The mailboxes of an address list, a group's members in its place.
    def self.parse_list(text : String) : Array(Address) | MailError
    # As a person reads it: `Name <user@example.com>`, the name quoted
    # when it is not atoms, nothing encoded.
    def to_s : String
    # Whether the address is more than ASCII (RFC 6532), which only a
    # server that offers SMTPUTF8 takes.
    def utf8? : Bool
  end
  # A message to be written: its addresses, subject, date and identifier,
  # its text and HTML, and its attachments.
  class Message
    protected def self.addresses(name : String, list : Array(Address)) : String
    # A file sent with the message, under *filename*, as *content_type*:
    # the type its extension names (std/mime) when nil.
    def attach(filename : String, data : String, content_type : String | ::Nil = nil) : self
    protected def self.attachment(filename : String, kind : String, data : String) : MailEntity
    def bcc : Array(Address)
    def cc : Array(Address)
    def date : String | ::Nil
    # An RFC 5322 date-time - `Mail.date` writes one - refused when it is
    # not one.
    def date=(value : String) : String
    # `filename="..."` for a short name of printable ASCII; RFC 2231's
    # `filename*=utf-8''...` for any other, in continuations of whole
    # characters when it is longer - 50 encoded bytes in the first, after
    # its charset, and 60 in the rest, so each fits a line. All but the
    # last end in `;`.
    protected def self.filename_params(filename : String) : Array(String)
    def from : Address | ::Nil
    def from=(value : Address | ::Nil) : Address | ::Nil
    # A header of the caller's own, written as unstructured text. The
    # headers the message writes itself are refused here.
    def header(name : String, value : String) : self
    def html : String | ::Nil
    def html=(value : String) : String
    def initialize
    def message_id : String | ::Nil
    # `<left@right>`, the brackets added when they are not there.
    def message_id=(value : String) : String
    # The parts under one boundary, made from their own hash.
    protected def self.multipart(subtype : String, children : Array(MailEntity)) : MailEntity
    # Every address the message goes to - To, Cc and Bcc - once each.
    def recipients : Array(String)
    def reply_to : Array(Address)
    # ASCII without NUL, in lines of 78 or fewer.
    protected def self.seven_bit?(text : String) : Bool
    def subject : String | ::Nil
    def subject=(value : String) : String
    def text : String | ::Nil
    def text=(value : String) : String
    protected def self.text_part(subtype : String, text : String) : MailEntity
    def to : Array(Address)
    # The message, CRLF line breaks and all.
    def to_s : String
    # Whether an address in the message is RFC 6532's UTF-8.
    def utf8? : Bool
  end
  # A message or one of its parts, as read: its header fields unfolded and
  # in order, and its body - a multipart's parts, a `message/rfc822`'s
  # message, or bytes in a transfer encoding.
  class Part
    # The mailboxes of every field named *name* - `From`, `To`, `Cc` -
    # none when there is no such field.
    def addresses(name : String) : Array(Address) | MailError
    def attachment? : Bool
    # The parts whose disposition is `attachment`, in order.
    def attachments : Array(Part)
    # The bytes the body stands for, its transfer encoding undone.
    def body : String | MailError
    # The charset text is in: `us-ascii` when none is named (RFC 2045
    # section 5.2), in lower case.
    def charset : String
    # The disposition in lower case - `attachment`, `inline` - or nil.
    def disposition : String | ::Nil
    # The file name of Content-Disposition, or else Content-Type's `name`.
    def filename : String | ::Nil

pub class Mutex(T)
  protected def self.build(value : T) : Mutex(T)
  # The block's answer, worked out with the lock held. It must be `Share`,
  # because it leaves the lock.
  def get(&block : (T -> R)) : R | Cancelled forall R
  # Runs the block with the value, the lock held; answers nil, or
  # `Cancelled` when the task was cancelled while it waited.
  def lock(&block : (T -> _)) : Nil | Cancelled
  # Whether some task holds it now: an answer that may be old by the time
  # it is read, for a report rather than a decision.
  def locked? : Bool
  # The value is the block's: made here, so nothing outside holds it. The
  # constructor that takes a value is private for that reason.
  def self.new(&block : (-> U)) : Mutex(U) forall U
  protected def self.task_id : UInt64
  # Whether this thread has anything to run besides the waiting task:
  # tasks ready to run, tasks asleep, tasks waiting on I/O.
  protected def self.thread_busy? : Bool
  protected def self.thread_id : UInt64
  # The value replaced by the block's answer, with the lock held: what a
  # number or any other value type wants, which a block cannot change in
  # place.
  def update(&block : (T -> T)) : Nil | Cancelled
  # Runs the block with the lock held each time the value changes, until it
  # answers something other than nil, and answers that: a condition and
  # what is done once it holds, in one step no other task can come between.
  #
  #     queue = Mutex.new { [] of Int32 }
  #     job = queue.wait_for { |q| q.empty? ? nil : q.shift }.or_panic
  #
  # A change is any lock, get, update or wait_for of this Mutex by another
  # task; between them the waiter holds no lock, and what it does while it
  # waits is `lock`'s: yields, then sleeps a millisecond at a time, and on
  # Linux a thread with nothing else to run sleeps in the kernel until the
  # next release. Cancellable, as `lock` is. A wait nothing could end - one
  # thread, and nothing else on it to run - panics saying so.
  def wait_for(&block : (T -> R | ::Nil)) : R | Cancelled forall R
end

module std/password

# bcrypt, Provos and Mazières (USENIX 1999), as OpenBSD's `bcrypt.c`
# writes it and Crystal's `Crypto::Bcrypt::Password` reads it: a password
# hashed into a 60-character string that carries its own cost and salt,
#
#     $2b$11$ 22 characters of salt 31 characters of hash
#
# both in bcrypt's own base64 (`./A-Za-z0-9`, no padding). `hash` draws 16
# bytes of salt from `Random::Secure` and writes `$2b$`; `verify` reads
# `$2a$`, `$2b$` and `$2y$`, hashes the password again under the salt and
# cost it finds, and compares the two strings with
# `Subtle.constant_time_compare`, so how long a wrong guess takes does not
# say how much of it was right.
#
# The password is OpenBSD's key: its bytes up to the first NUL, cut to 72
# bytes, then a NUL, and only the first 72 bytes of that matter. So a
# password's 73rd byte onwards changes nothing, and neither does anything
# after a NUL: "a\0b" hashes as "a" does, which is what OpenBSD's C, with
# its `strlen`, does with it. OpenBSD's `$2a$` once counted the length in a
# byte and wrapped at 255 (the reason for `$2b$`); this reads `$2a$` as
# `$2b$`, so a `$2a$` hash that old code made of a password of 255 bytes or
# more does not verify here.
#
# *cost* is the log2 of the number of key-schedule passes: each one more
# doubles the time. 11 is Crystal's default and this one's; outside 4 to
# 31 `hash` panics with a sentence. A stored hash is data, and a malformed
# one, or one whose cost is outside 4 to 31, does not verify: `verify`
# answers false for it rather than ending the task.
pub struct Bcrypt
  def self.hash(password : String | Array(UInt8), cost : Int32 = 11) : String
  def initialize
  def self.verify(password : String | Array(UInt8), hash : String) : Bool
end

# scrypt, RFC 7914: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 spread into *p* blocks of `128 * r`
# bytes, each block walked through a table of *n* versions of itself
# (ROMix) by BlockMix, a chain of Salsa20/8 cores, and PBKDF2 once more
# over what comes out. The table is what makes it costly to guess at: a
# guess needs `128 * r * n` bytes of memory, or the time to recompute
# what it did not keep. RFC 7914's interactive-login figure is n = 16384,
# r = 8, p = 1, sixteen mebibytes.
#
# *max_memory* is a refusal, not a cap: the parameters ask for
# `128 * r * p + 128 * r * (n + 2)` bytes, which is how OpenSSL counts
# them, and past the limit the call panics rather than allocate. Its
# default, 32 MiB, is OpenSSL's and so Python's, so a call one library
# accepts the other accepts too. Refused with a sentence besides: an *n*
# that is not a power of two above 1, or not below 2^(16r) (RFC 7914 §2;
# OpenSSL refuses it too), an *r*, *p* or length below one, and a
# `128 * r * p` that does not fit an `Int32` (p * r of 2^24 and up).
pub struct Scrypt
  def self.derive(password : String | Array(UInt8), salt : String | Array(UInt8), n : Int32, r : Int32, p : Int32, length : Int32, max_memory : Int64 = 33554432_i64) : Array(UInt8)
  def initialize
end

module std/png

# Pixels, row after row from the top, each pixel's samples in `layout`
# order; a sample is one byte at depth 8, two (big-endian, as PNG stores
# them) at depth 16. `transparent`, for a Gray or RGB image, is the one
# color that is to be read as transparent (a gray value, or red, green and
# blue), in the image's own depth.
pub class Image
  def channels : Int32
  def self.channels_of(layout : Layout) : Int32
  def depth : Int32
  def height : Int32
  def initialize(width : Int32, height : Int32, layout : Layout, depth : Int32, samples : String, transparent : Array(Int32) | ::Nil = nil)
  def layout : Layout
  def self.layout_name(layout : Layout) : String
  # Sample *c* of the pixel at column *x*, row *y*: 0 to 255, or to 65535
  # at depth 16. Outside the image, a panic.
  def sample(x : Int32, y : Int32, c : Int32) : Int32
  def samples : String
  # Four bytes a pixel, red, green, blue and alpha. A gray sample is all
  # three colors; a pixel of the transparent color has alpha 0, any other
  # without an alpha sample 255; a 16-bit sample is its high byte.
  def to_rgba8 : String
  def transparent : Array(Int32) | ::Nil
  def width : Int32
end

# Which samples a pixel has, in the order they are stored.
pub enum Layout : Int32
  Gray = 0
  GrayAlpha = 1
  RGB = 2
  RGBA = 3
end

pub struct Png
  def self.assemble(width : Int32, height : Int32, depth : Int32, ctype : Int32, interlace : Bool, plte : String, trns : String, texts : Array(::Tuple(String, String)), filtered : String) : String
  def self.chunk(io : String::Builder, name : String, data : String) : Nil
  # The file in *data*, decoded; or what is wrong with it. A file whose
  # IHDR claims more than *max_pixels* pixels is refused before anything
  # is allocated for them.
  def self.decode(data : String, max_pixels : Int64 = MAX_PIXELS) : PngFile | PngError
  # *image* as a PNG file. *texts* are written as tEXt chunks, keyword
  # and text, or as iTXt where the text is not Latin-1.
  def self.encode(image : Image, interlace : Bool = false, texts : Array(::Tuple(String, String)) = [] of ::Tuple(String, String)) : String
  # A palette image: *indices* one byte a pixel, row after row, each an
  # entry of *palette*, whose entries are red, green, blue and alpha. The
  # bit depth is the smallest of 1, 2, 4 and 8 the palette fits; tRNS is
  # written up to the last entry that is not opaque.
  def self.encode_indexed(width : Int32, height : Int32, indices : String, palette : Array(::Tuple(Int32, Int32, Int32, Int32)), interlace : Bool = false, texts : Array(::Tuple(String, String)) = [] of ::Tuple(String, String)) : String
  # A zlib stream in a metadata chunk, inflated to at most MAX_METADATA.
  def self.inflate_metadata(stream : String, name : String) : String | PngError
  def initialize
  # The image data inflated into exactly the bytes IHDR promised, the
  # filters undone, and the pixels laid out.
  def self.pixels(d : PngDecode, data : String, idats : Array(::Tuple(Int32, Int32))) : Image | PngError
  # tEXt, zTXt or iTXt (sections 11.3.3.2-4).
  def self.read_text(name : String, p : Pointer(UInt8), body : Int32, len : Int32) : PngText | PngError
  # A keyword is 1 to 79 Latin-1 printable bytes, no space at either end
  # and no two together (section 11.3.3.2): anything else is a panic.
  def self.text_chunk(keyword : String, text : String) : ::Tuple(String, String)
end

# What is wrong with a PNG file: `message` names the chunk, and its offset
# in the file where that helps.
pub struct PngError
  def initialize(message : String)
  def to_s : String
end

# A decoded file: the image and what the file said about it.
pub class PngFile
  def bit_depth : Int32
  # IHDR's color type (0, 2, 3, 4 or 6) and bit depth, as written.
  def color_type : Int32
  # gAMA's value, the gamma times 100,000; nil without one.
  def gamma : Int32 | ::Nil
  # iCCP's profile name and the profile inflated; nil without one.
  def icc_name : String | ::Nil
  def icc_profile : String | ::Nil
  def image : Image
  def initialize(image : Image, color_type : Int32, bit_depth : Int32, interlaced : Bool, palette : String, transparency : String, gamma : Int32 | ::Nil, srgb_intent : Int32 | ::Nil, icc_name : String | ::Nil, icc_profile : String | ::Nil, texts : Array(PngText), skipped : Array(String))
  def interlaced : Bool
  # PLTE's entries, red, green and blue a byte each; "" without one.
  def palette : String
  # The ancillary chunks skipped, by name, in file order.
  def skipped : Array(String)
  # sRGB's rendering intent, 0 to 3; nil without one.
  def srgb_intent : Int32 | ::Nil
  def texts : Array(PngText)
  # tRNS as written: an alpha byte per palette entry, or the transparent
  # gray or RGB sample(s) as two bytes each; "" without one.
  def transparency : String
end

# A tEXt, zTXt or iTXt chunk: `chunk` says which. `language` and
# `translated_keyword` are iTXt's, "" for the other two.
pub class PngText
  def chunk : String
  def initialize(chunk : String, keyword : String, text : String, language : String = "", translated_keyword : String = "")
  def keyword : String
  def language : String
  def text : String
  def translated_keyword : String
end

impl Error for PngError
  def message : String
end

modules.surface:
module std/process

# The child's standard input, as a pipe this program writes.
pub class ChildInput
  # Closes the pipe: the child reads the end of its input.
  def close : Nil
  def initialize(child : ProcessChild)
  # Writes all of *text*, parking while the pipe is full. A child that
  # closed its input, or ended, is `ChildInputClosed`; `close` has made it
  # so too.
  def write(text : String) : Nil | ChildInputClosed | Cancelled
end

# A write to a child that had closed its input - or ended.
pub struct ChildInputClosed
  def initialize(pid : Int64)
  def pid : Int64
end

# One of the child's output streams, as a pipe this program reads. Each
# read parks until the child has written, or its end of the pipe closed.
pub class ChildOutput
  def initialize(child : ProcessChild, output : ::Bool)
  # What the child has written that this program has not read, up to
  # *max* bytes, once there is some: nil at the end.
  def read(max : Int32 = 65536) : String | ::Nil | Cancelled
  # Everything the child writes from here to its end.
  def read_all : String | Cancelled
  # The next line, without its `\n` (and a `\r` before it) unless *chomp*
  # is false; the last one need not end in one. nil at the end.
  def read_line(chomp : ::Bool = true) : String | ::Nil | Cancelled
end

# A child started by `Process.spawn`, running beside this program.
pub class ChildProcess
  # Whether the child has ended, without waiting; once it has, `status`
  # says how.
  def ended? : ::Bool
  def initialize(child : ProcessChild, input : ::Bool, output : ::Bool, error : ::Bool)
  # Ends the child: SIGKILL on Linux and darwin, and on Windows the child
  # and every program it started. Nothing once it has ended.
  def kill : Nil
  # The child's process id, which the operating system may give another
  # process once this one has ended and been waited for.
  def pid : Int64
  # Sends *number* to the child, Linux and darwin. Windows has no signals,
  # and a call there panics: `terminate` and `kill` are what it has.
  def signal(number : Int32) : Nil
  # How the child ended, once it has; nil while it runs.
  def status : ProcessStatus | ::Nil
  # The child's standard error, asked for as `Redirect::Pipe`.
  def stderr : ChildOutput
  # The child's standard input, asked for as `Redirect::Pipe`.
  def stdin : ChildInput
  # The child's standard output, asked for as `Redirect::Pipe`.
  def stdout : ChildOutput
  # Asks the child to stop: SIGTERM on Linux and darwin, which it may
  # handle. Windows has no request to stop a program, and ends it and what
  # it started, as `kill` does. Nothing once it has ended.
  def terminate : Nil
  # Parks until the child has ended and answers how; at once if it had.
  # Its input, if a pipe, is closed first: a child reading to the end of
  # its input would otherwise wait for this program while this program
  # waits for it.
  def wait : ProcessStatus | Cancelled
end

pub struct Process
  # Replaces this program with *command*, and answers only if it could not:
  # a `ProcessError`, with this program as it was, in the directory it was.
  #
  # On Linux and darwin the process becomes the program - the same pid,
  # this program's three standard streams and none of its other
  # descriptors (on Linux from 5.11, which marks them for the exec) - and
  # nothing after the call runs. Windows cannot replace a program: there
  # the program runs on this program's streams, this program waits for it
  # and ends with its exit code, and a pid is not kept.
  #
  # *command*, *args*, *chdir* and *env* are `run`'s. What this program had
  # written to its own buffered streams is flushed first.
  def self.exec(command : String, args : Array(String) = [] of String, chdir : String | ::Nil = nil, env : Hash(String, String) | Hash(String, String | ::Nil) | Hash(String, Nil) | Nil = nil) : ProcessError
  # This program's own executable, as a path; nil where the platform will
  # not say.
  def self.executable : String | ::Nil
  def initialize
  # This program's own process id.
  def self.pid : Int64
  # Runs *command* with *args* and answers once it has ended.
  #
  # *command* is a path, or a name looked for on `PATH` (on Windows also as
  # `NAME.exe` and `NAME.com`; a `.bat` or `.cmd` is refused). Each of
  # *args* reaches the child as one argument, and no shell reads them.
  # *input* is written to the child's standard input, and without it the
  # child reads nothing. *chdir* is the directory it runs in. *env* changes
  # the child's environment alone: a name given a value is set, a name
  # given `nil` removed. With *capture* false the child writes to this
  # program's own streams and the result's texts are empty.
  #
  # Answers a `ProcessResult` for a child that ran, whatever its exit code;
  # a `ProcessError` when it could not be started; and `Cancelled`, after
  # the child is ended, when the task running this is cancelled. Nothing
  # blocks the thread: the other tasks run while the child does.
  def self.run(command : String, args : Array(String) = [] of String, input : String | ::Nil = nil, chdir : String | ::Nil = nil, capture : ::Bool = true, env : Hash(String, String) | Hash(String, String | ::Nil) | Hash(String, Nil) | Nil = nil) : ProcessResult | ProcessError | Cancelled
  # Starts *command* and answers at once with the running child, which
  # this program then talks to and waits for: `ChildProcess`.
  #
  # *command*, *args*, *chdir* and *env* are `run`'s. Each of *input*,
  # *output* and *error* is a `Redirect`: `Pipe` to write the child's input
  # or read its output through the handle, `Inherit` to share this
  # program's own stream (which is flushed first), `Null` for the null
  # device. All three are inherited unless asked.
  #
  # Answers a `ProcessError` when the child could not be started.
  #
  # The child runs until it ends or is ended; `wait` collects its end and
  # is what a program owes every child it starts. A pipe nobody reads fills
  # and stops the child that writes it, so read what is asked for as a
  # pipe - on two tasks at once for both output and errors - before or
  # while waiting. A task cancelled in any of the handle's calls ends the
  # child before it answers `Cancelled`, as `run` does: a task that stops
  # leaves no program running.
  def self.spawn(command : String, args : Array(String) = [] of String, input : Redirect = Redirect::Inherit, output : Redirect = Redirect::Inherit, error : Redirect = Redirect::Inherit, chdir : String | ::Nil = nil, env : Hash(String, String) | Hash(String, String | ::Nil) | Hash(String, Nil) | Nil = nil) : ChildProcess | ProcessError
end

# A program that could not be started, and the platform's error number for
# why. `directory` is set when it was the directory it was to run in.
pub struct ProcessError
  def code : Int32
  def command : String
  def denied? : ::Bool
  def directory : String | ::Nil
  def initialize(command : String, code : Int32, directory : String | ::Nil = nil)
  # Nothing by that name: not on PATH, no such file, no such directory.
  def not_found? : ::Bool
  def reason : String
end

# What a program that ran came back with. `exit_code` is the child's own;
# on Linux and darwin a child ended by a signal has `signal` set and the
# exit code a shell would report for it, 128 plus the signal. On Windows
# `signal` is always 0 and a crash is its exception code, `0xC0000005` for
# an access violation, read as an Int32.
pub struct ProcessResult
  def exit_code : Int32
  def initialize(exit_code : Int32, signal : Int32, stdout : String, stderr : String)
  def signal : Int32
  def stderr : String
  def stdout : String
  def success? : ::Bool
end

# How a child ended: `exit_code`, and on Linux and darwin the `signal`
# that ended it, as `ProcessResult` says them.
pub struct ProcessStatus
  def exit_code : Int32
  def initialize(exit_code : Int32, signal : Int32)
  def signal : Int32
  def success? : ::Bool
end

# How one of a spawned child's standard streams is connected.
pub enum Redirect : Int32
  Pipe = 0
  Inherit = 1
  Null = 2
end

impl Error for ProcessError
  def message : String
end

impl Error for ChildInputClosed
  def message : String
end

modules.name: std/random
modules.surface:
module std/random

pub class Random
  # The operating system's randomness, for anything a guess must not reach:
  # tokens, keys, nonces, query IDs. It is a `Random`, so `rand(n)`,
  # `rand(range)`, `hex` and every other draw take their values from it, and
  # `Random::Secure.rand(n)` answers without an instance. There is no state to
  # seed: each draw is a fresh request to the kernel (or libSystem, or the
  # Windows or WASI host), and nothing is held between draws, so a `fork`
  # cannot hand the child the parent's next value.
  class Secure < ::Std::Random::Random
    # *count* bytes at *buffer*, every one from the platform's entropy source,
    # or a panic that says why there are none: a byte that only looks random
    # is never the answer.
    def self.fill(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Nil
    # The generator fields a `Random` carries, which nothing here reads.
    def initialize
    def next_u : UInt32
    # The whole buffer in one request rather than four bytes at a time.
    def random_bytes(buffer : Array(UInt8)) : Nil
  end
  # *n* random bytes in base64 with `+` `/` and `=` padding, no line breaks.
  def base64(n : Int32 = 16) : String
  def self.base64(n : Int32 = 16) : String
  # *n* random bytes as two lowercase hex digits each.
  def hex(n : Int32 = 16) : String
  def self.hex(n : Int32 = 16) : String
  # The stream came from the seed, and one seed was one stream: the other
  # library takes the stream apart from the seed, zero unless asked, and
  # the same seed gave two different sequences in the two libraries.
  def initialize(seed : UInt64, sequence : UInt64 = 0_u64)
  # Any integer seed and sequence, as the other library takes them. There
  # were two overloads, an `Int32` and an `Int64` seed with a `UInt64`
  # sequence, beside this class's own `UInt64` pair: `Random.new(7, 3)`,
  # the form the comment above writes, cast its literals to all three and
  # was an ambiguous call, and a `UInt32` seed matched none of them. A
  # negative seed or sequence panics in the conversion, as it raises there.
  def self.new(seed : ::Int, sequence : ::Int = 0_u64) : Random
  def self.new : Random
  def next_bool : Bool
  def self.next_bool : Bool
  # 2^53 values, the high draw first: two 32-bit draws make the integer,
  # and it is divided by 2^53 - 1, so both ends can come out.
  def next_float : Float64
  def next_u : UInt32
  # The same draws without a generator in hand, from one seeded the first
  # time it is asked, as the other library's `Random.rand` draws from its
  # default. `Random::Secure.rand(...)` and the rest are these, answered by
  # the operating system instead.
  def self.next_u : UInt32
  def rand(n : Int32) : Int32
  def rand(n : UInt32) : UInt32
  def rand(n : Int64) : Int64
  def rand(n : UInt64) : UInt64
  # In `[0, x)`: 2^53 evenly spaced values, scaled. Not `rand * x`, which
  # divides by 2^53 - 1 and can answer *x* itself.
  def rand(x : Float64) : Float64
  # The span is taken as the unsigned difference, so a range across zero
  # does not overflow on the way. The whole of `Int32` is one draw read as
  # an `Int32`, as the other library reads it, rather than added to the
  # bottom of the range, which would answer the same value with its top
  # bit turned over.
  def rand(range : Range(Int32, Int32)) : Int32
  # As the `Int32` range: the whole of `Int64` is 2^64 values, one more than
  # a `UInt64` span can count, and is two draws, high first, read as one.
  def rand(range : Range(Int64, Int64)) : Int64
  # An end left out is the other library's choice too: `rand(x)` cannot
  # reach *x*, and an inclusive range scales `rand`, which can.
  def rand(range : Range(Float64, Float64)) : Float64
  def rand : Float64
  def self.rand(n : Int32) : Int32
  def self.rand(n : UInt32) : UInt32
  def self.rand(n : Int64) : Int64
  def self.rand(n : UInt64) : UInt64
  def self.rand(x : Float64) : Float64
  def self.rand(range : Range(Int32, Int32)) : Int32
  def self.rand(range : Range(Int64, Int64)) : Int64
  def self.rand(range : Range(Float64, Float64)) : Float64
  def self.rand : Float64
  # Four bytes a draw, low byte first, the last draw cut short: a seeded
  # generator fills a buffer with the other library's bytes.
  #
  # The bytes are an `Array(UInt8)`, as `UUID#bytes` and std/digest's
  # `hash_bytes` are, rather than the other library's `Bytes`: std/slice
  # reaches this module through std/indexable's `sample`, and an import
  # back would be a cycle.
  def random_bytes(buffer : Array(UInt8)) : Nil
  def random_bytes(n : Int32 = 16) : Array(UInt8)
  def self.random_bytes(buffer : Array(UInt8)) : Nil
  def self.random_bytes(n : Int32 = 16) : Array(UInt8)
  # The bytes as a String, which is how std/base64 takes them.
  protected def self.text_of(bytes : Array(UInt8)) : String
  # *n* random bytes in the URL-safe alphabet, `-` and `_`; unpadded unless
  # asked, as the other library answers it, since a token in a URL or a
  # file name has no use for the `=`.
  def urlsafe_base64(n : Int32 = 16, padding : Bool = false) : String
  def self.urlsafe_base64(n : Int32 = 16, padding : Bool = false) : String
end

class ::Array(T)
  def sample(random : Std::Random::Random | ::Nil = nil) : T
  # *n* distinct elements. One is `sample` in a list; more are a reservoir
  # (each element past the first *n* replaces a slot with probability
  # n/(i+1)) shuffled at the end - both as the other library does it.
  def sample(n : Int32, random : Std::Random::Random | ::Nil = nil) : Array(T)
  def shuffle(random : Std::Random::Random | ::Nil = nil) : Array(T)
  # Fisher-Yates from the back, `rand(i + 1)` a step: the other library's
  # `shuffle!`, so a seeded generator puts the elements where it would.
  def shuffle_in_place(random : Std::Random::Random | ::Nil = nil) : Array(T)
end

struct ::StaticArray(T, N)
  def initialize
  # `Array#shuffle_in_place` for the array that holds its elements inline:
  # the other library's `StaticArray#shuffle!`, the same draws in the same
  # order, so a seeded generator puts the elements where it would. Its
  # sample of noise does exactly this to a 256-entry permutation table.
  def shuffle_in_place(random : Std::Random::Random | ::Nil = nil) : self
end

modules.name: std/reference_storage
modules.surface:
module std/reference_storage

pub struct ReferenceStorage(T) < Value
  # Field-wise, with class fields compared by identity. `T#==` on a
  # `String` field follows the pointer, so uninitialized storage died of
  # a memory fault; two storages with equal string contents at different
  # addresses compared equal while `hash` mixed the pointer bytes. Whole-
  # blob compare is also wrong: `other` is passed by value and padding
  # bytes are not copied, so two constructed `Node`s compared unequal.
  def ==(other : ReferenceStorage(T)) : Bool
  def ==(other : Object) : Bool
  # Field by field, exactly as `==` compares: a class field by its
  # identity, any other by its own `hash`, mixed with a wrapping step
  # (checked `h * 31` panicked once `instance_sizeof(T)` passed a few
  # bytes). Mixing the raw bytes disagreed with `==`: a `Float64` field
  # holding `0.0` and one holding `-0.0` compare equal and differ in their
  # sign bit, and a `String?` field compares by content while its bytes
  # are the pointer, so equal storages hashed apart.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize
  def inspect : String
  def to_reference : T
  def to_s : String
end

class ::Reference
  def self.pre_initialize(address : Pointer)
  def self.unsafe_construct(address : Pointer, *args, **opts) : self
end

modules.name: std/regex
modules.surface:
module std/regex

pub struct Regex
  # One match: the text it was found in and where each group began and
  # ended, in bytes. A group that took no part in the match - the second
  # of `(a)|(b)` when `a` matched, `(x)?` when `x` did not - has no span,
  # and `[]?` answers nil for it.
  class MatchData
    # The text group *n* matched. A group the pattern does not have, or one
    # that took no part in this match, is a mistake the program made, and
    # it panics with the reason.
    def [](n : Int32) : String
    # The text the group called *name* matched; a name the pattern does not
    # have, or a group that took no part, panics with the reason.
    def [](name : String) : String
    # The text group *n* matched, or nil for a group that took no part or
    # that the pattern does not have.
    def []?(n : Int32) : String | ::Nil
    # The text the group called *name* matched, or nil for a group that
    # took no part or a name the pattern does not have.
    def []?(name : String) : String | ::Nil
    # Where group *n* begins, in characters, as the other library counts:
    # `"クリスタル".match(/リ(ス)/).begin(0)` is 1 where `byte_begin` is 3.
    def begin(n : Int32 = 0) : Int32
    # Where group *n* begins, in bytes: what `String#[]` and `index` count
    # in. A negative *n* counts from the last group.
    def byte_begin(n : Int32 = 0) : Int32
    # Where group *n* ends, in bytes.
    def byte_end(n : Int32 = 0) : Int32
    # What each unnamed group matched, in order, nil for one that took no
    # part; the named ones are `named_captures`, as in the other library.
    def captures : Array(String | ::Nil)
    # Where group *n* ends, in characters.
    def end(n : Int32 = 0) : Int32
    # *replacement* with its references filled from this match: `\0` to
    # `\9` are groups, `\k<name>` a named one, `\\` one backslash, and any
    # other `\` is itself - how the other library reads the replacement
    # `String#sub` and `gsub` are given. A group that took no part is
    # empty; a name the pattern does not have panics.
    def expand(replacement : String) : String
    # How many capture groups the pattern has, the whole match not counted.
    def group_size : Int32
    def initialize(regex : Regex, string : String, slots : Array(Int32))
    # `Regex::MatchData("ab" 1:"a" name:"b")`, as the other library writes it.
    def inspect : String
    # What each named group matched, nil for one that took no part.
    def named_captures : Hash(String, String | ::Nil)
    # The text after the match.
    def post_match : String
    # The text before the match.
    def pre_match : String
    # The pattern that matched.
    def regex : Regex
    # How many groups there are, the whole match counted: `(a)(b)` is 3.
    def size : Int32
    # The text the match was found in.
    def string : String
    # Every group, the whole match first.
    def to_a : Array(String | ::Nil)
    # The text the whole pattern matched.
    def to_s : String
  end
  # The flags a whole pattern is compiled with, combined with `|`. The
  # numbers are the other library's, which is what lets a literal's flags
  # (`/a/i`, `/a/mx`) reach this type unchanged.
  enum Options : Int32
    IGNORE_CASE = 1
    MULTILINE = 6
    DOTALL = 2
    MULTILINE_ONLY = 4
    EXTENDED = 8
  end
  # The same pattern with the same flags.
  def ==(other : Regex) : Bool
  # Whether the pattern occurs anywhere in *text*: what `case text when
  # /x/` asks.
  def ===(text : String) : Bool
  # Where the first match begins, in bytes, or nil. It sets nothing: the
  # other library's `=~` also fills `$~`, which iyi does not have, and a
  # program that wants the groups asks `match`.
  def =~(text : String) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Where the first match at or after byte *offset* begins, in bytes, as
  # `String#byte_index` answers for a string.
  def byte_index(text : String, offset : Int32 = 0) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # How many capture groups the pattern has.
  def capture_count : Int32
  # The machine is compiled first either way: it is what refuses a pattern
  # this engine does not take, and the fast paths only ever see one it did.
  # They read the pattern's text as written, so a pattern with flags, which

  # finds them.

  # nothing else - with `x` too, whose whitespace and `#` are escaped.

  def group_index(name : String) : Int32 | ::Nil

  def inspect : String

  # *pos* counts from the end. `^` and `\A` still mean the start of the

  # `String#matches?` here.

  # `\A` mean its start, not *pos*, and `\b` sees the byte before *pos*.

  def match_at(text : String, pos : Int32) : MatchData | ::Nil

  def name_table : Hash(Int32, String)
  # The other library's name for `compile`.
  def self.new(pattern : String, options : Options = Options::None) : Regex
  # The flags the pattern was compiled with; inline ones are the
  # pattern's own text and are not here.
  def options : Options

  # sequence with a million matches each did not finish. The replacement
  # is taken as written; `String#gsub` is the one that reads `\1` in it.

  # replacement cannot say.
  def replace(text : String, & : (String -> String)) : String

  # literal was compiled from, for a program that prints its patterns.

module std/router

# A route's pattern, `[METHOD ][HOST]/[PATH]`, parsed: what `Router#handle`
# registers. `match` reads a request path's wildcards; `relation` and
# `conflict` are the comparisons that decide precedence and refuse two
# patterns neither of which is more specific.
pub class Pattern
  # Two relations of parts (methods, then each segment) as the relation
  # of the whole: a superset in one part and a subset in another is
  # neither, an overlap.
  def self.combine(first : Int32, second : Int32) : Int32
  # The sentence refusing this pattern beside *other*, nil when the two
  # can be registered together: when they have the same host and match
  # the same requests, or some requests in common with neither more
  # specific. It names both and a request both match.
  def conflict(other : Pattern) : String | ::Nil
  # Whether this pattern matched *pieces* without its trailing wildcard
  # taking anything: `/x/` on `/x/`, not on `/x/y`. What decides whether
  # `/x` is redirected to `/x/`.
  def exact?(pieces : Array(String)) : Bool
  def host : String
  # A wildcard's name: an ASCII letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `_`.
  def self.identifier?(name : String) : Bool
  def initialize(text : String, method : String, host : String, kinds : Array(Int32), names : Array(String))
  protected def kinds : Array(Int32)
  # The wildcards' values when *path* - a request path, rooted and clean,
  # still percent-encoded - matches this pattern's path; nil when it does
  # not. The method and host are not looked at.
  def match(path : String) : Hash(String, String) | ::Nil
  # `match` on a path already cut into `pieces`.
  def match_pieces(pieces : Array(String)) : Hash(String, String) | ::Nil
  # Whether a request of *method* is one this pattern's method takes.
  def matches_method?(method : String) : Bool
  def method : String
  # Whether this pattern matches a strict subset of *other*'s requests,
  # methods and paths together; hosts are not compared.
  def more_specific?(other : Pattern) : Bool
  protected def names : Array(String)
  # *text* read as a pattern, or why it is not one: an invalid method, no
  # `/` to start the path, a `{` in the host, a path a request's cleaned
  # path never equals (`//`, `.`, `..`), a wildcard that is not a whole
  # segment, `{$}` or `{name...}` before the end, a name that is not an
  # identifier or is used twice, a malformed percent escape.
  def self.parse(text : String) : Pattern | RouterError
  # *path*'s segments after its first `/`, each percent-decoded: `/` is
  # one empty piece, and a trailing slash is a last empty one. Nil for a
  # path that is not rooted or holds a malformed escape. Decoded a segment
  # at a time, so `%2F` is inside a segment, never between two.
  def self.pieces(path : String) : Array(String) | ::Nil
  # How this pattern's requests relate to *other*'s, methods and paths
  # together: `EQUIVALENT`, `MORE_GENERAL`, `MORE_SPECIFIC`, `DISJOINT` or
  # `OVERLAPS`.
  def relation(other : Pattern) : Int32
  # The pattern as it was written.
  def to_s : String
end

# Requests sent to handlers by pattern, Go 1.22's `ServeMux`:
#
#     router = Router.new
#     router.handle("GET /users/{id}") { |req, params| Response.new(200, params["id"]) }
#     router.handle("/static/") { |req, params| FileServer.serve(root, req) }
#     Server.serve(listener) { |req| router.call(req) }
#
# `handle` panics on a pattern that is not one, on one that conflicts with
# a pattern already registered, and after the router has answered a
# request. `call` answers with the most specific pattern's handler, or a
# 301 (to the cleaned path, or to a subtree's `/`), a 405 with `Allow`, a
# 400 for a malformed escape, a 404.
pub class Router
  # The answer to *req*: its handler's, or the router's own 301, 400, 404
  # or 405.
  def call(req : Request) : Response
  # *path* - rooted - with `.` and empty segments dropped and `..` taking
  # the one before it off, its trailing slash kept: Go's `cleanPath`.
  def self.clean(path : String) : String
  # Sends the requests *pattern* matches to the block, with the request
  # and the wildcards' values by name.
  def handle(pattern : String, &handler : (Request, Hash(String, String) -> Response)) : Nil
  # A `Host` value without its port, as Go's `stripHostPort` has it: an
  # IPv6 address in brackets loses the brackets with the port.
  def self.host_of(value : String) : String
  def initialize
  # The patterns registered, in the order they were.
  def patterns : Array(Pattern)
  def self.plain(status : Int32, text : String) : Response
  def self.redirect(path : String, query : String | ::Nil) : Response
end

# Why a pattern is refused: `Pattern.parse`'s answer for text that is not
# a pattern. `Router#handle` panics with its `message`.
pub struct RouterError
  def initialize(reason : String)
  def reason : String
  def to_s : String
end

impl Error for RouterError
  def message : String
end

pub enum RsaHash : Int32
  SHA1 = 0
  SHA256 = 1
  SHA384 = 2
  SHA512 = 3
  def digest(data : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  # The DER of a DigestInfo up to the digest itself (RFC 8017 section 9.2,
  # note 1): the algorithm's OID with NULL parameters, then the OCTET
  # STRING's header.

end

# An RSA private key with its CRT parameters (RFC 8017 section 3.2, the
# first representation and the second together), which signs.
pub struct RsaPrivateKey
  # The modulus's length in bits, and in bytes: a signature's length.
  def bits : Int32
  # The one key in a PEM text: an `RSA PRIVATE KEY` block (PKCS #1) or a
  # `PRIVATE KEY` block (PKCS #8).
  def self.from_pem(text : String) : RsaPrivateKey | RsaError
  # An RSAPrivateKey (appendix A.1.2) of two primes: version 0 and the
  # eight numbers.
  def self.from_pkcs1(der : Array(UInt8)) : RsaPrivateKey | RsaError
  # A PKCS #8 PrivateKeyInfo or OneAsymmetricKey (RFC 5958) naming
  # rsaEncryption, its privateKey an RSAPrivateKey. Attributes are passed
  # over; a public key, which version 1 may carry, must be the key's own.
  def self.from_pkcs8(der : Array(UInt8)) : RsaPrivateKey | RsaError
  def initialize(public_key : RsaPublicKey, p : BigInt, q : BigInt, dp : BigInt, dq : BigInt, qi : BigInt, prf : Array(UInt8))
  # The key from its eight numbers, each big-endian - n, e, d, p, q, dp,
  # dq, qi - or why they are not one.
  def self.new(modulus : Array(UInt8), exponent : Array(UInt8), d : Array(UInt8), p : Array(UInt8), q : Array(UInt8), dp : Array(UInt8), dq : Array(UInt8), qi : Array(UInt8)) : RsaPrivateKey | RsaError
  def public_key : RsaPublicKey
  # RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 (section 8.2.1) of *message* under *hash*: 0x00
  # 0x01, the 0xFF padding, 0x00, the hash's DigestInfo and the digest.
  def sign_pkcs1v15(hash : RsaHash, message : Array(UInt8) | String) : Array(UInt8)
  # RSASSA-PSS (section 8.1.1) of *message* under *hash*, MGF1 over the
  # same hash: EMSA-PSS-ENCODE (section 9.1.1) with a salt as long as the
  # digest, drawn as the module's header says.
  def sign_pss(hash : RsaHash, message : Array(UInt8) | String) : Array(UInt8)
  def size : Int32
end

pub struct RsaPublicKey
  # The modulus's length in bits, and in bytes: a signature's length.
  def bits : Int32
  def exponent : BigInt
  # An RSAPublicKey (RFC 8017 appendix A.1.1): SEQUENCE { modulus, exponent }.
  def self.from_pkcs1(der : Array(UInt8)) : RsaPublicKey | RsaError
  # A SubjectPublicKeyInfo (RFC 5280 section 4.1.2.7) naming rsaEncryption.
  def self.from_spki(der : Array(UInt8)) : RsaPublicKey | RsaError
  def self.from_spki(value : DerValue) : RsaPublicKey | RsaError
  def initialize(modulus : BigInt, exponent : BigInt, bits : Int32)
  def modulus : BigInt
  # The key from a modulus and an exponent, each big-endian.
  def self.new(modulus : Array(UInt8), exponent : Array(UInt8)) : RsaPublicKey | RsaError
  def size : Int32
  # Whether *signature* is the PKCS #1 v1.5 signature (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5,
  # section 8.2.2) of *message* under *hash*.
  def verify_pkcs1v15(hash : RsaHash, message : Array(UInt8) | String, signature : Array(UInt8)) : Bool
  # Whether *signature* is an RSASSA-PSS signature (section 8.1.2) of
  # *message* under *hash*, MGF1 over the same hash, with a salt of
  # *salt_length* bytes (the digest's length when nil).
  def verify_pss(hash : RsaHash, message : Array(UInt8) | String, signature : Array(UInt8), salt_length : Int32 | ::Nil = nil) : Bool
end

impl Error for RsaError
  def message : String
end

  # parameter is `SemanticVersion` for the reason `Prerelease#<=>` gives:

  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(major : Int32, minor : Int32, patch : Int32, prerelease : String | Prerelease | Nil = nil, build : String | ::Nil = nil)

  def minor : Int32

  def self.parse?(str : String) : self | ::Nil

  # Adds value and answers the set, for chaining: `set << 1 << 2`.

  # The same members, in any order, where one element type holds the
  # other, as tuples compare (src/iyi/object.iyi).
  def ==(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U
  # Symmetric difference: what is in exactly one of the two.
  def ^(other : Set(U)) : Set(T | U) forall U
  # Adds every element of other; answers the set.
  def concat(other : Set(T)) : Set(T)
  # No element in common; two empty sets are disjoint.
  def disjoint?(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U
  # A copy with the same elements in the same order.

  # hold is not.

  # through splitmix64's finaliser before a wrapping sum, which does not
  # care about order the way the sets do not, and the size is folded in
  # after, as `Array#hash` folds it. The members' hashes summed as they
  # were put a set of small integers at their total, `Int32#hash` being the
  # value: {1, 4} and {2, 3} were one key, the 11,175 sets {i, j} with
  # i < j < 150 had 297 hashes between them, and a table of such keys grew
  # quadratically.
  def hash : Int32
  # At least one element in common.
  def intersects?(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U
  # A subset that is not the same set.
  def proper_subset_of?(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U
  def proper_superset_of?(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U
  # Every element of this set is in other. The empty set is a subset of
  # every set, itself included.
  def subset_of?(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U
  def superset_of?(other : Set(U)) : Bool forall U

  def []?(index : Int32) : T | ::Nil

  # other library counts it: `s[3..1]` is the empty slice at 3. The count is
  # taken only once the end is known to be past the start, and the
  # inclusive end is added only while the count can still fit, so an end
  # near the top of `Int32` answers nil instead of overflowing.
  def []?(range : Range(Int32, Int32)) : Slice(T) | ::Nil

  def bytesize : Int32
  # Returns a copy of this slice.
  def clone : Slice(T)
  # Copies *count* elements from raw *source* pointer into this slice.
  def copy_from(source : Pointer(T), count : Int32) : Nil
  # Copies all elements from *source* slice into this slice.
  def copy_from(source : Slice(T)) : Nil

  def copy_to(target : Pointer(T), count : Int32) : Nil

  def copy_to(target : Slice(T)) : Nil

  # refused, so a read-only slice could not be duplicated at all.

  def each_with_index(& : (T, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil

  def self.empty : self

  def empty? : Bool
  # Fills *count* elements starting at *start* with *value*.
  def fill(value : T, start : Int32, count : Int32) : self
  # Fills the entire slice with *value*.
  def fill(value : T) : self
  # Fills the entire slice by yielding each index to the block.
  def fill(& : (Int32 -> T)) : self
  # Returns a lowercase hex string representation of Bytes.
  def hexstring : String
  # Creates a slice wrapping *pointer* bounded by *size*.
  #
  # `read_only` is named in this and every `Slice.new`, as in the other
  # library. Positional, it took the value's place when `T` is `Bool`:
  # `Slice(Bool).new(3, true)` was `Slice[false, false, false]`, read-only.
  def initialize(pointer : Pointer(T), size : Int32, *, read_only : Bool = false)
  def inspect : String
  # Moves *count* elements from *source* pointer into this slice, safely handling overlaps.
  def move_from(source : Pointer(T), count : Int32) : Nil
  # Moves all elements from *source* slice into this slice, safely handling overlaps.
  def move_from(source : Slice(T)) : Nil
  # Moves *count* elements from this slice into *target* pointer, safely handling overlaps.
  def move_to(target : Pointer(T), count : Int32) : Nil
  # Moves all elements from this slice into *target* slice, safely handling overlaps.
  def move_to(target : Slice(T)) : Nil
  # Allocates a slice of *size* elements initialized to *value*.
  #
  # These three answer `Slice(T)`, not `self`, as `Array.new` does: when the
  # element type is left to the value or the block, `self` is still the
  # unbound `Slice(T)` while the body builds `Slice(Int32)`, so
  # `Slice.new(3) { |i| i + 1 }` and `Slice.new(3, 7)` did not compile.
  def self.new(size : Int32, value : T, *, read_only : Bool = false) : Slice(T)
  # Allocates a slice of *size* elements on the heap.
  def self.new(size : Int32, *, read_only : Bool = false) : self
  # Allocates a slice of *size* elements initialized by yielding each index.
  def self.new(size : Int32, & : (Int32 -> T)) : Slice(T)
  def self.new(size : Int32, *, read_only : Bool, & : (Int32 -> T)) : Slice(T)
  def read_only? : Bool
  # Reverses the elements of the slice in-place.
  def reverse : self
  def reverse_in_place : self
  # Returns true if this slice and *other* point to the exact same memory and have the same size.
  def same?(other : Slice(T)) : Bool
  def size : Int32
  # Swaps elements at index *i* and index *j*.
  def swap(i : Int32, j : Int32) : self
  # Returns an Array containing all elements in this slice.
  def to_a : Array(T)
  # String representation: Bytes[...] for Slice(UInt8), Slice[...] for others.
  def to_s : String
  # Raw pointer to the underlying buffer.
  def to_unsafe : Pointer(T)
  # Raw element access without bounds checks (required for Indexable).
  def unsafe_fetch(index : Int32) : T
  # Raw element write without bounds checks.
  def unsafe_put(index : Int32, value : T) : T
end

# The lazy half, which `Slice` had no way into: `std/iterator`'s header says
# a concrete collection provides its own iterator constructor and names this
# type twice as one that should, and then the only route from a slice to a
# lazy chain was `fs.to_a` — copying the whole sequence, which is the cost
# the tower exists to avoid.
#
# A class, as `ArrayIterator` is (std/iterator): an adaptor keeps its source
# by value, and a struct source was copied into it, so `it.first(2).to_a`
# and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where an array's iterator
# gives [1, 2] and [3, 4].
pub class SliceIterator(T)
  def initialize(slice : Slice(T))
  def next : T | Stop
end

impl Std::Indexable::Indexable for Slice(T) forall T
end

impl Std::Enumerable::Enumerable for Slice(T) forall T
  def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
end

impl Std::Iterator::Iterator for SliceIterator(T) forall T
end

modules.name: std/smtp
modules.surface:
module std/smtp

pub enum SmtpAuth : Int32
  Plain = 0
  Login = 1
  CramMd5 = 2
end

# A session with a mail server.
pub class SmtpClient
  def self.ascii?(text : String) : Bool
  # AUTH as *user* with *password*, by *mechanism*, or by the first the
  # server offers of PLAIN, LOGIN and CRAM-MD5.
  def auth(user : String, password : String, mechanism : SmtpAuth | ::Nil = nil) : SmtpError | ::Nil
  # Whether a password may go over a connection without TLS.
  def cleartext_auth : Bool
  # Whether a password may go over a connection without TLS.
  def cleartext_auth=(value : Bool) : Bool
  # The connection closed, without QUIT.
  def close : Nil
  def closed? : Bool
  # *line* sent, and its reply.
  def command(line : String) : SmtpReply | SmtpError
  # A session with *host* on *port*: connected, greeted, EHLO said, and
  # under TLS as *security* asks.
  def self.connect(host : String, port : Int32, security : SmtpSecurity = SmtpSecurity::StartTls, config : TlsConfig = TlsConfig.new, helo : String | ::Nil = nil, timeout_ms : Int32 = TIMEOUT_MS) : SmtpClient | SmtpError
  def self.digit?(b : UInt8) : Bool
  # What EHLO named, by its keyword in upper case: each extension's
  # parameters ("" when none). Empty after HELO.
  def extensions : Hash(String, String)
  # The server's 220.
  def greeting : SmtpReply
  def initialize(socket : IyiSocket, host : String, helo : String, timeout_ms : Int32)
  # `[192.0.2.1]`, or `[IPv6:2001:db8::1]` (section 4.1.3).
  def self.literal(address : String) : String
  def self.mechanism_name(mechanism : SmtpAuth) : String
  protected def open(security : SmtpSecurity, config : TlsConfig) : SmtpError | ::Nil
  # QUIT, its 221 read, and the connection closed.
  def quit : SmtpError | ::Nil
  # The next reply, every line of it.
  def reply : SmtpReply | SmtpError
  # *data*, a whole message, from *sender* to *recipients*; *utf8* when
  # the message is RFC 6532's, as SMTPUTF8 carries.
  def send(sender : String, recipients : Array(String), data : String, utf8 : Bool = false) : SmtpError | ::Nil
  # *message* to its recipients - To, Cc and Bcc - from its From.
  def send(message : Mail::Message) : SmtpError | ::Nil
  # *data* as DATA sends it (section 4.5.2): line breaks CRLF, a dot
  # doubled at a line's start, a CRLF at the end if it had none, and the
  # lone dot after.
  def self.stuffed(data : String) : String
  # Whether the session is under TLS.
  def tls? : Bool
  def self.unsafe?(text : String) : Bool
end

# What a session answered that it should not have, or could not do, as a
# value. `code` is the reply's code, 0 when there was no reply to have
# one; `reply` the reply's text, its lines joined with newlines.
pub struct SmtpError
  def cancelled? : Bool
  def code : Int32
  def initialize(reason : String, code : Int32 = 0, reply : String = "", timed_out : Bool = false, cancelled : Bool = false)
  def reason : String
  def reply : String
  # Whether a read or a write waited `timeout_ms` and nothing came.
  def timed_out? : Bool
  def to_s : String
end

# One reply: its code and its lines' text, the code and separator taken
# off each.
pub struct SmtpReply
  def code : Int32
  def initialize(code : Int32, lines : Array(String))
  def lines : Array(String)
  def text : String
end

# How the connection is kept from the wire.
pub enum SmtpSecurity : Int32
  StartTls = 0
  Tls = 1
  Cleartext = 2
end

impl Error for SmtpError
  def message : String
end

modules.surface:
module std/socket

# What a resolver answers and is built from, under the names a program
# that connects by name already imports from here.
pub alias DnsError = Std::Dns::DnsError

# Either family's address: what a resolver answers for a name.
pub alias IPAddress = IPv4Address | IPv6Address

pub struct IPv4Address
  def b0 : UInt8
  def b1 : UInt8
  def b2 : UInt8
  def b3 : UInt8
  def initialize(b0 : UInt8, b1 : UInt8, b2 : UInt8, b3 : UInt8)
  def to_s : String
end

# Sixteen bytes in network order, held as two words: `high` is bytes 0 to
# 7. Written the RFC 5952 way - lowercase, no leading zeros, the longest
# run of two or more zero groups as `::`, the first of two equal runs -
# and an IPv4-mapped address with its dotted tail, `::ffff:192.0.2.1`.
pub struct IPv6Address
  # Byte *index*, 0 to 15.
  def [](index : Int32) : UInt8
  # The 16-bit group *index*, 0 to 7. Not `group`: that name is the task
  # group's in iyi (SPEC.md III.4.9).
  def hextet(index : Int32) : Int32
  def high : UInt64
  def initialize(high : UInt64, low : UInt64)
  def low : UInt64
  # The sixteen bytes at *bytes*, network order.
  def self.new(bytes : Pointer(UInt8)) : IPv6Address
  def to_s : String
end

pub class IyiSocket
  alias AcceptExFn = Proc(UInt64, UInt64, ::Pointer(Void), Int32, Int32, Int32, Pointer(Int32), ::Pointer(Void), Int32)
  alias ConnectExFn = Proc(UInt64, ::Pointer(Void), Int32, ::Pointer(Void), Int32, Pointer(Int32), ::Pointer(Void), Int32)
  lib LibAdvapi32
  end
  lib LibWs2_32
    # Two slots of an address and the sixteen bytes after it, room for
    # the widest family this file makes.
    struct AcceptAddresses
    end
    struct PollFd
    end
    # A WSABUF, and the two address slots AcceptEx fills in - each a
    # `sockaddr_in` and the sixteen bytes it insists on after one. They are
    # declared here so that the callers below can keep them on the stack:
    # the kernel reads and writes these while the fiber is parked, and a
    # heap chunk whose only reference is a local the posting call has
    # finished with is a chunk the collector can hand to somebody else
    # first. `bench/server_load.iyi` died of a memory fault on exactly
    # that, with the accepted addresses on the heap.
    struct WSABuf
    end
  end
  # Room for any family's `sockaddr`, zeroed, so a unix path the kernel
  # did not end with a NUL still ends.
  def self.__address_room : Pointer(UInt8)
  # A `sockaddr` the kernel filled, as text: dotted IPv4, IPv6 written as
  # RFC 5952 has it, or a unix socket's path.
  def self.__address_text(addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32) : String
  # Winsock's address length is an `int*` where POSIX has a `socklen_t*`:
  # the same width and the same bytes, so the callers above keep one
  # signature.
  def self.__sys_accept(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32), family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_accept_posted(s : UInt64, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32), family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_addr_size(family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_bind(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32) : Int32
  # Every close of a socket in this file goes through here. `__iyi_close` is
  # the descriptor close, and on Windows a socket is not a descriptor:
  # `CloseHandle` on a SOCKET releases the kernel handle and leaves Winsock's
  # half of it standing, and the graceful close that makes a peer's read
  # answer EOF rather than a reset is `closesocket`'s.
  def self.__sys_close(fd : Int32) : Nil
  # The failures above arrive as the Winsock number negated.
  def self.__sys_code(result : Int64) : Int32
  def self.__sys_connect(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32) : Int32
  # A unix socket connects blocking, and is made non-blocking after:
  # `ConnectEx` is TCP's alone, and the plain `connect` on a socket
  # already non-blocking is not an answer here. Measured on the runner,
  # it came back connected to a path whose listener had closed, and,
  # waited for with `select`, refused a listener that was there. On a
  # socket still blocking it is Go's `connect` on this platform, and
  # its answer is the outcome: the listener is on this machine, and its
  # kernel queues the connection or refuses it at once.
  def self.__sys_connects_blocking?(family : Int32) : ::Bool
  # The plain call, not `__sys_connect`'s `ConnectEx`, which is TCP's: a
  # datagram socket's connect records the peer and returns.
  def self.__sys_dgram_connect(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32) : Int32
  # The plain call, not `__sys_send`'s posted one: a datagram of a
  # query's size goes out whole or not at all, and there is no room to
  # wait for.
  def self.__sys_dgram_send(fd : Int32, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64) : Int64
  # The resolver's datagram socket: UDP, non-blocking, and - unlike
  # `std/udp`'s - with Windows' report of an ICMP port-unreachable left
  # on. This one is connected to one name server, so the report says
  # that server has nothing on its port, and the next server is asked at
  # once instead of after the timeout.
  def self.__sys_dgram_socket(family : Int32) : Int32
  # Not `await_readable`: the scheduler's readable-wait is a zero-byte
  # overlapped read, and on a datagram socket that read takes the
  # datagram and leaves nothing for the receive after it (measured, and
  # the reason `std/udp` posts its receive instead). `WSAPoll` asks
  # without taking, but it blocks the thread for as long as it is told,
  # and every other task on the thread with it; so it is asked with no
  # wait at all, and the task sleeps on the scheduler between askings -
  # at Windows' timer tick, 15.6 ms, which is nothing next to a name
  # server's round trip.
  def self.__sys_dgram_wait(fd : Int32, ms : Int32) : ::Bool | Cancelled
  # The machine's resolver configuration, read from the registry:
  #
  # - name servers: the TCP/IP service's own `NameServer` (a policy's),
  #   then each IPv4 interface that has an address - `NameServer` when
  #   it was set by hand, else `DhcpNameServer` - then each IPv6
  #   interface's `NameServer`, without repeats, at most
  #   `ResolvConf::MAX_NAMESERVERS`;
  # - search list: `SearchList`, else the primary DNS suffix (`Domain`,
  #   else `DhcpDomain`).
  #
  # What it cannot see: which interface is up (a stale DHCP lease on an
  # unplugged adapter still has an address in the registry), the order
  # of the interfaces' metrics (they are read in the registry's order),
  # IPv6 servers learned from router advertisements or DHCPv6 (stored as
  # binary, not read), and per-connection suffixes. Those need
  # iphlpapi; see the `lib` above for why it is not linked.
  def self.__sys_dns_config : ResolvConf
  # The failure the last call left, negated. The POSIX arms answer the
  # kernel's errno this way — Linux the negative return itself, darwin
  # `errno` read after a -1 — and this answers Winsock's number in the same
  # shape, so nothing above learns a second convention: a negative result
  # is the failure, and the two predicates below are the only things that
  # read which failure it was.
  def self.__sys_error : Int64
  # The pointer to one of mswsock's extension functions, asked of the
  # socket that will use it. Fetched where it is used rather than cached:
  # it is one call, and both callers are about to do a TCP handshake.
  def self.__sys_extension(s : UInt64, low : UInt64, high : UInt64) : Pointer(UInt64)
  def self.__sys_getpeername(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32)) : Int32
  def self.__sys_getsockname(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32)) : Int32
  # A SOCKET from the `Int32` the class carries, and back: see the note
  # above the `lib` block for why that is lossless.
  def self.__sys_handle(fd : Int32) : UInt64
  def self.__sys_in_progress?(result : Int32) : ::Bool
  # Winsock caps a backlog at SOMAXCONN, 200, and turns the next connect
  # away as refused - where Linux holds it - unless the backlog is asked
  # as SOMAXCONN_HINT(n), which is -n: 220 connects to a listener asked
  # for 256 lost 20.
  def self.__sys_listen(fd : Int32, backlog : Int32) : Int32
  # Windows raises no SIGPIPE; a write to a closed connection answers
  # WSAECONNRESET or WSAESHUTDOWN.
  def self.__sys_no_sigpipe(fd : Int32) : Nil
  # The wait a cancelled post still owes the kernel. `CancelIoEx` is a
  # request, and on a socket tied to a completion port the operation is not
  # over when it returns: measured here, the status stays STATUS_PENDING
  # and the address block, the descriptor and the OVERLAPPED are the
  # kernel's until the completion packet is taken *off the port* — the
  # poller's `GetQueuedCompletionStatus` is what writes them. The same
  # measurement on an unassociated socket had the status written by
  # `CancelIoEx` itself, which is why this is not obvious. So
  # `WSAGetOverlappedResult`'s own wait flag cannot be the wait either: it
  # waits on the OVERLAPPED's event, the scheduler's OVERLAPPED has none,
  # and the socket handle it falls back to is never signalled for a socket
  # on a port — it hung forever on the first cancelled receive tried.
  #
  # What ends the operation is the poller, so the frame parks once more and
  # lets it. `IyiScheduler.cancel` has already unregistered this fiber,
  # which is what would have left the packet to be dropped; parking puts it
  # back, and the wake means the dequeue has happened. Asked first, because
  # a completion the poller delivered *before* the cancel is already over
  # and no second packet is coming — parking on one would never wake.
  def self.__sys_overlapped_await(s : UInt64, ov : Pointer(UInt8)) : Int64
  # What a posted operation ended with, read off the operation itself. The
  # completion port's byte count cannot tell a failure from a success that
  # transferred nothing, and a successful `AcceptEx` or `ConnectEx` is
  # exactly that — both complete with zero bytes. Nothing waits here: the
  # completion has already arrived, which is what the 0 says.
  def self.__sys_overlapped_result(s : UInt64, ov : Pointer(UInt8)) : Int64
  # TCP names its protocol; a unix socket has only the one, and says 0.
  def self.__sys_protocol(family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_recv(fd : Int32, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64) : Int64
  def self.__sys_send(fd : Int32, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64, ms : Int32) : Int64
  # The send as the wait, with the write's deadline on it: a deadline
  # that comes first cancels the send, and the cancellation's completion
  # wakes this frame, so what the send did is known when it returns.
  def self.__sys_send_posted(s : UInt64, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64, ms : Int32) : Int64
  def self.__sys_set_nonblock(fd : Int32) : Int32
  # Not SO_REUSEADDR, which on Windows lets a *different* socket bind a
  # port this one is already bound to, and the last binder takes the
  # packets; what the POSIX arms ask for with it is only the waiver of
  # the TIME_WAIT wait, which Windows does not impose on a listener's
  # port. The opposite: SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE (~SO_REUSEADDR, -5). Without
  # it the port was not the listener's either - a bind to 127.0.0.1:P went
  # through while 0.0.0.0:P listened, and the other way round, from any
  # process, and the more specific listener took the connections.
  def self.__sys_set_reuseaddr(fd : Int32) : Int32
  # IPV6_V6ONLY (27) at IPPROTO_IPV6 (41). Windows' default already, and
  # said anyway: the default is a registry's, and this is the program's.
  def self.__sys_set_v6only(fd : Int32) : Int32
  # SO_ERROR at SOL_SOCKET, as on the POSIX arms. `__sys_connect` above has
  # already waited for the handshake and answered what it ended with, so
  # the shared `connect` reaches this only when its task was cancelled —
  # and `wait_writable` answers `Cancelled` before it gets here. It reads
  # the option rather than guessing, so it is the truth for anything that
  # does ask.
  def self.__sys_sock_error(fd : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_socket(family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_winsock : Nil
  # WSAEWOULDBLOCK answers both questions here: it is what a non-blocking
  # call with nothing to do says, and it is what a connect that is under
  # way says, where POSIX has EAGAIN and EINPROGRESS for the two.
  def self.__sys_would_block?(result : Int64) : ::Bool
  def accept : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  def self.await_readable(fd : Int32, ms : Int32 = -1) : ::Bool | Cancelled
  def self.await_writable(fd : Int32, ms : Int32 = -1) : ::Bool | Cancelled
  # A timeout as the waits take it: milliseconds, -1 for none.
  def self.bound(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32
  protected def bound_path(path : String) : Nil
  # *path* with the NUL a system call reads to.
  def self.c_path(path : String) : Pointer(UInt8)
  def close : Nil
  def closed? : ::Bool
  # `localhost` is 127.0.0.1 and then ::1: a refused or unreachable
  # 127.0.0.1 is tried again at ::1. Windows names both, ::1 first, and a
  # dev server that binds `localhost` there is often on ::1 alone, where
  # a connect to 127.0.0.1 only was "connection refused". 127.0.0.1 goes
  # first because a listener here binds `localhost` there. Windows takes
  # 2 s to refuse a connect, so a ::1-only listener is reached in 2 s
  # (2017 ms measured) and a port nobody holds is refused in 4 s, not 2.
  #
  # Any other host name is resolved by the machine's resolver
  # (`Resolver.system`) and its addresses tried in the order the resolver
  # answers them - IPv4 first, then IPv6, as `localhost` is - until one
  # connects; a name that does not resolve is a `SocketError` whose
  # `unresolved?` is true and whose sentence names the host. It panicked,
  # "cannot resolve address: \"example.com\"", for every name but
  # `localhost`, so `HTTP.get("http://example.com/")` could not run.
  #
  # *timeout_ms* bounds each address's handshake (-1: as long as the
  # kernel waits, which on Linux is about two minutes of SYN retries for
  # a host that drops them); one that runs out is a `SocketError` whose
  # `timed_out?` is true, and the next address is tried.
  def self.connect(host : String, port : Int32, timeout_ms : Int32 = -1) : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  # The same, with a host name resolved by *resolver*: name servers, a
  # hosts file and search list of the program's choosing, rather than the
  # machine's. An address and `localhost` are what they are either way.
  def self.connect(host : String, port : Int32, resolver : Resolver, timeout_ms : Int32 = -1) : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  # A connect to *addr*, waiting at most *ms* milliseconds for the
  # handshake (-1: as long as the kernel does). The resolver's TCP query
  # is the caller with a bound; `connect` waits as the kernel does, as it
  # always has.
  def self.connect_to(addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32, peer : String, ms : Int32 = -1) : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  # The stream socket listening at *path*.
  def self.connect_unix(path : String) : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  # *host* and *port* as a message names them: an IPv6 literal in its
  # brackets, as a URL writes it. Bare, `::1:57456` was an address with
  # no port, and `ff02::1:80` another address altogether.
  def self.endpoint(host : String, port : Int32) : String
  def fd : Int32
  # The address family, the platform's number for it: an accepted
  # connection is its listener's, and on Windows the socket `AcceptEx`
  # fills in has to be made in it.
  def initialize(fd : Int32, family : Int32 = AF_INET)
  def self.listen(host : String, port : Int32, backlog : Int32 = 128) : IyiSocket
  def self.listen(port : Int32, backlog : Int32 = 128) : IyiSocket
  # A stream socket at *path*. The path must not exist: a socket file an
  # earlier run left behind is refused rather than taken over, since
  # which program owns it is not something a bind can know. `close`
  # removes the file.
  def self.listen_unix(path : String, backlog : Int32 = 128) : IyiSocket
  def local_address : String
  # The port sits at the same two bytes of a `sockaddr_in` and a
  # `sockaddr_in6`.
  def local_port : Int32
  # `localhost` in any case, and with the one trailing dot of a name
  # written fully qualified: a host name's case is not part of it (RFC
  # 4343), and getaddrinfo, Python and curl all answer 127.0.0.1 for
  # `LOCALHOST` and `localhost.`. Matched exactly, these were "cannot
  # resolve address: \"LOCALHOST\"", and so were `Localhost` and
  # `localhost.`.
  def self.localhost?(host : String) : ::Bool
  def self.make_sockaddr_in(ip : IPv4Address, port : Int32) : Pointer(UInt8)
  # A `sockaddr_in6`: family, port, a zero flow label, the address, a zero
  # scope. The family's number and where it sits are the platform's.
  def self.make_sockaddr_in6(ip : IPv6Address, port : Int32) : Pointer(UInt8)
  # A `sockaddr_un`: the family, then the path and its NUL. The room for
  # the path is the platform's - 104 bytes on darwin, 108 elsewhere - and a
  # longer one is refused rather than cut, since a cut path is another
  # path.
  def self.make_sockaddr_un(path : String) : Pointer(UInt8)
  # Dotted-decimal IPv4 only: four octets of 0 to 255, no leading zero
  # (`"010.1.1.1"` is refused; glibc's `inet_aton` reads `010` as octal 8,
  # CVE-2021-29921, so it must not quietly be 10 here), plus `localhost`.
  # The refusal inspects the host so a stray space shows.
  def self.parse_ip(host : String) : IPv4Address
  # Eight groups of up to four hex digits, `::` once for a run of zero
  # groups, and a dotted IPv4 tail for the last two (`::ffff:1.2.3.4`). A
  # zone (`fe80::1%eth0`) is refused by name: it names an interface, and
  # this parser has no way to ask the platform which.
  def self.parse_ipv6(host : String) : IPv6Address

  # The reading alone, the refusal's sentence as the answer: see
  # `read_ipv4`.
  def self.read_ipv6(host : String) : IPv6Address | String
  # The bounds on a read's and a write's wait, in milliseconds; nil waits
  # as long as it takes.

  def recv(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError

  def remote_address : String | ::Nil
  def remote_port : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Every address *host* stands for, by the machine's resolver: what
  # `connect` tries, in the order it tries them. See `Resolver#resolve`.
  def self.resolve(host : String) : Array(IPAddress) | DnsError | Cancelled

pub alias ResolvConf = Std::Dns::ResolvConf

# A stub resolver: a host name's addresses, from a hosts file and then
# from name servers, as the C library's resolver finds them - but iyi's,
# so asking costs no library (see the header of this file).
#
# `Resolver.system` is the machine's: `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/hosts`
# on Linux and darwin, the registry and
# `%SystemRoot%\System32\drivers\etc\hosts` on Windows (see
# `__sys_dns_config` for what the registry can and cannot say). A
# resolver built with `new` or `from_config` asks exactly what it was
# given, which is how a test asks a server it runs itself.
#
# `resolve` answers every address for a name, IPv4 first and then IPv6
# (the order `connect` tries `localhost` in), each family in the order
# the hosts file or the server gave it:
#
# 1. An address, or `localhost` (127.0.0.1 and ::1: RFC 6761 6.3 keeps it
#    off the network), is itself. Anything that is not a host name is
#    `invalid_name?`.
# 2. The hosts file: every line naming the host, in any case. A name
#    found there is not asked about.
# 3. The names the search list and `ndots` make of it (`DnsName.candidates`),
#    in order. Each is asked for A and then AAAA records; NXDOMAIN or no
#    records moves on to the next, and any other failure ends the lookup
#    with that failure - a server that timed out on `db.corp.example` must
#    not turn the answer into `db.example`'s (musl's rule; glibc moves on).
#
# A query is one UDP datagram from a fresh socket (so a fresh source
# port), with an ID from `Random::Secure`, to each server in turn, each
# waited for `timeout_ms`, and the round repeated `attempts` times. A
# datagram that does not carry the ID and the question is ignored and the
# wait goes on; one from any other address never arrives, because the
# socket is connected to the server. An answer with TC set is asked again
# over TCP. SERVFAIL, REFUSED and a server that does not answer move on to
# the next server; NXDOMAIN is the answer. An answer that cannot be read
# is ignored like a forgery, and is the failure reported if nothing
# better arrives before the timeout.
pub class Resolver
  def attempts : Int32
  # A resolver from a parsed resolv.conf and a hosts file's text. A
  # `nameserver` line this resolver cannot use - an IPv6 address with a
  # zone, a typo - is skipped as glibc skips one; with none left, the
  # servers a machine without a configuration is assumed to run.
  def self.from_config(config : ResolvConf, hosts : String = "") : Resolver
  # A resolver from a resolv.conf and a hosts file at these paths. A file
  # that is not there reads as empty, as it does to the C library.
  def self.from_files(resolv_conf : String, hosts : String) : Resolver
  # The hosts file's text, read before any server is asked.
  def hosts : String
  # *nameservers* are addresses, each with an optional port:
  # `"192.0.2.1"`, `"192.0.2.1:5353"`, `"2001:db8::1"`,
  # `"[2001:db8::1]:5353"`. One that is not is refused here, by name: it is
  # the program's own mistake. None at all is a resolver that reads only
  # *hosts*.
  def initialize(nameservers : Array(String), search : Array(String) = [] of String, ndots : Int32 = 1, timeout_ms : Int32 = 5000, attempts : Int32 = 2, hosts : String = "")
  def nameservers : Array(String)
  def ndots : Int32
  # The monotonic clock in milliseconds: the runtime's, which its sleep
  # queue keeps deadlines by. A target without the runtime has no socket
  # to wait on either (`__sys_dgram_socket` refuses there), so nothing
  # there reads a time.
  def self.now_ms : Int64
  def self.rcode_name(rcode : Int32) : String
  # Every address *host* stands for: see the class's comment for the
  # order things are asked in.
  def resolve(host : String) : Array(IPAddress) | DnsError | Cancelled
  def search : Array(String)
  # A name server written as an address with an optional port, or the
  # sentence saying why it is not one.
  def self.server(text : String) : NameServer | String
  # The machine's resolver, read afresh each time: a configuration the
  # network manager rewrote is the one the next lookup uses.
  def self.system : Resolver
  def timeout_ms : Int32
end

# A connection's own failure: which operation, and the platform's error
# number for why - or, for a host name that could not be turned into an
# address, the resolver's `DnsError`, and no number (`code` 0); or, for a
# protocol layered on the connection (TLS), that protocol's own sentence,
# and no number either.
pub struct SocketError
  def code : Int32
  # The peer is gone: it reset the connection, or closed it and the write
  # found the pipe broken, or the connection was aborted.
  def disconnected? : ::Bool
  # Why the host's name did not resolve; nil for every other failure.
  def dns_error : DnsError | ::Nil
  def initialize(operation : String, code : Int32, dns_error : DnsError | ::Nil, layer_reason : String | ::Nil)
  def initialize(operation : String, code : Int32, dns_error : DnsError | ::Nil)
  def initialize(operation : String, code : Int32)
  # What the protocol over the connection said went wrong; nil otherwise.
  def layer_reason : String | ::Nil
  # A failure of the protocol over the connection, in its words: `cannot
  # read from example.com: tls: a record that does not decrypt`.
  def self.layered(operation : String, reason : String) : SocketError
  def operation : String
  def reason : String
  def refused? : ::Bool
  # A wait for the peer that ran past its socket's timeout, carrying the
  # platform's own number for it so `reason` and `timed_out?` read it as
  # they read the kernel's.
  def self.timed_out(operation : String) : SocketError
  # The peer did not answer in time: a connect the network timed out, or a
  # read or write past its socket's timeout.
  def timed_out? : ::Bool
  def unreachable? : ::Bool
  # The host was a name, and no address came of it: `dns_error` says why
  # (`not_found?` for NXDOMAIN, `server_failure?` for SERVFAIL, ...).
  def unresolved? : ::Bool
end

# A socket as a stream, for what is written against streams: `read_line`,
# `puts`, `IyiIO.copy` between it and a file or a pipe. Its reads and
# writes are the socket's own, which park the task and keep its
# timeouts. A stream has no error to answer, so a read the socket refuses
# ends the stream, `read_failed?` true, and a write it refuses panics,
# naming the reason; a program that answers those reads the socket.
# Writes are buffered: `flush`, or `IyiIO.copy`, which flushes, sends
# them. Closing it closes the socket.
pub class SocketIO < ::IyiIO
  def initialize(socket : IyiSocket, buffer_size : Int32 = 4096)
  def socket : IyiSocket
end

impl Error for SocketError
  def message : String
end
