module std/sse

# One dispatched event: its type (`message` unless the stream named one
# with `event:`), its data, and the last event ID as it stood when it was
# dispatched, which an event without an `id:` field inherits.
pub struct Event
  def data : String
  def event : String
  def id : String
  def initialize(event : String, data : String, id : String)
end

# §9.2.6's interpretation of an event stream, fed its bytes as they come:
# `feed(bytes) { |event| ... }` yields each event a blank line
# dispatches, and keeps what a piece ended inside - a line, an event, the
# CR of a CRLF - for the next. `finish` discards it, as the end of a
# stream does. `last_event_id` is the source's last event ID string,
# set at each blank line; `retry` the reconnection time the stream set,
# nil until it sets one; `dispatched` the events yielded so far.
pub class EventParser
  # A `retry` value: ASCII digits and nothing else, base ten, saturating
  # at `MAX_RETRY`; nil for anything else, the empty value included.
  protected def self.digits(text : String) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def dispatched : Int64
  def feed(text : String, & : (Event -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The end of the stream: a line or an event not yet ended is discarded,
  # not dispatched. The last event ID and the reconnection time stay.
  def finish : Nil
  # A parser for a stream whose last event ID is *last_event_id* so far:
  # a reconnection's, which carries the one before it (see the module's
  # header for why).
  def initialize(last_event_id : String = "")
  def last_event_id : String
  def retry : Int32 | ::Nil
end

# What `SSE.stream`'s block writes with: an event a `send`, a comment a
# `comment`, each one chunk sent at once. The first write that fails -
# the client went - is kept, and it and every write after it answer it;
# `gone?` says whether one has.
pub class EventWriter
  # A comment, a `:` line per line of *text*: read past by every client,
  # and a write that finds a client gone.
  def comment(text : String = "") : Nil | Cancelled | SocketError
  # Whether a write found the client gone.
  def gone? : Bool
  def initialize(writer : BodyWriter)
  # *text* cut at each CRLF, CR and LF: one line for a text without one,
  # an empty last line for a text that ends with one.
  protected def self.lines(text : String) : Array(String)
  # One event: `event:`, `id:` and `retry:` when given, *data* a `data:`
  # line per line (CRLF, CR and LF each end one, and each arrives as LF),
  # then the blank line that dispatches it. An empty *data* is an event
  # whose data is empty; an empty *id* resets the client's last event ID.
  def send(data : String, event : String | ::Nil = nil, id : String | ::Nil = nil, retry : Int32 | ::Nil = nil) : Nil | Cancelled | SocketError
  protected def self.utf8(text : String, what : String) : Nil
end

pub struct SSE
  # Whether a `Content-Type` is `text/event-stream`, in any case, with any
  # parameters.
  def self.event_stream?(type : String) : Bool
  # One connection's answer read: true when the block stopped, false when
  # the stream ended, or why it could not be read.
  protected def self.follow(response : Response, parser : EventParser, block : Proc(Event, Bool)) : Bool | SSEError | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError
  def initialize
  # The event stream at *url*, each event handed to *block*, which answers
  # true to go on and false to stop (nil, the connection closed). A
  # connection that drops or ends is made again after the reconnection
  # time - *retry* ms until the stream sets its own - with the last event
  # ID (*last_event_id* to start with, to resume a stream) in
  # `Last-Event-ID`. Once *reconnects* + 1 connections in a row have
  # brought no event, the last one's failure is the answer. An answer
  # that is not a 200 `text/event-stream` is an `SSEError` at once.
  # *headers* go with every request; `Accept` and `Last-Event-ID` are the
  # stream's own and are refused there.
  def self.open(url : String, headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String, last_event_id : String | ::Nil = nil, reconnects : Int32 = RECONNECTS, retry : Int32 = RETRY, &block : (Event -> Bool)) : Nil | Cancelled | SocketError | HTTPError | SSEError
  # The answer to a request for an event stream: a 200, `text/event-stream`,
  # `Cache-Control: no-cache` unless *headers* names its own, whose body
  # *block* writes through an `EventWriter` as it goes. The stream ends
  # when the block returns. A `Content-Type` in *headers* is refused.
  def self.stream(headers : Hash(String, String) = {} of String => String, &block : (EventWriter -> Nil)) : Response
end

# What the other end did that fails an event stream (§9.2.3), as a value:
# an answer that is not a 200, one that is not `text/event-stream`, or a
# stream that kept ending with no event until the client gave up.
# `status` is the answer's. `message` says it is SSE's.
pub struct SSEError
  def initialize(reason : String, status : Int32 = 200)
  def reason : String
  def status : Int32
  def to_s : String
end

impl Error for SSEError
  def message : String
end

module std/static_array

pub alias StaticArray = ::StaticArray

struct ::StaticArray(T, N)
  # Comparison based on lexicographical element order. Written out here: it
  # forwarded to `Slice#<=>`, which the slice module does not have, so any
  # call of this method failed to compile.
  def <=>(other : StaticArray(T, N)) : Int32
  # Equality. Returns true if corresponding elements are equal, where one
  # element type holds the other, as tuples compare (src/iyi/object.iyi).
  # Restricted to `StaticArray(T, N)`, a `StaticArray(Int32, 2)` was taken
  # for a `StaticArray(Int32?, 2)` and not back: the one equality answered
  # true one way and false the other.
  def ==(other : StaticArray(U, M)) : Bool forall U, M
  def ==(other : Object) : Bool
  # Returns the element at the given *index*. Negative indices count backward.
  def [](index : Int) : T
  # Sets the element at *index* to *value*.
  def []=(index : Int, value : T) : T
  # Returns the element at *index*, or nil if out of bounds.
  def []?(index : Int) : T | ::Nil
  def all? : Bool
  def any? : Bool
  def clone : self
  def count(item) : Int32
  def count : Int32
  # Duplicates this static array.
  def dup : self
  # Yields each element in order.
  def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Yields each element alongside its index.
  def each_with_index(offset : Int = 0, & : (T, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Returns true when the static array contains zero elements.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Fills *count* elements starting at *start* with *value*.
  #
  # A negative count and a start outside are refused before anything is
  # filled, as the other library and `Slice#fill` refuse them: an early
  # return for `c <= 0` came first, so `fill(7, 0, -1)` and `fill(7, 9, 0)`
  # of four elements answered the array untouched and said nothing.
  def fill(value : T, start : Int, count : Int) : self
  # Fills the entire static array with *value*.
  def fill(value : T) : self
  # Returns the first element. Raises if empty.
  def first : T
  # Returns the first element or nil if empty.
  def first? : T | ::Nil
  # Hashing follows the `==` above, mixed as `Array#hash` mixes. There was
  # only the other library's `hash(hasher)`, which no table here calls, so
  # `Object#hash` answered the type's id: every `StaticArray(Int32, 2)` was
  # one slot, and 40,000 of them took 13 s to insert where the same pairs
  # as tuples took 3 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  # Returns true if *object* is in the array.
  def includes?(object) : Bool
  # Returns the index of *object*, or nil if not found.
  def index(object, offset : Int = 0) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def inspect(io : IO) : Nil
  def inspect : String
  # Returns the last element. Raises if empty.
  def last : T
  # Returns the last element or nil if empty.
  def last? : T | ::Nil
  # Returns a new StaticArray with mapped elements.
  def map(&block : (T -> U)) : StaticArray(U, N) forall U
  # Returns a new StaticArray with mapped elements and indices.
  def map_with_index(offset : Int = 0, &block : (T, Int32 -> U)) : StaticArray(U, N) forall U
  # Creates a new StaticArray filled by invoking the block for each index.
  def self.new(& : (Int32 -> T)) : self
  # Creates a new StaticArray filled with the given value.
  def self.new(value : T) : self
  def none? : Bool
  def one? : Bool
  # Yields elements in reverse order.
  def reverse_each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Reverses elements in place.
  def reverse_in_place : self
  # Returns the last index of *object*, or nil if not found.
  def rindex(object, offset : Int = N - 1) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Rotates elements in place by *n* positions. Reduced in `Int64` before it
  # is narrowed, as `index_within` and `BitArray`'s rotation count: `n.to_i`
  # panicked "arithmetic overflow" for 3000000001_i64, which rotates four
  # elements by one.
  def rotate_in_place(n : Int = 1) : self
  # Returns the size of self.
  def size : Int32
  # Returns a new sorted static array.
  def sort : StaticArray(T, N)
  def sort(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  def sort_by(&block : (T -> _)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  # Each key computed once, by `Array#sort_in_place_by`, the merge sort of
  # key and element pairs: a comparison of `yield(a) <=> yield(b)` computed
  # it twice per comparison, 63,992,000 times for 8,000 elements.
  def sort_by_in_place(&block : (T -> _)) : self
  # Sorted by `Array#sort_in_place`, the stable merge sort, and copied
  # back. It was an insertion sort of its own, quadratic: 8,000 elements in
  # reverse order took 31,996,000 comparisons where the array's sort takes
  # under 100,000. Equal elements keep their order, as they did.
  def sort_in_place : self
  # In-place sort with custom block comparator, by the same merge sort.
  def sort_in_place(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : self
  # Converts this static array into a heap Array.
  def to_a : Array(T)
  # The text `to_s` builds, written as `BitArray#to_s(io)` writes it. It
  # asked each element for `inspect(io)`, which no prelude type has, and
  # `IyiIO` for `<<`, which only `import std/io` gives it: `to_s(STDOUT)`
  # of a `StaticArray(Int32, 3)` did not compile, and `inspect(io)` with it.
  def to_s(io : IO) : Nil
  # Into one builder: adding each element to the text so far copied that
  # text once per element, and 10,000 elements took 1.4 s where `to_a.to_s`
  # of the same took 1 ms.
  def to_s : String
  # Returns a Slice backed by this static array.
  def to_slice : Std::Slice::Slice(T)
  # Returns a pointer to this static array's data.
  def to_unsafe : Pointer(T)
  # Returns the element at *index* without bounds checking.
  def unsafe_fetch(index : Int) : T
  # Sets the element at *index* to *value* without bounds checking.
  def unsafe_put(index : Int, value : T) : T
  def unstable_sort : StaticArray(T, N)
  def unstable_sort(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  def unstable_sort_by(&block : (T -> _)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  def unstable_sort_by_in_place(&block : (T -> _)) : self
  def unstable_sort_in_place : self
  def unstable_sort_in_place(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : self
  macro [](*args)
end

# A time zone: the offsets from UTC a place has kept, and when it changed
# from one to the next. `Location.load("Europe/Istanbul")` reads the IANA
# database the machine has; `Location.local` is the machine's own zone;
# `Location.fixed(19800)` is an offset and nothing else; `Location::UTC` is
# UTC. A `Time` carries one, and its date and clock are read in it.
#
# The database is the system's TZif files, RFC 8536: `$ZONEINFO` when it
# names a directory, then `/usr/share/zoneinfo`, `/usr/share/lib/zoneinfo`
# and `/etc/zoneinfo`. Versions 1 to 4 are read. A time before the first
# change has the file's first offset, and one after the last has its POSIX
# footer's rule, so a slim file answers for the year 2100 as a fat one does.
# Leap seconds are not counted, as no clock this module reads counts them.

  def minute : Int32
  def self.monotonic : Span
  def self.monotonic_nanoseconds : UInt64
  def month : Int32
  def nanosecond : Int32
  def nanoseconds : Int32
  def self.new(year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32, hour : Int32 = 0, minute : Int32 = 0, second : Int32 = 0, millisecond : Int32 = 0, nanosecond : Int32 = 0) : Time
  def offset : Int32
  def self.pad2(n : Int32) : String
  def self.pad3(n : Int32) : String
  # Four digits, and a negative year keeps its sign in front of them rather
  # than inside: written as `n < 10 ? "000" + n.to_s`, year -1 printed
  # `000-1-01-01`, which is neither a year nor a date. ISO 8601 spells it
  # `-0001`, and the conversions themselves were right all along - the epoch
  # round-trips through it.
  def self.pad4(n : Int32) : String
  def self.pad6(n : Int32) : String
  def self.pad9(n : Int32) : String
  # Reads *string* by *pattern*'s directives (see `Time::Format`). A text
  # that names no zone is read at *offset* seconds east of UTC, as Crystal's
  # `Time.parse` reads one at the location it is given.
  def self.parse(string : String, pattern : String, offset : Int32) : Time | TimeParseError
  # Reads *string* by *pattern* in *location*: a text that names no zone is
  # the wall clock there, its offset the one the location kept at that date
  # (a wall time a change repeats or skips is read as `Time.local` reads
  # it), and the time answered is in *location* whether the text named a
  # zone or not.
  def self.parse(string : String, pattern : String, location : Location) : Time | TimeParseError
  def self.parse_iso8601(string : String) : Time | TimeParseError
  # `parse` in the machine's own zone.
  def self.parse_local(string : String, pattern : String) : Time | TimeParseError
  # Any of RFC 9110's three HTTP date forms; see `Time::Format::HTTP_DATE`.
  def self.parse_rfc1123(string : String) : Time | TimeParseError
  def self.parse_rfc2822(string : String) : Time | TimeParseError
  # Parses an RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 string into a UTC Time, and panics with the
  # parser's sentence when it is not one. Handles forms like:
  #   2024-02-29T12:30:45Z
  #   2024-02-29T12:30:45.123Z
  #   2024-02-29T12:30:45.123456789Z
  #   2024-02-29 12:30:45Z
  #   2024-02-29T12:30:45+05:00
  #   2024-02-29T12:30:45-08:00
  #   -0001-01-01T00:00:00Z and 12345-06-07T08:09:10Z, as `to_rfc3339` writes them
  # `Time::Format::RFC_3339.parse` reads the same grammar and answers a
  # `TimeParseError` instead, for text the program did not write itself.
  def self.parse_rfc3339(str : String) : Time
  # `parse` at UTC when the text names no zone.
  def self.parse_utc(string : String, pattern : String) : Time | TimeParseError
  def second : Int32
  def seconds : Int64
  # Moves the date by calendar years and months, then by weeks and days,
  # then by the smaller units, in that order, as Crystal's `shift` does. A
  # day the month does not have becomes its last: `Time.utc(2024, 1,
  # 31).shift(months: 1)` is 2024-02-29. The date moves on the wall clock
  # of the time's location, so the time of day is kept across a change of
  # offset - a day after 12:00 on the Saturday summer begins is 12:00 on
  # Sunday, 23 hours later - and the hours, minutes, seconds and
  # nanoseconds are exact. A year past an Int32 is refused with the
  # constructor's sentence, and a span the Int64 seconds do not hold with
  # `Span`'s.
  def shift(*, years : Int32 = 0, months : Int32 = 0, weeks : Int64 = 0_i64, days : Int64 = 0_i64, hours : Int64 = 0_i64, minutes : Int64 = 0_i64, seconds : Int64 = 0_i64, nanoseconds : Int64 = 0_i64) : Time
  def to_local : Time
  # RFC 1123's date as HTTP writes it, RFC 9110's IMF-fixdate, always in GMT:
  # `Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT`.
  def to_rfc1123 : String
  # RFC 2822's date, `Mon, 15 Feb 2016 04:35:50 +0000`, at *offset*, or at
  # the time's own offset when none is given.
  def to_rfc2822(offset : Int32 | ::Nil = nil) : String
  # RFC 3339 at the time's own offset: `Z` at UTC, `+02:00` in CEST. An
  # offset RFC 3339 cannot write, one with seconds in it as local mean time
  # before standard time had, is written as the same instant in UTC.
  def to_rfc3339(fraction_digits : Int32 = 0) : String
  # The instant written as it reads at *offset* seconds east of UTC:
  # `to_s("%F %T %:z", 19800)` is the wall clock in India.
  def to_s(format : String, offset : Int32) : String
  # The time written by *format*'s directives (see `Time::Format`) as its
  # own location reads it; `%Z` is the zone's abbreviation, `CEST`.
  def to_s(format : String) : String
  # `2016-02-15 10:20:30 UTC`, and in any other location the offset in
  # place of `UTC`: `2016-02-15 11:20:30 +01:00`.
  def to_s : String
  def to_unix : Int64
  def to_unix_f : Float64
  # Refused with the module's sentence past the milliseconds an Int64
  # holds, some 292 million years either side of 1970, where the multiply
  # was the prelude's bare "arithmetic overflow" for a year `Time.utc`
  # accepts, 300,000,000. Both edges answer to the last millisecond that
  # fits: the lowest 808 an Int64 holds were refused, so
  # `Time.unix_ms(Int64::MIN).to_unix_ms` panicked. A negative second is
  # taken one up and its milliseconds from 1000 down, so the product fits
  # too.
  def to_unix_ms : Int64
  def to_utc : Time
  def self.unix(seconds : Int64, nanoseconds : Int32 = 0) : Time
  def self.unix_ms(milliseconds : Int64) : Time
  def self.utc(year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32, hour : Int32 = 0, minute : Int32 = 0, second : Int32 = 0, millisecond : Int32 = 0, nanosecond : Int32 = 0) : Time
  def self.utc : Time
  def utc? : Bool
  def self.wall_clock_nanoseconds : UInt64
  # The instant of a day of an ISO 8601 week, as Crystal's `week_date` makes
  # it: `Time.week_date(2016, 1, 1)` is Monday 2016-01-04. A week the year
  # does not have and a day past Sunday are refused, where the other library answered
  # a day of some other week.
  def self.week_date(year : Int32, week : Int32, day_of_week : Int32, hour : Int32 = 0, minute : Int32 = 0, second : Int32 = 0, nanosecond : Int32 = 0) : Time
  # Days since 1970-01-01 of a day of an ISO 8601 week. Week 1 is the week
  # holding January 4th, so its Monday is the Monday on or before that day.
  def self.week_date_days(year : Int32, week : Int32, day_of_week : Int32) : Int64
  # A year has 53 ISO 8601 weeks when it starts on a Thursday, or on a
  # Wednesday in a leap year: either way it has 53 Thursdays, and a week
  # belongs to the year that holds its Thursday.
  def self.weeks_in_year(year : Int32) : Int32
  def year : Int32
  # The zone this instant is in at its location: its abbreviation, offset
  # and whether it is summer time.
  def zone : Location::Zone
end

# What `Time::Format#parse` and the named parsers answer when the text is not
# a time the pattern describes. Bad input is the caller's to handle, not a
# panic: a header or a log line from somewhere else is not a bug in the
# program reading it. `message` is the sentence, naming the byte the parser
# stood at and the text; `position` is that byte, counted from 0.
pub struct TimeParseError
  def initialize(message : String, input : String, position : Int32)
  def input : String
  def position : Int32
  def to_s : String
end

impl Error for TimeParseError
  def message : String
end

impl Std::Traits::Comparable for Span
  def <=>(other : self) : Int32
end

impl Error for LocationError
  def message : String
end

impl Std::Traits::Comparable for Time
  def <=>(other : self) : Int32
end

modules.name: std/tls
modules.surface:
module std/tls

# The alerts of RFC 8446 section 6, by the code each is sent as.
pub struct TlsAlert
  def initialize
end

# A connection to a server, its handshake done.
pub class TlsClient < TlsConnection
  # A connection to *host* on *port*, its handshake done and the server's
  # certificate checked for *host*.
  def self.connect(host : String, port : Int32, config : TlsConfig = TlsConfig.new, timeout_ms : Int32 = -1) : TlsClient | TlsError
  def handshake : TlsError | ::Nil
  def initialize(socket : IyiSocket, host : String, config : TlsConfig)
  # The handshake over a connected *socket*, for *host*, done within
  # *timeout_ms* (none when 0).
  def self.over(socket : IyiSocket, host : String, config : TlsConfig = TlsConfig.new, timeout_ms : Int32 = HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS) : TlsClient | TlsError
  def server_side? : Bool
end

# What a connection is checked against and offers.
pub class TlsConfig
  # Protocols offered by ALPN (RFC 7301), most wanted first: `["h2",
  # "http/1.1"]`. None offered when empty.
  def alpn : Array(String)
  # Protocols offered by ALPN (RFC 7301), most wanted first: `["h2",
  # "http/1.1"]`. None offered when empty.
  def alpn=(value : Array(String)) : Array(String)
  # The certificate and key sent to a server that asks for one (mutual
  # TLS), when the request names its scheme; none sent when nil.
  def identity : TlsIdentity | ::Nil
  # The certificate and key sent to a server that asks for one (mutual
  # TLS), when the request names its scheme; none sent when nil.
  def identity=(value : TlsIdentity | ::Nil) : TlsIdentity | ::Nil
  def initialize
  # The oldest version spoken. TLS 1.3 by default, and then a server that
  # answers in 1.2 is refused as one that does not speak 1.3; `TLS12`
  # offers 1.2 beside it (see the module's header for what it requires).
  def min_version : TlsVersion
  # The oldest version spoken. TLS 1.3 by default, and then a server that
  # answers in 1.2 is refused as one that does not speak 1.3; `TLS12`
  # offers 1.2 beside it (see the module's header for what it requires).
  def min_version=(value : TlsVersion) : TlsVersion
  # The time certificates are checked at; now when nil.
  def now : Time | ::Nil
  # The time certificates are checked at; now when nil.
  def now=(value : Time | ::Nil) : Time | ::Nil
  # The roots a server's chain must reach; the system's when nil, read
  # once for the whole process and kept, since reading them is most of a
  # handshake's own cost.
  def roots : Array(Certificate) | ::Nil
  # The roots a server's chain must reach; the system's when nil, read
  # once for the whole process and kept, since reading them is most of a
  # handshake's own cost.
  def roots=(value : Array(Certificate) | ::Nil) : Array(Certificate) | ::Nil
  def trusted_roots : Array(Certificate) | TlsError
end

# What either end of a connection does once it has keys: records read and
# written under them, alerts, KeyUpdate, close_notify. `TlsClient` and
# `TlsServer` are its two ends; each runs its own half of the handshake.
pub abstract class TlsConnection
  def abort : Nil
  # The protocol chosen by ALPN, if one was.
  def alpn_protocol : String | ::Nil
  def cipher_suite : String
  # close_notify, then the socket closed.
  def close : Nil
  def closed? : Bool
  # *length* bytes bound to this connection, for *label* and *context*
  # (RFC 8446 section 7.5, RFC 5705's interface): the same at both ends and
  # nowhere else - a channel binding, or keys for another protocol riding
  # on this one. No context is the empty one, as TLS 1.3 has it; in TLS
  # 1.2 (RFC 5705 section 4, over the extended master secret) an empty
  # context is none, as OpenSSL's exporter takes it when told of none.
  def export_keying_material(label : String, context : Array(UInt8) = [] of UInt8, length : Int32 = 32) : Array(UInt8)
  # The alert the error names (its last parenthesised word), sent before
  # the socket closes, by either end (RFC 8446 section 6.2): under the keys
  # this side writes with, or in the clear before there are any. None for
  # an alert the peer sent, whose sentence names no alert of this side's.
  # A server then reads and drops what the client goes on sending, until
  # it closes, for at most `LINGER_BYTES` and `LINGER_MS` in all: a close
  # with the client's flight unread is a reset, which can take the alert
  # from the client's buffer before it is read - a client refused for its
  # certificate would read "reset", not why.
  protected def fail(error : TlsError) : TlsError
  def self.group_name(group : Int32) : String
  def initialize(socket : IyiSocket, peer : String, place : String)
  # Records one write key carries before the next (RFC 8446 section 5.5:
  # AES-GCM's is 2^24.5 full records; ChaCha20-Poly1305's far more): past
  # it, the next write moves to new keys first - or, in TLS 1.2, which has
  # no KeyUpdate, is refused, and the connection with it. Settable, for a
  # test.
  def key_limit : UInt64
  # Records one write key carries before the next (RFC 8446 section 5.5:
  # AES-GCM's is 2^24.5 full records; ChaCha20-Poly1305's far more): past
  # it, the next write moves to new keys first - or, in TLS 1.2, which has
  # no KeyUpdate, is refused, and the connection with it. Settable, for a
  # test.
  def key_limit=(value : UInt64) : UInt64
  # Moves this side's writes to new keys (section 4.6.3), asking the peer
  # to move its own when *request*: what `write` does by itself at
  # `key_limit`, for a program that wants it sooner. TLS 1.2 has no
  # KeyUpdate: there it is a `TlsError`, and the connection stays open.
  def key_update(request : Bool = false) : TlsError | ::Nil
  # The chain the peer's certificate was checked through, leaf first: the
  # server's, for a client; the client's, for a server that asked for one.
  def peer_certificates : Array(Certificate)
  # Up to *max* bytes the peer sent: "" once it has closed with
  # close_notify. The socket's read timeout bounds the whole call.
  def read(max : Int32 = 16384) : String | TlsError
  # How long a read or a write of the connection under it may wait.
  def read_timeout_ms=(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Whether this is the server's end.
  abstract def server_side? : Bool
  # The version negotiated: "TLSv1.3", or "TLSv1.2" for a client whose
  # server chose it.
  def version : String
  # *block* under a deadline *ms* from now (none when 0), cleared after.
  protected def within(ms : Int32, &block : (-> T)) : T forall T
  # Sends *data*, in records of at most 2^14 bytes; answers its size.
  def write(data : String | Array(UInt8)) : Int32 | TlsError
  def write_timeout_ms=(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
end

# What a connection answers when it cannot be made or kept, or a read that
# came back with nothing yet.
pub struct TlsError
  # The alert this refusal sends the peer (`TlsAlert`), or nil: none for a
  # failure of the socket, or for an alert the peer sent.
  def alert : UInt8 | ::Nil
  def cancelled? : Bool
  # *message*, the alert's name after it when there is one: the sentence
  # shows the alert, and the alert is the field, not the sentence.
  def initialize(message : String, alert : UInt8 | ::Nil = nil, timed_out : Bool = false, cancelled : Bool = false)
  # A read that waited past its timeout, or that was cancelled: nothing was
  # lost and the connection is open - read again. Any other error ended it.
  def timed_out? : Bool
  def to_s : String
end

# A certificate chain, leaf first, and the key that signs for it -
# Ed25519, ECDSA on P-256 (std/p256) or RSA (std/rsa), each in constant
# time: what a server presents, and what a client presents when a server
# asks.
pub class TlsIdentity
  # The ClientCertificateType a TLS 1.2 CertificateRequest must list for
  # this key: rsa_sign (1), or ecdsa_sign (64) for P-256 and, by RFC 8422
  # section 5.5, Ed25519.
  def certificate_type : UInt8
  # The chain as sent, leaf first, each certificate's DER.
  def chain : Array(Array(UInt8))
  # *chain*'s certificates, leaf first, and the 32-byte Ed25519 *seed*
  # that is the leaf's private key.
  def self.from_der(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), seed : Array(UInt8)) : TlsIdentity | TlsError
  # *chain*'s certificates, leaf first, and the P-256 *key* that is the
  # leaf's.
  def self.from_der(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), key : P256PrivateKey) : TlsIdentity | TlsError
  # *chain*'s certificates, leaf first, and the RSA *key* that is the
  # leaf's (2048 bits or more, std/rsa's floor for signing).
  def self.from_der(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), key : RsaPrivateKey) : TlsIdentity | TlsError
  # The chain in *certificates*' CERTIFICATE blocks, leaf first, and the
  # leaf's private key in *private_key*: a PRIVATE KEY block (PKCS #8, an
  # Ed25519 key as RFC 8410 section 7 writes it, a P-256 one as RFC 5915
  # does, or an RSA one), an EC PRIVATE KEY block (SEC 1) or an RSA
  # PRIVATE KEY block (PKCS #1) - or why they are not a certificate and
  # key.
  def self.from_pem(certificates : String, private_key : String) : TlsIdentity | TlsError
  def initialize(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), leaf : Certificate, schemes : Array(Int32), seed : Array(UInt8) | ::Nil, p256 : P256PrivateKey | ::Nil, rsa : RsaPrivateKey | ::Nil)
  def leaf : Certificate
  # The scheme to sign under for a peer that takes *offered* (its
  # signature_algorithms, in its order): the first of them this key makes,
  # or nil when it makes none.
  def scheme_for(offered : Array(Int32)) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # A scheme by the name RFC 8446 gives it.
  def self.scheme_name(scheme : Int32) : String
  # Schemes by name, for a sentence: "a, b or c".
  def self.scheme_names(schemes : Array(Int32)) : String
  # The schemes CertificateVerify can be signed under, by the key's kind:
  # ed25519 (0x0807), ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 (0x0403), or for an RSA key
  # rsa_pss_rsae_sha256, -384 and -512 (0x0804 to 0x0806). PKCS #1 v1.5
  # is never one: RFC 8446 section 4.2.3 keeps it out of CertificateVerify.
  def schemes : Array(Int32)
  # The leaf key's signature of *content* under *scheme*, one of
  # `schemes`: what CertificateVerify carries.
  def sign(scheme : Int32, content : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
end

# The key schedule of one connection (RFC 8446 section 7.1), over the
# cipher suite's hash: SHA-384 for TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, SHA-256 for the
# other two.
pub class TlsKeySchedule
  # Derive-Secret over the messages so far.
  def derive_secret(secret : Array(UInt8), label : String, transcript : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  # The early secret with no PSK, and the "derived" salt for the next stage.
  def early_secret : Array(UInt8)
  # HKDF-Expand-Label: the label prefixed "tls13 ", and the context, in an
  # HkdfLabel.
  def expand_label(secret : Array(UInt8), label : String, context : Array(UInt8), length : Int32) : Array(UInt8)
  def extract(salt : Array(UInt8), ikm : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  # A Finished message's verify_data under *secret* (section 4.4.4).
  def finished(secret : Array(UInt8), transcript : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  def handshake_secret(shared : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  def hash(data : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  def hash_size : Int32
  def hmac(key : Array(UInt8), data : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  def initialize(sha384 : Bool)
  def master_secret(handshake_secret : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  # The next generation of a traffic secret (section 7.2).
  def next_secret(secret : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  # TLS 1.2's PRF (RFC 5246 section 5): P_hash over this schedule's hash -
  # SHA-256, or SHA-384 for a suite that names it - keyed by *secret*, over
  # *label* and *seed*, *length* bytes of it.
  def prf(secret : Array(UInt8), label : String, seed : Array(UInt8), length : Int32) : Array(UInt8)
  def zeros : Array(UInt8)
end

# One direction's record protection (section 5.2): the AEAD keyed from a
# traffic secret, and the record sequence number its nonces are made of -
# or TLS 1.2's, keyed from its key block.
pub class TlsRecordCipher
  # TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.
  def initialize(suite : Int32, schedule : TlsKeySchedule, secret : Array(UInt8))
  # TLS 1.2's (RFC 5246 section 6.2.3.3) for one of its AEAD suites, *key*
  # and *iv* from the key block: AES-GCM's four-byte salt, to which each
  # record's eight-byte explicit nonce is added (RFC 5288 section 3), or
  # ChaCha20-Poly1305's twelve bytes, XORed with the sequence number as TLS
  # 1.3 does it (RFC 7905 section 2).
  def initialize(suite : Int32, key : Array(UInt8), iv : Array(UInt8))
  def key_iv : Array(UInt8)
  # The type and content of a protected record whose 5-byte header is
  # *header* and body *body*.
  def open(header : Array(UInt8), body : Array(UInt8)) : ::Tuple(UInt8, Array(UInt8)) | TlsError
  # The whole record that carries *content* of *type*, protected.
  def seal(type : UInt8, content : Array(UInt8)) : Array(UInt8)
  def sequence : UInt64
end

# A connection from a client, its handshake done: TLS 1.3 as a server,
# its certificate's key (Ed25519 or P-256) signing for it.
pub class TlsServer < TlsConnection
  # The handshake, or why it failed - the client sent that alert first.
  def handshake : TlsError | ::Nil
  # The certificate and key this connection was shown under: the config's
  # `identity`, or one of its `others` the client asked for by name.
  def identity : TlsIdentity
  def initialize(socket : IyiSocket, config : TlsServerConfig)
  # The handshake with the client on *socket*. A handshake that fails
  # sends the client the alert its error names, and the socket is closed.
  def self.over(socket : IyiSocket, config : TlsServerConfig, timeout_ms : Int32 = HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS) : TlsServer | TlsError
  # The host the client named (server_name, RFC 6066), if it named one.
  def server_name : String | ::Nil
  def server_side? : Bool
end

# What a server presents and asks: its identity, the protocols it speaks
# by ALPN, and - for mutual TLS - the roots a client's certificate must
# chain to.
pub class TlsServerConfig
  # *identity* shown to a client asking for a host its certificate names.
  def add_identity(identity : TlsIdentity) : TlsServerConfig
  # Protocols this server speaks by ALPN (RFC 7301), most wanted first; a
  # client that offers some and none of these is refused. None when empty.
  def alpn : Array(String)
  # Protocols this server speaks by ALPN (RFC 7301), most wanted first; a
  # client that offers some and none of these is refused. None when empty.
  def alpn=(value : Array(String)) : Array(String)
  def chain : Array(Array(UInt8))
  def client_required : Bool
  def client_required=(value : Bool) : Bool
  # When set, the server asks for a client's certificate (a
  # CertificateRequest) and checks it as std/x509 checks a client's
  # (clientAuth) against these roots, then its CertificateVerify; a client
  # that sends none is refused (certificate_required) while
  # `client_required`. Not asked when nil.
  def client_roots : Array(Certificate) | ::Nil
  # When set, the server asks for a client's certificate (a
  # CertificateRequest) and checks it as std/x509 checks a client's
  # (clientAuth) against these roots, then its CertificateVerify; a client
  # that sends none is refused (certificate_required) while
  # `client_required`. Not asked when nil.
  def client_roots=(value : Array(Certificate) | ::Nil) : Array(Certificate) | ::Nil
  def self.from_der(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), seed : Array(UInt8)) : TlsServerConfig | TlsError
  def self.from_der(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), key : P256PrivateKey) : TlsServerConfig | TlsError
  def self.from_der(chain : Array(Array(UInt8)), key : RsaPrivateKey) : TlsServerConfig | TlsError
  # `TlsIdentity.from_pem`'s identity, as a server's.
  def self.from_pem(certificates : String, private_key : String) : TlsServerConfig | TlsError
  def identity : TlsIdentity
  # The identity a client asking for *name*, taking signatures under
  # *schemes*, is shown: the first of `others` that names the host and
  # signs under a scheme the client takes, else `identity` if it does; nil
  # when none of them does.
  def identity_for(name : String | ::Nil, schemes : Array(Int32)) : TlsIdentity | ::Nil
  def initialize(identity : TlsIdentity)
  def leaf : Certificate
  # The time a client's certificate is checked at; now when nil.
  def now : Time | ::Nil
  # The time a client's certificate is checked at; now when nil.
  def now=(value : Time | ::Nil) : Time | ::Nil
  # More identities, each shown to a client that asks by server_name (RFC
  # 6066) for a host its certificate names; `identity` to any other.
  def others : Array(TlsIdentity)
  def schemes : Array(Int32)
end

# The versions a client may speak: TLS 1.3, or TLS 1.2 as well (RFC 5246),
# for a server that never moved past it.
pub enum TlsVersion : Int32

modules.name: std/toml
modules.surface:
module std/toml

# `derive toml_serializable`, in a struct or class whose fields are written
# with their types: the type reads and writes itself as a TOML table, a
# key per field, named as the field is.
#
#     pub struct Coord
#       getter x : Float64
#       getter name : String
#       derive toml_serializable
#     end
#
#     Coord.from_toml("x = 1.5\nname = \"a\"\n").x   # => 1.5
#     coord.to_toml                                 # => "x = 1.5\nname = \"a\"\n"
#
# It is std/yaml's `derive yaml_serializable` over TOML, field for field:
# a value is read and written as `TOML.read_value` and `TOML.to_any` take
# its type (Bool, Int32, Int64, UInt8, UInt64, Float64, String,
# `TOMLDateTime`, `Any`, an `Array` or a `Hash(String, _)` of them,
# another derived type, each of them or nil). TOML has no null, so a nil
# field is not written, and a missing key is read as YAML's derive reads
# one: a field with a default keeps it, a nilable field holds nil, and any
# other is refused by name. A key the type has no field for is passed
# over. A type that is several writes `derive serializable,
# yaml_serializable, toml_serializable`: what this one generates shares no
# method with theirs (`to_toml`, `from_toml`, `to_toml_any` and
# `initialize(toml : Any)` of this module's `Any`).
pub macro toml_serializable(declaration)

# The value a document holds. A document is a table: `TOML.parse` answers
# an `Any` whose `raw` is a `Hash(String, Any)`.
pub struct Any
  alias Type = Bool | Int64 | Float64 | String | TOMLDateTime | Array(Any) | Hash(String, Any)
  def !=(other : Any) : Bool
  # Structural: same kind, same value; a table equals a table with the
  # same pairs in any order. `1` and `1.0` are different values, two NaNs
  # the same one, and `0.0` equals `-0.0` as the doubles do. Arrays and
  # tables are compared in methods of their own and scalars in a third,
  # so the frames a deep value recurses through stay small: with all of
  # it here, comparing two arrays nested 100 deep overflowed a task's
  # stack in a plain build.
  def ==(other : Any) : Bool
  def [](key : String) : Any
  def [](index : Int32) : Any
  def []?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def []?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def as_a : Array(Any)
  def as_a? : Array(Any) | ::Nil
  def as_bool : Bool
  def as_bool? : Bool | ::Nil
  def as_datetime : TOMLDateTime
  def as_datetime? : TOMLDateTime | ::Nil
  # A float, or an integer widened to one.
  def as_f : Float64
  def as_f? : Float64 | ::Nil
  def as_h : Hash(String, Any)
  def as_h? : Hash(String, Any) | ::Nil
  def as_i : Int64
  def as_i? : Int64 | ::Nil
  def as_s : String
  def as_s? : String | ::Nil
  def dig(key : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig(key : String | Int32, *rest : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig?(key : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(key : String | Int32, *rest : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  # Agrees with `==`: a table's hash does not depend on its order, `0.0`
  # and `-0.0` share one and so do all NaNs. Mixed as std/yaml's `Any`
  # mixes, for the spread that file measured.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(raw : Type)
  def initialize(value : Int32)
  # A value as TOML writes it inline: strings quoted and escaped, floats
  # as `dump` spells them, tables as inline tables.
  def inspect : String
  # Which member of the union `raw` is, as one of the KIND_ constants.
  # Reference types are tested first, for the reason std/yaml's header
  # gives.
  def kind : Int32
  # The name of the kind, for the sentences below.
  def kind_name : String
  def raw : Type
  # Items of an array, keys of a table, characters of a string.
  def size : Int32
  # A string as itself, anything else as `inspect` writes it.
  def to_s : String
end

pub struct TOML
  # TOML for a table, ending in a line break unless the table is empty.
  def self.dump(value : Any) : String
  # The document `text` holds, read into `type`: `Bool`, `Int32`, `Int64`,
  # `UInt8`, `UInt64`, `Float64`, `String`, `TOMLDateTime`, `Any`, a type
  # with `derive toml_serializable`, one of those or nil, or an `Array` or a
  # `Hash(String, _)` of those. Text that is not TOML panics with the
  # `TOMLError`'s sentence; a value of another kind, or an integer outside
  # the type, is refused.
  def self.from_toml(text : String, type : T.class) : T forall T
  def initialize
  # The document `text` holds, a table, or what is wrong with it.
  def self.parse(text : String) : Any | TOMLError
  # The document, or nil where `parse` answers a `TOMLError`.
  def self.parse?(text : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Bool.class) : Bool
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Int32.class) : Int32
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Int64.class) : Int64
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : UInt8.class) : UInt8
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : UInt64.class) : UInt64
  # A float, or an integer widened to one: `y = 2` is the Float64 2.0.
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Float64.class) : Float64
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : String.class) : String
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : TOMLDateTime.class) : TOMLDateTime
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Any.class) : Any
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Array(T).class) : Array(T) forall T
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : Hash(String, V).class) : Hash(String, V) forall V
  # A type that reads itself, the `initialize(toml)` a `derive
  # toml_serializable` wrote; a type that admits nil reads as the other
  # type, since a value that is there is never null.
  def self.read_value(value : Any, type : T.class) : T forall T
  # The `Any` a value is written as. TOML has no null: a nil is refused
  # here, named, and a derived type leaves a nil field out before it gets
  # this far. Taken out before the rest dispatches, for the reason
  # std/json's `write_or_null` gives.
  def self.to_any(val : T) : Any forall T
  # TOML for any table `to_any` makes of `obj`, as `dump` writes it.
  def self.to_toml(obj : T) : String forall T
  def self.write_value(val : Bool) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : Int32) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : Int64) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : UInt8) : Any
  # A TOML integer is an `Int64`: a `UInt64` past it cannot be written.
  def self.write_value(val : UInt64) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : Float64) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : String) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : TOMLDateTime) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : Any) : Any
  def self.write_value(val : Array(T)) : Any forall T
  # TOML keys are strings, so a hash is written when its keys are.
  def self.write_value(val : Hash(String, V)) : Any forall V
  def self.write_value(val : T) : Any forall T : ToTOML
end

# A TOML date, time or date-time, with its kind. An offset date-time has
# every field and `offset_minutes` (0 for `Z`); a local date-time every
# field but the offset; a local date the date fields alone, a local time
# the time fields alone, the others 0. Two values are equal when their kind
# and every field are: `07:32:00Z` and `08:32:00+01:00` are one instant
# written two ways, and this keeps which way (`unix_seconds` says they are
# the same instant).
pub struct TOMLDateTime
  def !=(other : TOMLDateTime) : Bool
  def ==(other : TOMLDateTime) : Bool
  def day : Int32
  def self.days_in_month(year : Int32, month : Int32) : Int32
  def hash : Int32
  def hour : Int32
  # Fields that do not make a value of the kind are the caller's mistake,
  # refused with what is wrong; `problem` says it without panicking.
  def initialize(kind : Int32, year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32, hour : Int32, minute : Int32, second : Int32, nanosecond : Int32, offset_minutes : Int32)
  def inspect : String
  def kind : Int32
  def kind_name : String
  def self.leap_year?(year : Int32) : Bool
  def self.local_date(year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32) : TOMLDateTime
  def local_date? : Bool
  def self.local_date_time(year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32, hour : Int32, minute : Int32, second : Int32, nanosecond : Int32 = 0) : TOMLDateTime
  def local_date_time? : Bool
  def self.local_time(hour : Int32, minute : Int32, second : Int32, nanosecond : Int32 = 0) : TOMLDateTime
  def local_time? : Bool
  def minute : Int32
  def month : Int32
  def nanosecond : Int32
  def offset? : Bool
  def self.offset_date_time(year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32, hour : Int32, minute : Int32, second : Int32, nanosecond : Int32 = 0, offset_minutes : Int32 = 0) : TOMLDateTime
  def offset_minutes : Int32
  # `value` in decimal with zeros in front to `width` digits.
  def self.pad(value : Int32, width : Int32) : String
  # Nil when the fields make a value of `kind`, else what is wrong with
  # them, as the reader and `new` both say it.
  def self.problem(kind : Int32, year : Int32, month : Int32, day : Int32, hour : Int32, minute : Int32, second : Int32, nanosecond : Int32, offset_minutes : Int32) : String | ::Nil
  def second : Int32
  # As TOML writes it (RFC 3339 for an offset date-time): `T` between
  # date and time, `Z` for a zero offset, the fraction with its trailing
  # zeros dropped and left out when it is zero.
  def to_s : String
  # Seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z of an offset date-time, the
  # fraction left in `nanosecond`. The other three kinds name no instant.
  def unix_seconds : Int64
  def year : Int32
end

# What is wrong with a document, and where: `line` and `column` count from
# 1, a column in characters. `message` is "<reason> at line L, column C".
pub struct TOMLError
  def column : Int32
  def initialize(reason : String, line : Int32, column : Int32)
  def line : Int32
  def reason : String
  def to_s : String
end

# What `TOML.write_value` and `TOML.to_any` take besides the built-in
# types: a value whose type implements it, as a `derive
# toml_serializable` type does.
pub trait ToTOML
  abstract def to_toml_any : Any
end

impl Error for TOMLError
  def message : String
end

module std/tuple

struct ::NamedTuple(T)
  # Compares the values by name.
  #
  # Any named tuple: the keys are sorted and compared, then the values in
  # that order as tuples compare (src/iyi/object.iyi), member by member
  # where one type holds the other. `self` took `{a: 1, b: 2}` for `{a: 1,
  # b: y}` (y : Int32?) and not back, so the pair answered true one way and
  # false the other, and `case` over them did not match.
  def ==(other : NamedTuple) : Bool
  # Yields each key symbol and corresponding value.
  def each : Nil
  # Yields each value in order.
  def each_value : Nil
  # Returns true when the named tuple contains zero entries.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Returns true if the named tuple contains the given key symbol.
  #
  # The keys here and below are written with `symbolize`, never as
  # `:{{key.id}}`: a quoted key such as `"content-type"` or `"x y"` pasted
  # that way is `:content-type`, a symbol minus a call, or `:x y`, which
  # does not parse, so every one of these methods failed to compile for
  # such a key. `std/named_tuple` already wrote them this way.
  def has_key?(key : Symbol) : Bool
  # Hashing follows the `==` below, mixed as `Tuple#hash` mixes the members
  # (src/iyi/object.iyi). `Object#hash` answered the type's id, so
  # `{a: 1}` and `{a: 2}` hashed alike and 20,000 keys took 1.4 s to insert
  # where the same pairs as tuples took 1 ms. The values go in by sorted
  # key, because `==` matches by name: `{x: 1, y: 2} == {y: 2, x: 1}`, so
  # the two have to hash alike although their types list the keys in
  # another order.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize
  def inspect : String
  # Returns a Tuple containing the key symbols in order. Built with
  # `Tuple.new`, as `Tuple#map` is: for the named tuple with no keys,
  # braces are an empty hash literal.
  def keys
  # Value identity.
  def same?(other : self) : Bool
  # Number of key-value pairs in the named tuple.
  def size : Int32
  # The keys, and the values, in sorted key order: the order a type lists
  # its keys in is not part of the value.
  protected def sorted_keys
  protected def sorted_values
  # String representation: `{name: "Alice", age: 30}`. A key that is not a
  # name is quoted, as it is written: `{"content-type": "text/plain"}`.
  def to_s : String
  # Returns a Tuple containing the values in order.
  def values
end

struct ::Tuple(*T)
  # Concatenates two tuples.
  def +(other : Tuple(*U)) forall U
  # Yields each element sequentially.
  def each : Nil
  # Yields each element alongside its index.
  def each_with_index : Nil
  # Returns true when the tuple contains zero elements.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Returns the first element. Raises if empty.
  def first
  # Returns the first element, or nil if empty.
  def first?
  # Returns the last element. Raises if empty.
  def last
  # Returns the last element, or nil if empty.
  def last?
  # Returns a new Tuple with each element mapped through the block.
  #
  # This, `+`, `reverse`, and `NamedTuple#keys` and `#values` build with
  # `Tuple.new(...)`, not braces: with no members `{ }` is an empty hash
  # literal, so on the empty tuple each failed to compile with "for empty
  # hashes use '{} of KeyType => ValueType'".
  def map
  # Creates a new Tuple containing the given arguments.
  def self.new(*args : *T)
  # Reverses elements in tuple.
  def reverse
  # Value identity.
  def same?(other : self) : Bool
  # Converts the tuple into an Array typed as the union of all element types.
  # The empty tuple's is `[] of NoReturn`, the union of no types: the
  # `typeof` below had no argument there, and `Tuple.new.to_a` did not
  # compile.
  def to_a
end

modules.surface:
module std/udp

pub alias Bytes = Std::Slice::Bytes

# An incoming datagram with payload bytes and remote peer origin.
pub struct Datagram
  def [](i : Int32) : Bytes | String | Int32
  def data : Bytes
  def host : String
  def initialize(data : Bytes, host : String, port : Int32)
  def port : Int32
  # Decodes payload bytes as a String.
  def text : String
  def to_s : String
  def to_tuple : Tuple(Bytes, String, Int32)
end

# The address types, their parsers and the `sockaddr_in`/`sockaddr_in6`
# writers are `std/socket`'s; this module had copies, and the copies had
# drifted: its IPv6 parser read no dotted tail and its printer compressed
# only `::` and `::1`.
pub alias IPv4Address = Std::Socket::IPv4Address

pub alias IPv6Address = Std::Socket::IPv6Address

pub class UdpSocket
  lib LibWs2_32
    struct PollFd
    end
    # Both are kept on the caller's frame rather than the heap: the kernel
    # reads and writes them after a post, while the fiber is parked, and a
    # heap chunk whose only reference is a local the posting call has
    # finished with is a chunk the collector can hand to somebody else
    # first.
    struct WSABuf
    end
  end
  alias SockLen = Int32
  def self.__is_eagain(res : Int64) : ::Bool
  # Never: Winsock has no EINTR. A call either answers, or answers
  # WSAEWOULDBLOCK, or is posted and completed.
  def self.__is_eintr(res : Int64) : ::Bool
  # A datagram that did not fit is an error here where it is a silent
  # truncation everywhere else: WSAEMSGSIZE (10040), with the buffer
  # already filled, which is why the caller answers its capacity.
  def self.__is_msgsize(res : Int64) : ::Bool
  # Never: the report is turned off in `__sys_socket`.
  def self.__is_refused(res : Int64) : ::Bool
  # WSAEINVAL (10022): Winsock's answer to a receive, or an address asked,
  # on a socket that has none yet - one `client` made and nothing sent
  # from. POSIX has nothing queued there and port 0; Windows panicked.
  def self.__is_unbound(res : Int64) : ::Bool
  def self.__sys_bind(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), len : Int32) : Int32
  # A datagram socket's `connect` only records the peer, so there is no
  # handshake to wait for and nothing to post.
  def self.__sys_connect(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), len : Int32) : Int32
  # Winsock's error number, negated, which is the shape the POSIX arms
  # answer the kernel's errno in; the two predicates at the bottom are the
  # only things that read which number it was.
  def self.__sys_error : Int64
  def self.__sys_get_buffer_size(fd : Int32, level : Int32, optname : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_getsockname(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32)) : Int32
  def self.__sys_handle(fd : Int32) : UInt64
  # The wait a cancelled post still owes the kernel. `CancelIoEx` is a
  # request, and on a socket tied to a completion port the operation is not
  # over when it returns: measured here, the status stays STATUS_PENDING
  # and the descriptor, the caller's address and the OVERLAPPED are the
  # kernel's until the completion packet is taken *off the port* — the
  # poller's `GetQueuedCompletionStatus` is what writes them. The same
  # measurement on an unassociated socket had the status written by
  # `CancelIoEx` itself, which is why this is not obvious. So
  # `WSAGetOverlappedResult`'s own wait flag cannot be the wait either: it
  # waits on the OVERLAPPED's event, the scheduler's OVERLAPPED has none,
  # and the socket handle it falls back to is never signalled for a socket
  # on a port — it hung forever on the first cancelled receive tried.
  #
  # What ends the operation is the poller, so the frame parks once more and
  # lets it. `IyiScheduler.cancel` has already unregistered this fiber,
  # which is what would have left the packet to be dropped; parking puts it
  # back, and the wake means the dequeue has happened. Asked first, because
  # a completion the poller delivered *before* the cancel is already over
  # and no second packet is coming — parking on one would never wake.
  def self.__sys_overlapped_await(s : UInt64, ov : Pointer(UInt8)) : Int64
  # What the posted operation ended with, read off the operation itself:
  # the completion port's byte count cannot tell a failure from a datagram
  # of no bytes, which is a legal datagram. Nothing waits here, which is
  # what the 0 says.
  def self.__sys_overlapped_result(s : UInt64, ov : Pointer(UInt8)) : Int64
  # One descriptor, one event, and a bound on the wait, which is what the
  # epoll and kqueue arms do with theirs.
  def self.__sys_poll_read(fd : Int32, timeout_ms : Int32) : ::Bool
  # Winsock's address length is an `int*` where POSIX has a `socklen_t*`:
  # the same width and the same bytes, so the callers keep one signature.
  def self.__sys_recvfrom(fd : Int32, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64, flags : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32)) : Int64
  # The receive that waits, which on Windows is a posted one: see the note

  def to_unsafe : Int32

  def self.unbound(family : Int32 = 2) : UdpSocket

module std/unicode

pub struct Unicode
  # Options the case mappings take; combine them with `|`.
  enum CaseOptions : Int32
    ASCII = 1
    Turkic = 2
    Fold = 4
  end
  # The normalization forms `normalize` writes.
  enum NormalizationForm : Int32
    NFD = 0
    NFC = 1
    NFKD = 2
    NFKC = 3
  end
  def self.ascii?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The first character in titlecase and the rest in lowercase: `"ǆemal"` is
  # `"ǅemal"`, `"STRASSE"` is `"Strasse"`. The first character is still a
  # letter before the rest, so `"ΑΣ"` is `"Ας"`.
  def self.capitalize(text : String, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : String
  # Every character whose simple case folding is this one's, itself among
  # them, in code point order: `k` answers `K`, `k` and the Kelvin sign
  # U+212A, `σ` answers `Σ`, `ς` and `σ`, and `ß` answers `ß` and `ẞ`. A
  # character without case answers itself alone. It is what a
  # case-insensitive comparison of one character has to accept, and folding
  # both sides is not enough to build it: a class holding the Kelvin sign
  # has to take `K` as well, and only the folding read backwards says so.
  #
  # The simple folding here is CaseFolding.txt's C and S rows, which is
  # RE2's. `foldcase` answers the other library's, which has no S rows:
  # there `ẞ` folds to itself.
  def self.case_orbit(char : Char) : Array(Char)
  # The string with every maximal ill-formed subpart replaced by U+FFFD; a
  # well-formed string is answered as it is.
  def self.clean(text : String) : String
  # The bytes as a string, every maximal ill-formed subpart replaced by U+FFFD.
  def self.clean(bytes : Array(UInt8)) : String
  # Category C: Cc, Cf, Cs and Co — controls, format characters,
  # surrogates and private use.
  def self.control?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The string the UTF-16 code units spell. An unpaired surrogate is refused
  # with its index: `unpaired surrogate 0xD800 at index 3`.
  def self.decode_utf16(units : Array(UInt16)) : String
  # The string the UTF-16 code units spell, or nil at an unpaired surrogate.
  def self.decode_utf16?(units : Array(UInt16)) : String | ::Nil
  # The lowercase of one character, the simple mapping: `İ` becomes `i`
  # under Turkic rules and stays `İ` otherwise, because its full mapping is
  # `i` plus a combining dot.
  def self.downcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : Char
  # The full lowercase mapping, one character at a time.
  def self.downcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The string in lowercase, full mappings, with the final sigma: a capital
  # sigma that ends a word — a cased letter before it, none after, the
  # case-ignorable characters (combining marks, format characters, modifier
  # letters and the apostrophes, periods and colons that can sit inside a
  # word) looked through — becomes `ς`, so `"ΟΔΥΣΣΕΥΣ"` is `"οδυσσευς"`.
  # With `CaseOptions::Fold` this is `foldcase`.
  def self.downcase(text : String, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : String
  # Every orbit `case_orbit` answers that holds more than one character,
  # each once, as code points in order and in no particular order between
  # them. A case-insensitive class folds itself against these, about 1,400
  # of them, rather than asking `case_orbit` of each of the hundred
  # thousand code points a class like `\p{L}` holds.
  def self.each_case_orbit(& : (Array(Int32) -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Each grapheme cluster, in order.
  def self.each_grapheme(text : String, &block : (String -> _)) : Nil
  # The string's UTF-16 code units: one per character up to U+FFFF, a
  # surrogate pair above.
  def self.encode_utf16(text : String) : Array(UInt16)
  # The case folding of one character where it is one code point (`Σ`, `σ`
  # and `ς` all fold to `σ`); a character whose folding is longer, like `ß`,
  # is answered unchanged — the block form and the string form fold it.
  def self.foldcase(char : Char) : Char
  # The full case folding, one character at a time: `ß` yields `s` twice.
  def self.foldcase(char : Char, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The string folded for comparison: `"Straße"` and `"STRASSE"` both fold
  # to `"strasse"`.
  def self.foldcase(text : String) : String
  # The two-letter general category of a character: `"Lu"` for `A`, `"Po"`
  # for `!`, `"Sm"` for `+`; `"Cn"` for a code point no character is
  # assigned to.
  def self.general_category(char : Char) : String
  # How many grapheme clusters the string has: what a reader counts.
  def self.grapheme_size(text : String) : Int32
  # The string's extended grapheme clusters, as UAX #29 divides them: what
  # a reader sees as one character - `e` and a combining acute, a flag's
  # two regional indicators, a family emoji joined by ZWJs, a Devanagari
  # conjunct - is one string. A piece of ill-formed UTF-8 is a cluster of
  # its own, as the U+FFFD that stands for it would be.
  def self.graphemes(text : String) : Array(String)
  def initialize
  # Category L: Lu, Ll, Lt, Lm and Lo.
  def self.letter?(char : Char) : Bool
  # Category Ll.
  def self.lowercase?(char : Char) : Bool
  # Category M: Mn, Mc and Me — the combining marks.
  def self.mark?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The string in the given normalization form, NFC when none is named.
  def self.normalize(text : String, form : NormalizationForm = NormalizationForm::NFC) : String
  # Whether the string is already in the given form.
  def self.normalized?(text : String, form : NormalizationForm = NormalizationForm::NFC) : Bool
  # Category N: Nd, Nl and No — digits in every script, letter numbers, and
  # the fractions and superscripts.
  def self.number?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The code points a property names, as sorted `{from, to}` pairs that
  # neither overlap nor touch: a general category (`"Lu"`), a major class
  # by its letter (`"L"` is Lu, Ll, Lt, Lm and Lo; `"C"` is Cc, Cf, Cs and
  # Co, unassigned code points being in no category), or a script
  # (`"Greek"`). Nil for a name that is none of those. A class is built
  # from the ranges once rather than asking per character, which is what a
  # regex's `\p{..}` needs: ranges it can negate and case-fold.
  def self.property_ranges(name : String) : Array(Int32) | ::Nil
  # The script a character is written in, as `Scripts.txt` names it:
  # `"Latin"`, `"Greek"`, `"Han"`, and `"Common"` for the digits and
  # punctuation every script shares; `"Unknown"` for a code point the file
  # does not list.
  def self.script(char : Char) : String
  # The titlecase of one character, the simple mapping: the uppercase, except
  # for the digraphs, where `ǆ` and `Ǆ` both become `ǅ`.
  def self.titlecase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : Char
  # The full titlecase mapping, one character at a time: `ß` yields `S`, `s`.
  def self.titlecase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Category Lt: the digraphs whose first half is capital, `ǅ` and `ᾈ`.
  def self.titlecase?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The uppercase of one character: the simple mapping, so `ß` stays `ß`
  # (its full mapping is two letters; the block form gives it).
  def self.upcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : Char
  # The full uppercase mapping, one character at a time: `ß` yields `S` twice,
  # `ŉ` yields `ʼ` and `N`.
  def self.upcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The string in uppercase, full mappings: `"straße"` is `"STRASSE"`.
  # An ASCII-only string is the prelude's `upcase`, unless the Turkic rule
  # is on, which is a question about `i` itself.
  def self.upcase(text : String, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : String
  # Category Lu.
  def self.uppercase?(char : Char) : Bool
  # Whether the string's bytes are well-formed UTF-8.
  def self.valid?(text : String) : Bool
  # Whether the bytes are well-formed UTF-8.
  def self.valid?(bytes : Array(UInt8)) : Bool
  # Category Z: Zs, Zl and Zp — the spaces and the line and paragraph
  # separators. Tab and newline are controls, not whitespace, here.
  def self.whitespace?(char : Char) : Bool
end

class ::String
  def each_grapheme(&block : (String -> _)) : Nil
  def grapheme_size : Int32
  def graphemes : Array(String)
end

module std/uri

# An ordered multi-value collection representing URI query parameters
# or application/x-www-form-urlencoded form data.
pub struct Params
  # Returns the first value for *key*, or raises if not found.
  def [](key : String) : String
  # Sets the value for *key*, replacing all previous occurrences.
  def []=(key : String, value : String) : Nil
  # Returns the first value for *key*, or nil if not found.
  def []?(key : String) : String | ::Nil
  # Appends a key-value pair, preserving duplicate keys.
  def add(key : String, value : String) : Nil
  # Deletes all entries for *key*, returning the removed values or nil.
  def delete(key : String) : Array(String) | ::Nil
  # Iterates through each key-value pair.
  def each(& : (String, String -> Nil)) : Nil
  def empty? : Bool
  # Returns all values associated with *key*.
  def fetch_all(key : String) : Array(String)
  def has_key?(key : String) : Bool
  def initialize(keys : Array(String), values : Array(String))
  def initialize
  # Parses a query string into Params, decoding each name and value the
  # way the WHATWG URL standard reads `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`:
  # `+` is a space, `%XX` is the byte, and a `%` that does not start two
  # hex digits is itself. Pairs are separated by `&` and also by `;`, as
  # the other library separates them, where the standard and Python
  # 3.12's `parse_qsl` split at `&` alone: `a=1;b=2` is two pairs here and
  # one there.
  # Never a panic - the query is whatever a client sent, and `?q=100%`
  # is what browsers send for "100%". `URI.decode` stays strict: it is
  # asked of text a program made.
  def self.parse(query : String) : Params
  def size : Int32
  # Encodes parameters to application/x-www-form-urlencoded string.
  def to_s : String
end

pub class URI
  # The userinfo is compared as written, as the path is: `u%3Btype%3Da` and
  # `u;type=a` are two URIs (RFC 3986 section 2.2).
  def ==(other : URI) : Bool
  def absolute? : Bool
  # *host* as DNS looks it up and an HTTP `Host` header carries it: a
  # registered name's escapes decoded, since RFC 3986 section 3.2.2 has
  # them stand for UTF-8, and the name carried by `IDNA.to_ascii`, so
  # `Bücher.example` and `b%C3%BCcher.example` are both
  # `xn--bcher-kva.example`. An IP literal in brackets and an empty host
  # (`file:///x`) are answered as they are. What `IDNA.to_ascii` refuses
  # is its `IdnaError`, and so is a malformed escape. `hostname` is not
  # this: it answers what the reference wrote.
  def self.ascii_host(host : String) : String | IdnaError
  # `userinfo@host:port`, the userinfo and the host written as stored.
  def authority : String | ::Nil
  def self.decode(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = false) : String
  # Decodes `%XX` escapes (and `+` to a space when *plus_to_space*).
  # `decode?` answers nil and `decode` panics for a `%` not followed by
  # two hex digits; a multi-byte UTF-8 character encoded byte by byte
  # comes back as the character.
  def self.decode?(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = false) : String | ::Nil
  # `+` a space and `%XX` a byte, any other `%` kept as it is: the form
  # reading `Params.parse` makes.
  protected def self.decode_form_lenient(str : String) : String
  def self.decode_www_form(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = true) : String
  def self.decode_www_form?(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = true) : String | ::Nil
  def self.default_port(scheme : String) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def dup : URI
  # Percent-encodes every byte that is neither unreserved nor reserved,
  # `%` among them: `"%20"` becomes `"%2520"`, and a space `"%20"` (or
  # `"+"` when *space_to_plus*, which then writes a `+` as `"%2B"`). Bytes
  # above ASCII are encoded one by one, so UTF-8 text round-trips through
  # `decode`.
  def self.encode(str : String, space_to_plus : Bool = false) : String
  # Encodes a path, keeping `/` between its segments.
  def self.encode_path(str : String) : String
  # Encodes one path segment: only unreserved bytes pass.
  def self.encode_path_segment(str : String) : String
  # Encodes a user or a password for the authority: unreserved bytes and
  # the sub-delims, which RFC 3986 section 3.2.1 lets userinfo hold, pass;
  # `:`, which separates the two, and `@`, which ends them, do not.
  def self.encode_userinfo(str : String) : String
  # Encodes a form field the application/x-www-form-urlencoded way: a
  # space is `+` unless *space_to_plus* is false, and only unreserved
  # bytes pass.
  def self.encode_www_form(str : String, space_to_plus : Bool = true) : String
  def fragment : String | ::Nil
  def fragment=(value : String | ::Nil) : String | ::Nil
  # Gen-delims: ":" / "/" / "?" / "#" / "[" / "]" / "@"
  def self.gen_delim?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  # Hashing follows `==` (below), the eight parts mixed as a tuple's members
  # are. Without it every URI hashed to its type, so `http://a/` and
  # `https://b:8/x?y#z` hashed alike and a table of 16,000 URI keys took
  # 11.3 s to fill where the same texts as strings took 4 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  def host : String | ::Nil
  # Stored as given: an IPv6 address is written with its brackets,
  # `"[::1]"`, the way it appears in a URI, and `hostname` takes them off.
  def host=(h : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  # The host without the brackets an IPv6 address carries.
  def hostname : String | ::Nil
  def initialize(scheme : String | ::Nil = nil, host : String | ::Nil = nil, port : Int32 | ::Nil = nil, path : String = "", query : String | ::Nil = nil, user : String | ::Nil = nil, password : String | ::Nil = nil, fragment : String | ::Nil = nil)
  def normalize : URI
  def normalize_in_place : URI
  # The host in lower case and its escapes' hex digits upper-case, the
  # two rules RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.1 gives: `downcase` alone wrote
  # `%C3%A9` as `%c3%a9`, the one spelling of the escape the section
  # normalizes away from.
  protected def self.normalized_host(host : String) : String
  def opaque? : Bool
  def self.parse(raw_url : String) : URI
  # Reads *raw_url* as a URI reference. `parse?` answers nil and `parse`
  # panics with the reason for: a space or control character anywhere
  # (`space at byte 11 in "http://exa mple.com"`), a `:` before the first
  # `/`, `?` or `#` whose prefix is not a scheme (`invalid scheme "ht!tp"
  # in ...`), a `[` in the host with no `]`, a host with a byte a host
  # cannot hold, and a port that is not decimal digits or is above 65535.
  # Percent escapes are not checked here; `decode` does that.
  def self.parse?(raw_url : String) : URI | ::Nil
  def password : String | ::Nil
  def password=(password : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  def path : String
  def path=(value : String) : String
  def port : Int32 | ::Nil
  def port=(value : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def query : String | ::Nil
  def query=(value : String | ::Nil) : String | ::Nil
  def query_params : Params
  def query_params=(params : Params) : Nil
  def relative? : Bool
  # Linear in the path: the input buffer of section 5.2.4 is a cursor into
  # *path*, and each step moves it past what it took. Each step sliced the
  # rest of the path into a new string, so removing the dot segments took
  # time in the square of the path's length: 132 KB of `/a/./b/../c` took
  # 12.8 s in a release build, where splitting it at its slashes took 3 ms.
  def self.remove_dot_segments(path : String) : String
  # The dot segments of a relative reference's path taken out as resolving
  # it against any base would take them: a `..` that climbs past the
  # reference's own segments stays, since only the base knows what it
  # climbs out of, and a path that ends in a dot segment names a
  # directory, so `a/..` is `./`.
  protected def self.remove_relative_dot_segments(path : String) : String
  def self.reserved?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  # Resolves *ref* against this URI as Base URI according to RFC 3986 section 5.2.
  def resolve(ref : URI | String) : URI
  def scheme : String | ::Nil
  def scheme=(value : String | ::Nil) : String | ::Nil
  # Sub-delims: "!" / "$" / "&" / "'" / "(" / ")" / "*" / "+" / "," / ";" / "="
  def self.sub_delim?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  def to_s : String
  # Unreserved characters: ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." / "_" / "~"
  def self.unreserved?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  def self.unwrap_ipv6(h : String) : String
  # The user and the password are kept as the reference wrote them, escapes
  # and all, and written back so: decoded by `parse` and re-encoded by
  # `authority`, `u%3Btype%3Da@h` came back `u;type=a@h`, which RFC 3986
  # section 2.2 counts a different URI, and `é` came back `%C3%A9`. The
  # getters decode; the setters and the constructor encode what they are
  # given with `encode_userinfo`.
  def user : String | ::Nil
  def user=(user : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  def userinfo : String | ::Nil
  def userinfo=(info : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  # The user and the password as written, taken as they are.
  protected def written_userinfo(user : String | ::Nil, password : String | ::Nil) : Nil
end

# A group: its name, its id, and the accounts listed as its members. A
# user whose *primary* group this is need not be listed, and usually is
# not: `User#group_ids` is the question that counts both.
pub struct Group
  # The group whose id is *id*, or nil when there is none or *id* is not a
  # group id; compared as a number, as `User.find_by_id` compares.
  def self.find_by_id(id : String) : Group | ::Nil
  # The group called *name*, or nil when there is none.
  def self.find_by_name(name : String) : Group | ::Nil
  # The group id: a decimal number on Linux and darwin.
  def id : String
  def initialize(name : String, id : String, members : Array(String))
  # The names listed in the group, in the order they are listed.
  def members : Array(String)
  # The group's name: `"wheel"`.
  def name : String
  # Every group in *text*, written as `/etc/group` is
  # (`name:password:gid:member,member`), in order, without the lines a

modules.name: std/uuid
modules.surface:
module std/uuid

pub struct UUID
  def ==(other : UUID) : Bool
  def bytes : Array(UInt8)
  # Hashing follows `==`: the sixteen bytes, as an array of them hashes.
  # Without it every UUID hashed to its type, so the all-zero and the all-f
  # UUIDs hashed alike and a table of 16,000 UUID keys took 2.0 s to fill
  # where the same UUIDs as strings took 5 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  # The sixteen bytes are the UUID's own, copied in here and out of
  # `bytes`, as the other library's are a value: held as the caller's
  # array, a buffer reused for the next record changed every UUID made
  # from it (`b[0] = 255_u8` after `UUID.new(b)` turned `00000000-...`
  # into `ff000000-...`), and `u.bytes[1] = 255_u8` changed a UUID that
  # was already a hash key, which its table then could not find.
  def initialize(bytes : Array(UInt8))
  def self.parse(text : String) : UUID
  protected def stored : Array(UInt8)
  def to_s : String
  # Sixteen bytes from the operating system, six bits of them then set to
  # say version 4 and the RFC variant. Drawn from `Random.new`, they were
  # sixteen outputs of a fresh PCG generator: every UUID was a function of
  # the generator's 127 bits of state, and PCG makes no promise that its
  # outputs do not give that state away, where a version 4 UUID promises
  # 122 bits nobody can predict.
  def self.v4 : UUID
  # RFC 9562 version 7: 48 bits of Unix milliseconds, big-endian, then the
  # version, 12 bits of `rand_a`, the variant and 62 random bits.
  #
  # Two UUIDs from one millisecond would sort at random by their random
  # bits, so `rand_a` is a counter here (the RFC's "fixed bit-length
  # dedicated counter", section 6.2 method 1): a new millisecond starts it
  # at a random 11 bits, leaving at least 2,048 steps before it runs out,
  # and every UUID in the same millisecond, or one the clock stepped back
  # into, counts one up from the last. Past 4,095 the stamp moves on a
  # millisecond early, as the RFC allows. Each UUID this process makes
  # therefore sorts after the one before it, as bytes and as text; the
  # 62 bits after the counter are random every time, so two processes in
  # one millisecond still do not collide.
  def self.v7 : UUID
  def version : Int32
end
